26718.explanation: The Krebs cycle, or the citric acid cycle, is of central importance in all living cells, especially those that use oxygen as a part of cellular respiration. The cycle occurs in the matrix of the mitochondria.

26721.explanation: Hiccups are caused when the diaphragm contracts involuntarily. Hiccups can be best describe as jerky, incomplete inhalation of air. Most of the time hiccups do not need any medicines. They disappear on their own within a short time span. plate inhalation of air. In this, there is a spasmodic contraction of the diaphragm.

30915.explanation: During prolonged fasting, the primary source of energy i.e. carbohydrates is used by the body followed by fats and then proteins.

32367.explanation: The nerve in our body transmits message as electrical impulses through nerve cells. Human electricity in the brain and nervous system creates human magnetic fields.

53302.explanation: Aestivation is the arrangement of accessory floral organs in relation to one another in the bud condition. Aestivation may be open, valvate, twisted, and imbricate.

54279.explanation: Monera and Protista contain only micro-organisms. Monera contains unicellular prokaryotic organisms like bacteria. Protista contains unicellular eukaryotic organisms.

54775.explanation:
Methemoglobin cannot bind oxygen, unlike oxyhemoglobin. It is a bluish chocolate brown in color.

In human blood, a trace amount of methemoglobin is normally produced spontaneously, but when present in excess the blood becomes abnormally dark bluish brown.

The NADH-dependent enzyme methemoglobin reductase (MHbreductase enzyme) is responsible for converting methemoglobin back to hemoglobin. MHb is inactive forms that are converted into Hb that carries oxygen in the blood.

54900.explanation: Methemoglobinemia is a disorder characterized by the presence of a higher than normal level of methemoglobin in the blood. In the case of hereditary methemoglobinemia symptoms of cyanosis appear from birth.

54904.explanation:
Cadmium shows the danger of cumulative effects in the environment due to its acute and chronic toxicity.

Chemically cadmium is very similar to zinc, and the two metals can replace each other in many geochemical and biochemical processes. Both metals are found in (+2) oxidation state in water. This means that cadmium can replace zinc in some enzymes of our body, thereby altering the stereo-structure of the enzyme and impairing its catalytic activity. The acute cadmium poisoning in humans expresses as high blood pressure, kidney damage, destruction of testicular tissue, and red blood cells.

54988.explanation: Five kingdom classification was proposed by R.H. Whittaker in 1969. The kingdoms identified by him were Monera, Protista,Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.

54989.explanation: Kingdom Protista, kingdom Fungi, kingdom Plantae possess the nuclear membrane while the kingdom Monera does not possess a nuclear membrane.

54990.explanation: In Whittaker’s five kingdoms of classification, kingdom Protista, kingdom fungi, kingdom Plantae and kingdom Animalia are eukaryotic organisms. The kingdom monera includes prokaryotic organisms. Hence, four kingdoms out of five are eukayotes.

54991.explanation: The fifth kingdom, Monera, contains all the single-celled organisms that do not possess a true nucleus. Members of the kingdom Monera are commonly referred to as bacteria.

54992.explanation: Kingdom Protista has brought together Chlamydomonas, Chlorella which were earlier placed in Algae within Plants and (both having cell walls) with Paramoecium and Amoeba which was earlier placed in the animal kingdom which lacks it.

54993.explanation: The Kingdom Plantae includes all types of eukaryotic, multicellular, photosynthetic plants found in this biosphere. Most of the organism in this kingdom are autotrophs, which synthesis their own food with the help of solar energy.

54994.explanation: Aristotle was the earliest to attempt a more scientific basis for classification. He used simple morphological characters to classify plants into trees, shrubs, and herbs.

54995.explanation: Aristotle used simple morphological characters to classify plants into trees, shrubs, and herbs. He also divided animals into two groups, those which had red blood and those that did not.

54996.explanation: In Linnaeus' time, a two Kingdom system of classification with Plantae and Animalia kingdoms was developed that included all plants and animals respectively. This system was used until very recently.

54997.explanation: As spirogyra, chlorella and chlamydomonas have same characterstics which are perfectly suitable for the 'algae', they all are placed together in algae.

54998.explanation: Carl Linnaeus, also known as Carl von Linné or Carolus Linnaeus, is often called the Father of Taxonomy. His system for naming, ranking, and classifying organisms is still in wide use today with many changes.

54999.explanation: Artificial classification is based on a few morphological characters of organisms like flower shape, the stem type and types of seeds.

55000.explanation: The first phylogenetic system of classification was given by Engler and Prantl which was based on the evolutionary relationship of the organisms. Those evolved earlier are classified first and newly evolved later on.

55001.explanation: Chemotaxonomy as the method of biological classification based on similarities in the structure of certain compounds among the organisms being classified. Two organisms morphologically similar to each other are classified on the basis of chemotaxonomy.

55002.explanation: Prokaryotic organisms generally do not reproduce by sexual reproduction. However, they reproduce by asexual methods in favorable conditions.

55015.explanation: The cell wall of fungi is made up of chitin while the green plants had a cellulosic cell wall. Due to this, fungi were placed in a separate kingdom – Kingdom Fungi.

55016.explanation: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission. Sometimes, under unfavourable conditions, they produce spores. They also reproduce by a sort of sexual reproduction by adopting a primitive type of DNA transfer from one bacterium to the other.

55017.explanation: Mycelium is the vegetative part of a fungus or fungus-like bacterial colony, consisting of a mass of branching, thread-like hyphae.

55018.explanation: All prokaryotic, unicellular organisms are included in the kingdom Monera. The Eukaryotic unicellular organisms are placed in the Protista kingdom.

55019.explanation: The cell wall of fungi consists of special sugar molecules called chitin. The cell wall of plants is made up of cellulose.

55020.explanation: Euglena is photosynthetic in presence of sunlight and is saprophytic in absence of sunlight.

55021.explanation: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria oxidize various inorganic substances such as nitrates, nitrites, and ammonia and use the released energy for their ATP production. They play a great role in recycling nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorous, iron, and sulphur.

55022.explanation: In fungi, the asexual reproduction takes place by spores called conidia or sporangiospores or zoospores, and sexual reproduction is by oospores, ascospores and basidiospores.

55023.explanation: Algae grouped together the unicellular organisms and the multicellular ones.

55024.explanation: The three-domain system includes Archaebacteria, Eubacteria, and Bacteria domain.

55025.explanation: Methanogens are present in the guts of several ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes and they are responsible for the production of methane (biogas) from the dung of these animals.

55026.explanation: Blue-green algae are also called cyanobacteria. They are considered as the most primitive organism that still survives. It includes different forms of unicellular and multicellular organisms.

55027.explanation:
Mycoplasma is a genus of bacteria that lack a cell wall around their cell membrane. Without a cell wall, they are unaffected by many common antibiotics such as penicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics that target cell wall synthesis.

Mycoplasma species are the smallest bacterial cells yet discovered, can survive without oxygen, and come in various shapes. For example, M. genitalium is flask-shaped.

55028.explanation: Phycomycetes is a subdivision of fungus which are multicellular. Protozoa, slime moulds and euglenoids are part of the kingdom Protista which are unicellular and eukaryotic organisms.

55029.explanation: Commonly known forms of basidiomycetes are mushrooms, bracket fungi, or puffballs.

55030.explanation: The walls of the diatoms are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible.

55031.explanation: In fungi like ascomycetes and basidiomycetes, an intervening dikaryotic stage (n + n i.e. two nuclei per cell) occurs; such a condition is called a dikaryon and the phase is called dikaryon phase of fungus.

55032.explanation: The body of the filamentous fungus is known as mycelium, which is a thread-like structure. Mycelium produces hyphae and sporogenous cells to produce spores.

55034.explanation: Fungi is important in the nutrient cycle and acts as decomposer along with bacteria and mineralizers of the biosphere to regular recycling of nutrients in the biosphere.

55035.explanation: Different fungi contain different kinds of reserve food materials depending upon the habitat and body structure of the fungus. In some fungi, the food reserves are glycogen and fat.

55036.explanation: The mushroom belongs to class Basidiomycetes to kingdom fungi. Basidiomycetes produce basidiospores as reproductive units. The member of this group grows on dead and decaying matters.

55037.explanation: Bacteria belong to the kingdom Monera in which organisms are unicellular and prokaryotic. Prokaryotic organisms lack membrane-bounded organelles like mitochondria where respiration occurs. In bacteria, respiration occurs in the mesosome.

55038.explanation: A bacterium capable of tolerating extreme heat, dryness, and toxic chemicals have the ability to produce endospores inside the body that help them to tide over unfavorable conditions.

55039.explanation: When freshwater protozoan is placed in marine water, the contractile vacuole disappears because the function of the vacuole is to expel out excess water but in the case of marine water, the water should be retained instead of getting expelled. If the contractile vacuole will not disappear the cell will get dehydrated.

55040.explanation: The plant cells have a eukaryotic structure with prominent chloroplasts and cell walls mainly made of cellulose.

55041.explanation: The fluctuation between these diploid and haploid stages that occurs in plants is called the alternation of generations. The multicellular haploid plant structure is called the gametophyte, which is formed from the spore and gives rise to the haploid gametes.

55042.explanation: The sexual reproduction in the kingdom Animalia is by the population of males and female followed by embryological development.

55043.explanation: Drosera plant is partially heterotrophic. These plants capture insects to fulfil its protein requirement although it performs photosynthesis also.

55044.explanation: Beijerinck is considered one of the founders of virology. In 1898, he published results on the filtration experiments demonstrating that tobacco mosaic disease is caused by an infectious agent smaller than a bacterium and called the fluid as Contagiumvivum fluidum (infectious living fluid).

55045.explanation: A capsid is the protein shell of a virus. It consists of several oligomeric structural subunits made of a protein called protomers. The capsid encloses the genetic material of the virus.

55046.explanation: Most viruses have either RNA or DNA as their genetic material. The nucleic acid may be single- or double-stranded. The entire infectious virus particle, called a virion, consists of the nucleic acid and an outer shell of protein.

55047.explanation: T.O. Diener discovered a new infectious agent that was smaller than viruses and caused potato spindle tuber disease. It was found to be a free RNA. It lacked the protein coat that is found in viruses, hence the name viroid.

55048.explanation: A lichen is a composite organism that arises from algae or cyanobacteria living among filaments of multiple fungi in a symbiotic relationship. The combined lichen has properties different from those of its component organisms.

55049.explanation: A bacteriophage is a virus that infects and replicates within a bacterium.

55050.explanation: Viroids are smaller than viruses and caused potato spindle tuber disease. It was found to be a free RNA; it lacked the protein coat that is found in viruses, hence the name viroid. The RNA of the viroid was of low molecular weight.

55051.explanation: The name virus was first given by Beijerinck, in 1898.

55053.explanation: The virus in which genetic material is RNA is called a retrovirus. In this virus reverse transcription takes place to form DNA that synthesis proteins.

55054.explanation: Three kingdoms or domain system of classification does not include the viral domain. The virus was discovered after the invention of the electron microscope so, they were not part of the living world.

55055.explanation: A virus consists of genetic material (DNA or RNA) surrounded by protein capsules. They are of different shapes and sizes. The poliomyelitis virus is cubical in shape.

55056.explanation: Mycoplasmas are a group of organisms that lack a cell wall and are the smallest living organisms. They can survive without oxygen. Mycoplasmas are also called as PPLO (pleuro pneumonia-like organism).

55058.explanation: Euglena is a photosynthetic as well as a saprophytic organism. It contains chlorophyll for photosynthesis and can absorb food from dead and decaying materials.

55059.explanation: Mycophages are not a group of bacteria. They are a group of organisms that use algae as food. The animal virus is called Zoophagineae, plant virus phytophagineae, and the bacterial virus is called bacteriophages.

55060.explanation: Haemoglobin in RBCs imparts red colour to it. The organisms whose blood contains haemoglobin are called enaima and those without it are called anaima.

55061.explanation: Plasmogamy is the fusion of protoplasm of two cells which may be motile or non- motile. Plasmogamy occurs during sexual reproduction to form a diploid organism.

55062.explanation: Downy mildew disease is caused due to fungus that forms cottony growth on the surface of the host. The leaves' surface gets reduced that alters the photosynthesis rate.

55063.explanation: In Phaeophyceae, food is stored as complex carbohydrates which may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol.

55064.explanation: Kelps are marine algae of class Phaeophyceae or brown algae. The body of kelp may reach up to 100 meters long. They vary in colour from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon xanthophyll pigments, fucoxanthin present in them.

55065.explanation: The shape of a chloroplast varies from species to species. It may be cup-shaped (e.g., Chlamydomonas), (e.g., Vaucheria), Girdle (e.g., Ulothrix), Stellate or Star-shaped (e.g., Zygnema), Reticulate or net-like (e.g., Cladophora, Oedogonium), Spiral or ribbon or scalariform (e.g., Spirogyra), ovoid or disc or spheroid in higher plants.

55066.explanation: The common forms of Brown algae or Phaeophyceae are Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus.

55067.explanation: The plant body of Phaeophyceae is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast whereas the angiosperms attach to the substratum with the help of roots.

55068.explanation: Being photosynthetic, algae increase the level of dissolved oxygen in their immediate environment.

55069.explanation: In Ulothrix/Spirogyra reduction division (meiosis) occurs at the time of zygospore germination. The plant body of Ulothrix and Spirogyra is gametophytic (haploid), they produce zoogametes (n) which fuses to form zygospores (2n) diploid, which is a resting spore. The onset of favourable condition zygospore undergoes reductional division, or meiosis to produce zoo- meiospores.

55070.explanation: Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose.

55071.explanation: The class Chlorophyceae (Green Algae) contains chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, carotenoids, and xanthophylls as their primary pigments. These pigments give them a distinct green color and help in photosynthesis.

55072.explanation: The fusion between one large, non-motile female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed as oogamous e.g., Volvox, Fucus.

55073.explanation: The algal class Rhodophyta are commonly called red algae because it contains a red pigment, r-phycoerythrin along with chlorophyll a and d.

55074.explanation: Agar, one of the commercial products obtained from Gelidium are used to grow microbes and in preparations of ice-creams and jellies.

55075.explanation: Acetabularia is a genus of green algae, especially of the Polyphyaceae family. It is the largest unicellular organism.

55076.explanation: The green patchy structure that develops around the surface of stagnant water bodies having thread-like mass is called pond scum. They are actually a species of green algae, Spirogyra.

55077.explanation: Spirogyra is an alga that has a long thread-like structure having a ribbon-shaped chloroplast. Spirogyra is found in stagnant water forming a green layer around the surface called pond scum.

55091.explanation: Sphagnum is also known as peat moss as it provides peat that has long been used as fuel.

55092.explanation: Pteridophytes and Gymnosperms belong to a different division of plant kingdom but both of them possess Archegonia as female sex organ which produces female gamete for sexual reproduction.

55093.explanation: The gymnosperms (Gymnos: naked, Sperma: seeds) are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization. The seeds that develop post-fertilization, are not covered, i.e., are naked. Since Cycas has naked seeds, it belongs to gymnosperms.

55094.explanation: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores are known as heterosporous.

55096.explanation: One of the gymnosperms, Giant sequoias are the world's largest single tree with an average height of 50 - 85 m (164 - 279 ft) and 6 - 8 m (20 - 26 ft) in diameter.

55097.explanation: Equisetum of Pteridophyta belongs to class Sphenopsida.

55099.explanation: Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, in gymnosperms (Cedrus) the male and the female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence.

55100.explanation: Fern spores germinate to give rise to inconspicuous, small but multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophytes called prothallus. The gametophytes bear male and female sex organs called antheridia and archegonia.

55101.explanation: The cones bearing megasporophylls with ovules or megasporangia are called macrosporangiate or female strobili.

55102.explanation: In gymnosperms, male and female cones are formed that produce male and female gametes. The strobilus bearing microsporophylls and microsporangia are called microsporangia or male strobilus. The cones bearing megasporophylls with ovules or megasporangia are called microsporangia or female strobilus. So, the cone of gymnosperms represents the reproductive organs.

55103.explanation: The main plant body of the bryophyte is haploid. It produces gametes, hence is called a gametophyte.

55104.explanation: Roots in some genera of gymnosperms have a fungal association in the form of mycorrhizal (Pinus).

55105.explanation: The sporophytes bear sporangia that are subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls.

55107.explanation: In sexual reproduction, the sex organs antheridia and archegonia are produced at the apex of the leafy shoots.

55108.explanation: The bryophytes are divided into liverworts and mosses so they are closely related to each other.

55109.explanation:
The sporophyte of moss is differentiated into three parts - foot, seta, and capsule. The capsule, in turn, is differentiated into 3 regions.



 Apophysis - the sterile basal portion of the capsule, it is in continuity with seta
 Theca or body of capsule, which is the fertile region, and
 Operculum the apical region of capsule.


Apophysis is rich in chloroplast and thus the photosynthetic region of moss, it also provides nutrition to the developing sporangium.

55110.explanation: The spore of moss germinates to produce protonema. It is a creeping, green, branched, and frequently filamentous stage, which develops into secondary protonema as a lateral bud. This stage bears sex organs.

55112.explanation: Ginkgo is a living fossil. This plant belongs to the gymnosperms division. It is considered as one of the oldest plants known and still surviving in some parts of the world.

55113.explanation: Bryophytes are called amphibians of the plant kingdom as they can grow in both land and water. Water is essential for the completion of the life cycle as they release antherozoids into the water where they come in contact with archegonium to produce a zygote.

55114.explanation: The yellow or brown spots which have sporangia in fern are called sori. Spores are produced inside these sporangia to produce haploid gametophyte.

55115.explanation: In Gymnosperms, cross-pollination is mainly accompanied by wind. The pollen grains are produced in large quantities and generally lighter.

55119.explanation: Pinus belongs to division gymnosperms. In gymnosperms, seeds are formed but not inside the fruit. They are also called as plants with naked seeds.

55122.explanation: Cycas produces top-shaped multinucleate male gametes and mature seeds with one embryo having two cotyledons. Although, male and female gametes are generally uninucleate in gymnosperms.

55126.explanation: A dominant, independent, photosynthetic, thalloid, or erect phase of Bryophytes and pteridophytes is represented by a haploid gametophyte.

55127.explanation: In bryophytes, the dominant phase in the life cycle is the gametophytic plant body. However, in pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves.

55129.explanation: Megasporangium of seed plants is called an ovule. The ovule is present inside the ovary which becomes seed on maturation after fertilization. It produces megasporocytes or Megaspore mother cells that yield megaspores.

55130.explanation: Angiosperms plants have roots to hold the soil and remain erect. Similarly, Rhodophytes have holdfast by which they remain attached with substratum to absorb water and minerals.

55133.explanation: Epiphytes are dependent on other large plants for space or physical support. It remains to attach with other plants but does not obtain food or another nutrient from it so they are not parasitic on the supporting plants.

55134.explanation: Gametophytes and capsule are diploid structure and alternate with a haploid structure called spores by reduction division.

55135.explanation: The cryptogams are flowerless and seedless plants. They are simple plants like algae, mosses, and ferns which do not produce flowers, fruits, and seeds. Cryptogams are considered as lower plants.

55137.explanation: Oogamy is a form of anisogamy (heterogamy) in which the female gamete (e.g. egg cell) is significantly larger than the male gamete and is non-motile.

55138.explanation: Those animals in which the developing embryo has a three germinal layer, mesoderm in between the ectoderm and endoderm, are called triploblastic animals, and the absence of an internal body cavity is called coelomic.

55139.explanation: Animals possessing coelom are called coelomates such as annelids, molluscs, arthropods, echinoderms, hemichordates and chordates. In Platyhelmites coelom is absent.

55140.explanation: In coelenterates, the arrangement of cells is more complex. Here, the cells performing the same function are arranged into tissues, hence is called tissue level of organization.

55142.explanation: Arthropoda is the largest phylum of kingdom Animalia. It includes all insects, arachnids, myriapods, and crustaceans. They are characterized by jointed limbs and cuticles.

55143.explanation: The eggs of reptiles and birds are polyecithal because they contain a large amount of yolk inside the egg.

55144.explanation: The animals of class Mammalia have seven cervical vertebrae and a four-chambered heart. Mammalian is characterized by the presence of mammary glands to feed their young ones.

55145.explanation: The alimentary canal is absent in Taenia Solium. Taenia Solium is an obligate parasite and obtains digested food from the small intestine of the human being as well as pigs. Pick the animals with true placenta.

55146.explanation: The true placenta is present in Mongoose. Placenta help in the transfer of nutrients and respiratory gases from the mother to the growing foetus.

55147.explanation: The air bladder is present in Actinopterygii. It is also known as ray-finned fish due to the presence of fin rays.

55148.explanation: Book lung is a type of respiratory organ used for atmospheric gas exchange that is found in Arachnida such as scorpions and spiders.

55149.explanation: Amphioxus or lancelets are fish-like marine chordates found in shallow temperate and tropical seas. They have notochord throughout their life.

55150.explanation: Necton is an aquatic organism that can actively swim at will against the water current. Benthos and planktons float with the water current and not against the water current.

55151.explanation: Haemocoel is the main body cavity of invertebrates such as insects. It is also found in Pila which do not contain the blood circulating system.

55152.explanation: Most of the animals belonging to class Mammalia are viviparous, produces young ones. But, Duck-billed platypus belongs to mammalian class but lay eggs.

55170.explanation:
The animals of Phylum - Echinodermata have an endoskeleton of calcareous ossicles and, hence, the name Echinodermata. All are marine with the organ-system level of organization. The adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

They are triploblastic and coelomate animals. The digestive system is complete with a mouth on the lower (ventral) side and anus on the upper (dorsal) side.

55171.explanation: The organism beloging to class Cyclostomes have a sucking and circular mouth without jaws.They are primitive vertebrates. The cyclostomes are marine or fresh-water vertebrates.

55172.explanation: Platypus is the oviparous that lays eggs.

55173.explanation: The body of phylum Ctenophora bears eight external rows of ciliated comb plates, which help in locomotion.

55174.explanation: Torpedo fish has electric organ. They are known for being capable of producing an electric discharge ranging from 8 to 220 volts depending on species.

55175.explanation: Most of the animals are not able to fertilize their own egg by sperms but in liver fluke, self-fertilization takes place. Earthworm also possesses both male and female reproductive organs in the same individual but not able to fertilize its own egg.

55176.explanation: The endoskeleton is fully ossified (bony) and the long bones are hollow with air cavities (pneumatic) in class aves.

55177.explanation: Mammalia is found in a variety of habitats - polar ice caps, deserts, mountains, forests, grasslands, and dark caves. Some of them have adapted to fly or live in water. The most unique mammalian characteristic is the presence of milk-producing glands (mammary glands) by which the young ones are nourished. They have two pairs of limbs, adapted for walking, running, climbing, burrowing, swimming, or flying.

55178.explanation: Earthworms and leeches are monoecious, contain both male and female reproductive organs in the same individual.

55180.explanation: Phylum Platyhelminthes does not possess a coelom. The coelom is the body cavity in between organs. Animals with coelom are called coelomate and those without it are called acoelomate.

55182.explanation: Lancelets are classified in the phylum Chordata, subphylum Cephalochordata. lancelet, the name for small, fishlike lower chordate also called amphioxus it shows many affinities with the vertebrates. There are about 30 lancelet species, most belonging to the genus Branchiostoma (formerly Amphioxus). Lancelets are usually about 1 in. (2.5 cm) long, with transparent bodies tapered at both ends. There is no distinct head and no paired fins.

55183.explanation: The insects belong to phylum Arthropoda and hence, the excretory organ is Malphighian tubules.

55184.explanation: Locust (Locusta) is a gregarious pest belonging to phylum Arthropoda.

55186.explanation: Saccoglossus belong to phylum Hemichordata and hence the excretory organ is proboscis gland.

55187.explanation: Reptiles generally possess three-chamber heart, two upper chamber and single lower chamber. But in crocodile, the heart is four-chambered having two atrium and two ventricles.

55188.explanation: The mouth of molluscs contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called a radula.

55189.explanation: Air bladder is present in body fish that help them in maintaining balance and to swim up and down. Air bladder arises from the dorsal wall of the oesophagus.

55190.explanation: Phylum Mollusca is the second largest phylum after Arthropoda.

55191.explanation: Examples of poisonous snakes are Naja(Cobra), Bangarus(Krait), Vipera(Viper). Testudo is a non-poisonous snake. It is found in Europe.

55192.explanation: Asterias does not have an excretory system. Asterias includes starfish or sea star. They are exclusively marine.

55195.explanation: The ancestor of mammals belongs to class Therapsida. Therapsida is a group of synapsids that includes mammals and their ancestors.

55196.explanation: Bat is a member of order Chiroptera of class Mammalia. Bats are only mammals to have achieved powered to flight in which forelimb is modified as wings.

55197.explanation: Insects have the highest number of species in nature. Insect belongs to arthropods family of class Mammalia. They are characterized by jointed legs.

55198.explanation: Sycon does not perform locomotion, although it is an animal. Sycon remains attached to the substratum and does not move from one place to another.

55199.explanation: The larvae of urochordates are called tadpole. Tadpole change into adults by the process of metamorphosis. The structure of tadpole is totally different from the adult ones.

55200.explanation: The silk produced by Antheraeamylitta is called Tasar silk. This silk is considered as the most durable and best quality silk.

55201.explanation: The giant panda is going to extinct due to low reproductive rate. They live in mountain ranges in central China. There reproductively rate is very less due to climatic conditions.

55203.explanation: Lac is obtained by lac insects as secretion from the body. This secretion is wounded around the cocoon of lac insects.

55204.explanation: The life-span is the time period from birth to death of an organism. The life-span of honey bee drone is 1-2 months only. Queen has the longest life span in all three kinds of honey bees.

55205.explanation: The blue whale is the largest mammals about 30 meter in length and 180 tons in weight.

55206.explanation: The main nitrogenous excretory wastes of insects are uric acid. Uric acid is released in concentrated form. Other animals release nitrogenous wastes in form of ammonia and urea.

55207.explanation: Salamanders are a group of amphibians typically characterized by a lizard-like appearance, with slender bodies, blunt snouts, short limbs projecting at right angles to the body, and the presence of a tail in both larvae and adults.

55208.explanation: In elephants, two upper front teeth are modified into tusk of elephants. The continuous growth of tusk is enabled by formative tissues in the apical opening of the root of the teeth.

55209.explanation: Octopus belongs to molluscs but does not contain the shell. All other molluscs possess hard calcareous cells around their body to act as a protective covering.

55210.explanation: Crocodile and penguins are similar to whale and dogfish in having gill slits at some stage of their life cycle which is used as respiratory organs.

55212.explanation: Heloderma is the most poisonous, which is a verminous lizard native to the southwestern united states and Mexico.

55213.explanation: The voice producing organ of birds is called Syrinx. Voice is produced due to pressure variation. In human beings voice producing organ is called the larynx.

55214.explanation: Wool is generally obtained from sheep but the world’s highly prized wool yielding Paschimina breed is a goat generally reared in Kashmir valley. The wool is very soft with a lot of warmth.

55215.explanation: Project tiger is a tiger conservation programme launched in 1973 by the Government of India to maintain the rapidly decreasing number of tigers in India.

55216.explanation: The snakes generally do not build nest and lives in a burrow made by other animals or natural caves but King cobra found in India build their nest.

55217.explanation: The parasites live and obtain nutrients from the host. Head louse living on the human scalp and laying eggs in the hair are parasites in true sense.

55218.explanation: In some plants, like grass, Monstera, and the banyan tree, roots arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle and are called adventitious roots.

55219.explanation: The root is covered at the apex by a thimble-like structure called the root cap.

55220.explanation: The stem develops from the plumule of the embryo of a germinating seed.

55222.explanation: Roots developed from parts of the plant other than radicle are called adventitious roots.

55223.explanation: The leaf base bear two lateral small leaf like structures called stipules.

55224.explanation: Potato is a modified stem as it contains nodes in the form of eyes on potato tubers which germinate to produce new potato plants if placed in suitable conditions.

55226.explanation: The axillary buds of stems may also get modified into woody, straight, and pointed thorns in Citrus and Bougainvillea. They protect plants from browsing animals.

55227.explanation: A lateral branch with short internodes and each node bearing a rosette of leaves and a tuft of roots are found in aquatic plants such as Pistia and Eicchornia.

55228.explanation: The petiole help hold the blade to light. Long thin flexible petioles allow leaf blades to flutter in wind, thereby cooling the leaf and bringing fresh air to the leaf surface.

55229.explanation: The fleshy leaves of onion and garlic store food.

55231.explanation: Phylloclade are green succulent stems of indefinite growth that perform the function of photosynthesis due to the presence of chlorophyll.

55232.explanation: Those plants that eat insect to fulfil its protein requirement are called insectivorous plants. They have modified leaves to capture insects. Drosera is an insectivorous plant.

55252.explanation: In the acropetal succession of an inflorescence, the youngest floral buds are found at the distal end and the oldest flowers are found at the proximal end.

55253.explanation: In basal placentation, the placenta develops at the base of the ovary and a single ovule is attached to it.

55254.explanation: Aleurone layer of maize grain is rich in proteins. It is the outermost layer of the endosperm followed by the inner starchy endosperm.

55255.explanation: The flowers in which sepals and petals are not differentiated are called perianth. The individual component of the perianth is called Tepals.

55256.explanation: The condensed part of the stem which is specialized to take part in sexual reproduction of angiosperms is called flower. Flower produce seeds and fruits for the propagation of species.

55257.explanation: Fruits are the mature ovary or ovaries of one or more flowers. In fleshy fruits, the outer layer (which is often edible) is the pericarp, which is the tissue that develops from the ovary wall of the flower and surrounds the seeds.

55258.explanation: The mature seeds of plants do not possess endosperm because, it gets used up by the developing embryo during seed development.

55259.explanation: In monocotyledonous seeds, the single cotyledon is called as scutellum. It is found in cereal grains like rice, wheat, maize and other monocots.

55261.explanation: When more than one carpel is present, they may be free, it is called apocarpous.

55262.explanation: The placenta is the parenchymatous cushion present inside the ovary, ovules are borne. Ovules are attached with an ovary at the placenta to get nourishment.

55263.explanation: In parietal placentation, the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on the peripheral part. The ovary is one-chambered but it becomes two-chambered due to the formation of the false septum, e.g., mustard and Argemone.

55264.explanation: In the hypogynous flower, the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. The ovary in such flowers is said to be superior.

55265.explanation: When sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping, as in Calotropis, it is said to be valvate.

55266.explanation: The stamens in a flower may either remain free (polyandrous) or maybe united in varying degrees.

55267.explanation: Drupe is an indehiscent fruit in which an outer fleshy part and surrounds a shell of hardened endocarp with a seed. Mango is an example of a drupe.

55268.explanation: The edible part of Coconut is endosperm and embryo. The water inside the coconut is a cellular embryo and white kernel surrounding it is the main edible part that is the endosperm.

55269.explanation: A seed is made up of a seed coat and an embryo.

55270.explanation: In epigynous flowers, the margin of the thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it, the other parts of the flower arise above the ovary.

55273.explanation: In parietal placentation, the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on the peripheral part.

55274.explanation: Valvate aestivation is seen in the family Solanaceae.

55276.explanation: Monocarpic plants are those that flower, set seeds, and then die. Bamboo is monocarpic in nature that flowers once in a lifetime.

55277.explanation:
A true nut is a fruit composed of a hard shell and an edible seed. The shell does not open to release the seed (indehiscent), e.g., hazelnut, chestnuts.


Walnuts, almonds and pecans are drupes. The fruit of the coconut is a large, dry drupe. Cashew nuts are not true nuts. In the cashew nut, the ovary develops outside of the fruit (false fruit). The groundnut or peanut is not a true nut, but rather a legume. In groundnut, edible the cotyledons remain below ground and act as a storage organ.

55278.explanation: Cabbage is the bud of the cabbage plant. Cabbage bud is considered as largest bud present in angiosperms plants. A successive layer of leaves covers the buds to form the round structure on condensed stem.

55279.explanation: The white translucent, fleshy and edible structure present between seed and pericarp is called an aril. It is found in a mace of the nutmeg seed.

55280.explanation: The study of seed is called Spermology. Study of seed includes shape, size, colour and viability.

55281.explanation: The edible part of the apple is fleshy thalamus. Apple is an example of false fruit as it contains thalamus along with ovary.

55282.explanation: Pomegranate is the fruit which is formed from inferior ovary having succulent testa. Chambered compartment bears many seeds generally red in colour when ripened.

55284.explanation: When the several pistils of the same flower are separate and the ovary belongs to a single free carpel, it is called apocarpous.

55291.explanation: A plant having male, female and inter-sexual flowers is called polygamous flower. The same plant bears all three kinds of flowers.

55292.explanation: The symmetry in which a flower can be divided into two equal vertical halves by only one plane is called zygomorphic flower as in pea.

55293.explanation: Samara is a winged achene, a type of fruit which a flattened wing of fibrous, papery tissue develops from the ovary wall.

55294.explanation: A pinnately compound leaves are one which the midrib bears laterally a number of leaflets. Unipinnate compound leaves are present in neem plant.

55295.explanation: Placentation in a syncarpous, unilocular ovary bearing two or more placentae longitudinally along the wall is called parietal placentation.

55296.explanation: Cypsela is a single-seeded dry indehiscent fruit that develops one form part of the inferior ovary which is bicarpellary and syncarpous.

55297.explanation: Morphology is the branch of science in which we study about form, size, colour, structure and relative position of various parts of organisms.

55298.explanation: The smallest angiosperm plant is Wolffia. It is an aquatic plant, free-floating, green or yellow-green and without roots.

55299.explanation: Stipules are the small lateral outgrowth of the leaf base which protect the young leaf and its axillary buds in the young stage. It is a green leafy structure.

55300.explanation: Zostera is a marine angiosperms plant. The plants have broad leaves that help them in floating on the water surface, the root is poorly developed.

55302.explanation: The main plant body of banana is an aggregation of leaf base. The stem is highly reduced and rudimentary present at the base of the plant body.

55306.explanation: Conjunctive tissue is a narrow strip of tissue (parenchyma or sclerenchyma) that lies between xylem and phloem bundles of the root.

55310.explanation: In the conjoint type of vascular bundles, the xylem and phloem are situated at the same radius of vascular bundles. Such vascular bundles are common in stems and leaves. The conjoint vascular bundles usually have the phloem located only on the outer side of the xylem.

55330.explanation: Dumb-bell-shaped guard cells are found in grasses. Dumb-bell shaped guard cells are more advanced in evolutionary terms and more efﬁcient physiologically because guard cells of grasses require fewer solutes and less water to achieve a given unit increase in the aperture​.

55331.explanation: Monocotyledonous leaves are isobilateral as both the lower and upper sides of the leaves are the same.

55332.explanation: The palisade parenchymatous cell in the mesophyll region has numerous chloroplasts. Hence, it is the main seat of photosynthesis in leaf.

55333.explanation: Reticulate venation: In this type, the veins branch and unite forming a complicated network, All the veins are interconnected, like the strands of the net. Leaves of ‘Dicot plants’ generally have reticulate venation e.g., Hibiscus, Redgram.

55335.explanation: Bulliform cells or motor cells are large, bubble-shaped epidermal cells that occur in groups on the upper surface of the leaves of many monocots on the upper surface of the leaf.

55337.explanation: The stem shows the epidermis covered with a thin layer of cuticle, narrow cuticle, and each vascular bundle is conjoint, open, and is endarch protoxylem.

55340.explanation: A quiescent centre is a small group of cells with low mitotic activity. It is found at the tips of growing roots in the root meristem.

55341.explanation: The ground tissue of plants includes all tissues that are neither dermal nor vascular. It can be divided into three classes based on the nature of the cell walls.

55343.explanation: The vascular bundles in Hordeum vulgare (barley) plant are scattered in ground tissues, many in number, and vary in size-smaller towards the periphery and bigger towards the centre of the ground tissue, oval or rounded in outline, conjoint, collateral, and closed.

55344.explanation: The cells surrounding the stomata are called guard cells. The guard cells of the inner side are thicker and that of outer side is comparatively thinner.

55345.explanation: Opening and closing of stomatal pore of stomata is the function of guard cells. Change in osmotic potential cause the opening and closing of stomata.

55346.explanation: Epidermal cells are present on both sides of the leaves. The lower side contains more stomata. The upper surface of the leaf is called the adaxial epidermis.

55347.explanation: Tyloses are balloon-like ingrowths in vessels developing from parenchyma cells through the pits of the vessel wall of the xylem of secondary heartwood.

55348.explanation: Vascular bundles in which cambium is present between xylem and phloem are called open vascular bundles and those in which cambium is absent are called closed vascular bundles.

55353.explanation: Intrafascicular Cambium is primary meristem. It develops from the procambium of the stem apex. It is located inside the open vascular bundles, between phloem and xylem patches.

55407.explanation: Whales can live in cold water as they have a thick coat of blubber. Blubber help in providing insulating coat beneath the skin that prevents loss of heat from the body.

55409.explanation: Platelets are a little piece of blood cells that help wound healing and prevent bleeding by forming a blood clot. It is formed from the megakaryocytes.

55441.explanation: The lymph is different from the blood. It is known as tissue fluid. Lymph is yellowish in colour as it lacks RBCs and few proteins.

55445.explanation: Young ones of frogs are called nymphs. When the ootheca ruptures, 16 nymphs come out.

55449.explanation: All living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells.all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

55450.explanation: The first man to witness a live cell under a microscope was Anton van Leeuwenhoek, who in 1674 described the algae Spirogyra. Van Leeuwenhoek probably also saw bacteria.

55451.explanation: Cytoskeleton is a series of intercellular proteins that help a cell with shape, support andmovement. So, cytoskeleton is made up of proteinaceous filaments.

55452.explanation: Mitochondria contain cristae, finger-like projection of inner layer, thylakoid is present in chloroplast and lysosome is a digestive enzyme but RNA is absent in Chromosome.

55453.explanation: Mitochondria are present in both plants as well as animal cells. Plastids and central vacuoles are present in plant cells and centrioles are present in only animal cells.

55454.explanation: An animal cell does not possess plasmodesmata but they contain ribosomes, centriole, and plasmalemma. Plasmodesmata are the connection between two plant cells.

55455.explanation: Cellular Totipotency is the ability of a single cell to produce all cell types and to organize them into an entire organism when cultured in a suitable culture medium at the appropriate temperature and aeration conditions. Spores and Zygote are examples of totipotent cells.

55456.explanation: Fluid-Mosaic model is the most recent and accepted model of the plasma membrane. This model was proposed by Singer and Nicolson in 1972. The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables the lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.

55457.explanation: All animal cell has two small organelles called centrioles. Each centriole is surrounded by dense amorphous protoplasmic masses called Massules.

55458.explanation: Idiogram is a diagrammatic or systematized representation of the chromosome complement of an individual, species, or another group of organisms, indicating the number of chromosomes and their lengths, arm length ratio, centromere position, banding pattern.

55459.explanation: A special membranous structure is a mesosome which is formed by the extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell.

55460.explanation: PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms). They are generally smaller and multiply more rapidly than the eukaryotic cells.

55461.explanation: Glycocalyx differs in composition and thickness among different bacteria. It could be a loose sheath called the slime layer in some, while in others it may be thick and tough called the capsule. The cell wall determines the shape of the cell and provides strong structural support.

55462.explanation:
A bacterial flagellum has 3 basic parts: a filament, a hook, and a basal body.

The filament is the rigid, helical structure that extends from the cell surface.

The hook is a flexible coupling between the filament and the basal body.

The basal body consists of a rod and a series of rings that anchor the flagellum to the cell wall and the cytoplasmic membrane.

55463.explanation: The shapes of bacteria are bacillus (rod-like), coccus (spherical), vibrio (comma-shaped) and spirillum (spiral).

55478.explanation: Mitochondria are double membranous structure. The inner membrane of mitochondria thrown into folds to form finger-like structure is called cristae.

55479.explanation: The staining procedure developed by Gram viz., those that take up the gram stain are gram-positive and the others that do not are called gram-negative bacteria.

55480.explanation: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) differs from the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) in absence of ribosome on the surface of the endoplasmic reticulum.

55481.explanation: Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

55482.explanation:
The leucoplasts are the colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients. Leucoplast includes:



 Amyloplasts storing carbohydrates.
 Elaioplasts storing oils and fats.
 Aleuroplasts storing proteins.

55483.explanation: In a mature cell, the vacuole may occupy as much as 90 percent of the cell volume, such that the rest of the cell contents are flattened against the cell membrane.

55484.explanation: The chloroplast consists of a number of organized flattened membranous sacs called the thylakoids, Chlorophyll pigments are present in the thylakoids.

55485.explanation: The cell wall of a young plant cell, the primary walls capable of growth, which gradually diminishes as the cell matures and the secondary wall is formed on the inner (towards membrane) side of the cell.

55486.explanation: An elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures present in the cytoplasm is collectively referred to as the cytoskeleton.

55487.explanation: Active transport is the movement of molecules across a cell membrane in the direction against their concentration gradient, i.e. moving from an area of lower concentration to an area of higher concentration.

55488.explanation: Histone proteins the basic packer and arranger of chromatin.

55489.explanation: Animal cells have centrioles which are absent in almost all plant cells.

55490.explanation: Several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA and form a chain called polyribosomes or polysome. The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.

55491.explanation: The middle lamella is a layer mainly of calcium pectate which holds or glues the different neighbouring cells together.

55492.explanation: The plasmodesmata consist of pores, or channels, lying between individual plant cells, and connect the symplastic space in the plant. They can also be termed as "bridges" between two plant cells. The plasmodesmata separate the outer cell membranes of the plant cells. A plasmodesma (plural plasmodesmata, singular plasmodesma) is a channel through the cell wall that allows molecules and substances to move back and forth as needed.

55493.explanation: The German doctor Rudolf Virchow proposed in 1855 that all cells result from the division of previously existing cells, and this idea became a key piece of modern cell theory.

55494.explanation: The cytoskeleton in a cell is involved in functions like mechanical support, motility, maintenance of the shape of the cell.

55495.explanation: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP.

55496.explanation: Lysosomes are single membrane structures containing enzymes for digestion of all types of macromolecules.

55497.explanation: In-plant cells, the chloroplasts are responsible for trapping light energy essential for photosynthesis. The grana, in the plastid, is the site of light reactions.

55498.explanation: The nucleus contains the chromosomes which in turn contain the genetic material, DNA.

55499.explanation: Granum: A stacked membranous structure within the chloroplasts of plants and green algae that contains chlorophyll and is the site of the light reactions of photosynthesis. The saclike membranes that makeup grana are known as thylakoids.

55500.explanation: Most prokaryotic cells, particularly the bacterial cells, have a chemically complex cell envelope. All eukaryotic cells are not identical. Plant and animal cells are different as the former possess cell walls.

55501.explanation: The fluid mosaic model explains various observations regarding the structure of functional cell membranes. The model, which was devised by SJ Singer and GL Nicolson in 1972, describes the cell membrane as a two-dimensional liquid that restricts the lateral diffusion of membrane components.

55502.explanation: The cisternae of the Golgi apparatus is responsible for transporting, modifying, and packaging proteins and lipids into vesicles for delivery to targeted destinations.

55503.explanation:
Each ribosome consists of two subunits.

Eukaryotes have 80S ribosomes, each consisting of a small (40S) and large (60S) subunit.

Their 40S subunit has an 18S RNA (1900 nucleotides) and 33 proteins.

The large subunit is composed of a 5S RNA (120 nucleotides), 28S RNA (4700 nucleotides), a 5.8S RNA (160 nucleotides) subunits, and 46 proteins.

55504.explanation: Cell drinking is another name of pinocytosis. Pinocytosis, a process by which liquid droplets are ingested by living cells. Pinocytosis is one type of endocytosis, the general process by which cells engulf external substances, gathering them into special membrane-bound vesicles contained within the cell.

55505.explanation: Golgi complex or Golgi body consists of cisternae, tubules and spherical vesicles. Glycosome is not present in the Golgi complex.

55506.explanation: Lysosome is called a suicide bag because it contain a large number of digestive enzyme that can digest the whole cell in case of rapture.

55507.explanation: Plant cell contains large central vacuole which helps in waste disposal, cell elongation and storage but not involved in the formation of H2O2.

55508.explanation: A ribosome is a small, dense granular particle comprising usually three or four ribosomal RNA molecules and more than 50 protein molecules, interconnected to form the site of protein synthesis.

55509.explanation: The clear zone surrounding the Golgi apparatus is a zone of exclusion, where no other cellular activity takes place.

55510.explanation: Mitochondria is the largest cell organelles in animal cell and chloroplast is the largest cell organelles in a plant cell.

55511.explanation: A cell membrane shows fluid behaviour due to the mosaic of lipid and proteins. Fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane is the most accepted and recent model.

55512.explanation: Chromatin is the thread-like structure present in the nucleus. Chromatin has beads like structure called nucleosome that contain histone protein and DNA.

55513.explanation: Genetic material is mainly present in the nucleus of the cell but these two cell organelles also contain their own genetic material.

55514.explanation: A nerve cell or neuron is the longest cell in the human body. They are responsible for the transfer of information from one part of the body to the other in form of nerve impulses.

55515.explanation: Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organism (PPLO) or mycoplasma is considered as the smallest free-living organism.

55516.explanation: Tonoplasts are the fluid filled vacuoles or vesicles which are separated from cytoplasm by a selectively permeable membrane. It helps in maintaining turgidity of the cell.

55517.explanation: Secondary wall is formed inside the primary wall. Secondary wall is present nearest to the plasma membrane of a plant cell.

55518.explanation: Ions connected with forming cross-bridge is calcium ions (Ca2+) that help the impulse to cross the gaps at the synapse.

55519.explanation: A desmosome is a cell structure specialised for the cell to cell adhesion. They are located on lateral sides of plasma membranes.

55520.explanation: Prokaryotic and Eukaryotic cells and differentiated on the basis of the number of chromosomes, presence or absence of nuclear membrane and presence and absence of membrane-bounded organelles. The cell wall is not a difference.

55521.explanation: Oils have a lower melting point (e.g., gingely oil) and hence remain as oil in winters.

55523.explanation: Arachidonic acid has 20 carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon. Molecular formula - C20H32O2.

55524.explanation: Based on the number of amino and carboxyl groups, there are acidic (e.g., glutamic acid), basic (lysine) and neutral (valine) amino acids. Similarly, there are aromatic amino acids (tyrosine, phenylalanine, tryptophan).

55525.explanation: Sidechains that have pure hydrocarbon alkyl groups (alkane branches) or aromatic (benzene rings) are non-polar. Examples include valine, alanine, leucine, isoleucine, phenylalanine.

55526.explanation: Some lipids have phosphorous and a phosphorylated organic compound in them. These are phospholipids. They are found in the cell membrane.

55527.explanation: The cell wall of fungi is made of chitin, complex sugar molecules. The cell wall of plants is made up of cellulose.

55528.explanation: Hydrolysis of nucleic acid (DNA and RNA) produces pentose sugar (ribose or deoxyribose) purine and pyrimidine. Phosphoric acid is not released on hydrolysis of DNA or RNA.

55529.explanation: Enzymes are bio-catalyst. All the metabolic biochemical reactions are carried out with the help of the enzyme. No cell could survive without enzyme.

55530.explanation: Cellulose is the most abundant organic molecule present on earth. Cellulose forms the cell wall of all plant cells. The cell wall is the outermost protective layer of the cell.

55531.explanation: Everything in the universe is made up of elements. The body of living organisms contains mainly six elements. These are carbon, hydrogen, oxygen phosphorous, and sulphur. In fact, 98% of the living body is formed on these six elements.

55532.explanation: Chlorophyll molecule consists of a porphyrin ring and a long tail like a chain of carbon and hydrogen. The centre of the porphyrin ring is occupied by Mg ions.

55533.explanation: TDS stands for total dissolved solids which are inorganic salts dissolved in water. The TDS of soft water should be up to 120 ppm.

55552.explanation: The distance between two base pairs in DNA is 3.4 Ao. The length of DNA with 23 base pairs is 23 $\times$ 3.4 = 78.2 Ao.

55553.explanation: Both DNA and RNA consists of polymers of nucleotides. RNA is single-stranded but DNA is double-stranded. DNA polynucleotide contains thymine but RNA polynucleotide contains uracil.

55554.explanation: Each turn of DNA spirals contains 10 base pairs. So, in five turns of DNA total number of Base pair is 5 $\times$ 10 = 50 base pairs.

55555.explanation: Haemoglobin is responsible for carrying oxygen. The molecular formula of haemoglobin is C3032H872O872N780S8Fe4.

55557.explanation: The polymerisation is the chain of a large number of repeating units. Proteins are polymerization product of Amino acids combine together with peptide bonds.

55558.explanation: Collagen is a fibrous protein. It is the main structural protein in the extracellular space in the various connective tissues. It is the most abundant protein in mammals.

55559.explanation:
Proteins are made up of amino acids, which are organic compounds that combine to form the building blocks of proteins. There are 20 standard amino acids that are encoded by the universal genetic code and found in proteins. These include essential amino acids that must be obtained through the diet and non-essential amino acids that can be synthesized by the body.


Although there are some other amino acids like selenocysteine (sometimes referred to as the 21st amino acid) and pyrrolysine, these are not universally found in all proteins and are encoded by specific rare genetic mechanisms.

55560.explanation: Proteins are made of building blocks which are different. Proteins are heteropolymers made of amino acids.

55561.explanation: Ribulose bisphosphate Carboxylase-Oxygenase (RUBISCO) is the most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere.

55562.explanation: Tertiary structure: Long protein chain is folded upon itself like a hollow woolen ball. Gives a 3-dimensional view of protein, e.g., myosin.

55563.explanation: Dietary proteins are the source of essential amino acids. Therefore, amino acids can be essential or non-essential. The latter are those which our body can make, while we get essential amino acids through our diet.

55564.explanation: Proteins are molecules made of amino acids. They also play a central role in biological processes. For example, transport molecules such as oxygen, keep us healthy as part of the immune system and transmit messages from cell to cell.

55565.explanation: Glut-4 enables glucose transport into cells.

55566.explanation: Proteins human haemoglobin consists of 4 subunits. Two of these are identical to each other. Hence, two subunits of $\alpha $ type and two subunits of $\beta $ type together constitute the human haemoglobin (Hb).

55567.explanation: The ratio of the sum of guanine and cytosine to the sum of adenine and thymine is always constant for a species. This is due to the formation of hydrogen bonds between purine and pyrimidine.

55568.explanation: Protein molecules get denatured due to high temperature, very high or low pH, and high energy radiation but there is no effect due to high pressure.

55569.explanation: AUG codon is an initiation codon for protein synthesis. This codon code for amino acids methionine.

55573.explanation: Fevicol is a synthetic sticky substance insoluble in water and used for joining wood and paper is a type of resins.

55578.explanation: Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is a nucleotide. A nucleotide is formed by pentose sugar, nitrogenous base and phosphates. Many nucleotides join together to form polynucleotide.

55579.explanation: Enzymes are bio-catalyst that alter the rate of biochemical reactions in living organisms. The part of the enzyme where catalytic work is carried out is called the active site.

55581.explanation: The number of substrate molecules changed per minute by a molecule of the enzyme is called turn over number. Higher the turn over number more effective is the enzyme.

55582.explanation: Monoterpene eaters called pyrethroids found in flowers and leaves of chrysanthemum are used commercially for making insecticides.

55583.explanation: The inhibition of enzyme activity by the presence of a chemical that competes with the substrate for binding to the active site of the enzyme is called substrate analogue.

55585.explanation: Enzymes functional inside the living cells are called endoenzyme or intracellular enzyme. It functions only inside the cell in which it was produced.

55586.explanation: Inulin is a starchy substance found in a wide variety of fruits, vegetables and other herbs. This polysaccharide is not metabolized in the human body and used for kidney function.

55587.explanation: A number of enzymes require metal ions for their activity which form coordination bonds with side chains at the active site and at the same time form one or more coordination bonds with the substrate, e.g., zinc is a cofactor for the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase.

55588.explanation: Zinc is a cofactor for the pro­teolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase and forms coordina­tion bonds with the side chains of two histidines and one glutamic acid residue at the active site. A fourth bond is formed between zinc and the a-carboxyl group of the substrate amino acids, and it is here that the cleavage of the peptide occurs.

55589.explanation: Each enzyme shows its highest activity at a particular temperature and pH called the optimum temperature and optimum pH.

55591.explanation: Ligases catalyze the linking together of 2 compounds, e.g., enzymes that catalyze joining of C-O, C-S, C-N, P-O, etc. bonds.

55592.explanation: Apoenzyme: The polypeptide or protein part of the enzyme is called the apoenzyme and may be inactive in its original synthesized structure. The inactive form of the apoenzyme is known as a proenzyme or zymogen.

55594.explanation: Synthesis of glycoproteins and glycolipids take place in Golgi apparatus inside the cell. Golgi apparatus is located near the nucleus of the cell.

55595.explanation: The plants can show mitotic divisions in both haploid and diploid cells due to the alternation of generations in the life cycle.

55596.explanation: All the phases of the cell cycle in the mammalian cell are completed in 24 hours.

55597.explanation: S phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. During this time the amount of DNA per cell doubles. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C then it increases to 4C and even in anaphase, the chromosome numbers are changed.

55598.explanation: Yeast can progress through the cell cycle in only about 90 minutes due to its simple organisation.

55599.explanation: The M Phase represents the phase when the actual cell division or mitosis occurs/starts during the cell cycle.

55600.explanation: Onion root tip cells have 16 chromosomes in each cell, the same as the number of chromosomes in somatic cells.

55601.explanation: During the G2 phase, proteins and RNA are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.

55602.explanation: The interphase though called the resting phase is the time during which the cell is preparing for division by undergoing cell growth in an orderly manner. No divisional activities occur during this phase. Hence the name.

55603.explanation: In animals, mitotic cell division is only seen in the diploid somatic cell since mitosis produces cells with the same number of chromosomes as that of parents.

55604.explanation: In the Go stage, the cells are in a metabolically active state but do not divide unless there are some abnormal genes which reverse the same. This stage is also called the quiescent stage. Examples of human nerve cells.

55605.explanation: S phase marks the phase of DNA replication and chromosome duplication. In this phase increase in the amount of DNA takes place. No synthesis of proteins or RNA takes place.

55606.explanation: Before the completion of Mitosis reappearance of the nuclear membrane takes place along with the formation of nucleolus so that the cells become separate entities after cytokinesis but having the same chromosome number as parent cells.

55607.explanation: It is the stage of the cell cycle during which the cells remain metabolically active and do not divide due to the absence of mitogens and energy-producing compounds.

55608.explanation: Cell division consists of karyokinesis and cytokinesis. During karyokinesis division of chromosomes takes place and during cytokinesis division of cytoplasm takes place. Ultimately the cell divides into two halves.

55622.explanation: Four haploid cells are formed at the end of meiosis II. It is the reductional division resulting in a halving of chromosome number in daughter cells.

55623.explanation: The plane of alignment of the chromosomes at metaphase is referred to as the metaphase plate. This stage is also called a tetrad stage.

55624.explanation: The metaphase is characterized by all the chromosomes coming to lie at the equator with one chromatid of each chromosome connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from one pole and its sister chromatid connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from the opposite pole.

55625.explanation: Cell growth results in disturbing the ratio between the nucleus and the cytoplasm. It, therefore, becomes essential for the cell to divide to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio. The cell becomes stable when the N/C ratio is 1.

55626.explanation: Mitosis is called equational division. Since the parent cells are haploid so mitosis will lead to the restoration of chromosome number in haploid cells.

55627.explanation: Since in mitosis the number of chromosomes in the parent and progeny cells is the same, it is also called an equational division.

55628.explanation: In-plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls. The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor, called the cell plate which hardens to give rise to the middle lamella.

55629.explanation: The middle lamella cements the tertiary walls of two adjacent plant cells. It is formed out of materials of the cell plate.

55630.explanation: The astral body is formed of microtubules. Astral bodies are produced by centriolar division prior to the start off during cell division and attach with the centromere of the chromosome during.

55631.explanation: In the plant cell, mitosis cell division is generally controlled by cytokinin hormone. It increases the rate of cell division leading to increased cell production. Auxin is also required for cell division in the plant.

55633.explanation: In animal cell, cytokinesis takes place by furrow which appears at the margins of the plasma membrane and gradually deepens towards the central part of the cell. Ultimately the furrow divides the cell into two halves. This method of cytokinesis is known as cleavage cytokinesis.

55634.explanation: Colchicine is an alkaloid used in plant breeding for doubling of chromosomes by inhibiting cytokinesis. It is also called as mitotic poison. It is extracted from the bark of plant belonging to the genus Colchicum.

55635.explanation: The most common material used for the study of mitosis cell division in the classroom is onion root and broad bean root tip. They can be grown quickly and in all seasons. Also, they are easier to handle with and divisional stages are completed quickly.

55636.explanation: A disturbance in the nucleoplasmic ratio will cause the cell to divide and attain stable ration which is 1. If it is less or more than 1 the cell becomes unstable and divides again.

55637.explanation: Regeneration is the ability of an organism to regain its lost body parts. Regeneration is achieved by mitotic cell division to maintain the same number of chromosomes in the cell.

55638.explanation: Meiosis cell division consists of two phases. The first phase is called meiosis I during which the number of chromosomes reduces to half the number in parent cells. In meiosis II chromosome number remain the same.

55639.explanation: Interkinesis is the stage connecting meiosis I and meiosis II cell division. It is a brief period between two stages. No DNA synthesis occurs during this period. The cell undergoes preparation for the next divisional stages.

55640.explanation: Chromosome appeared beaded during leptotene stage of the prophase of meiosis I due to the distinct appearance of nucleosomes. Chromatin materials start condensing after that stage.

55641.explanation: Chiasmata is formed due to crossing over. During diakinesis of prophase, I of meiosis terminalization of chiasmata takes place which indicates the end of crossing over and separation of the non-sister chromatids.

55643.explanation: Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids of two homologous chromosomes involved in the pairing process.

55644.explanation: Meiosis cell division is involved in gametes formation as gametes contain half the number of chromosomes that a normal cell diploid cell contains. Gametes fuse to produce a diploid zygote.

55645.explanation: Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores. These structures serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres (formed by the spindle fibres) to the chromosomes.

55647.explanation: Meiosis cell division results in halving of chromosome number in daughter cells, recombination of genes and formation of spores and gametes.

55648.explanation: In telophase I, the nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear indicating the process of completion of nuclear division. Meiosis II is similar to mitosis.

55650.explanation: In oocytes of some vertebrates, diplotene can last for months or years. Such a nucleus showing arrested diplotene stage is called mesokaryotic nucleus.

55651.explanation: The stage between the two meiotic divisions is called interkinesis and is generally short-lived. Interkinesis is followed by prophase II, much simpler prophase than prophase I.

55652.explanation: Crossing over is the exchange of chromosomes segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous pair. It brings about gene recombination and produces genetic variation. Pachytene is the third stage of the prophase of meiosis during which the homologous chromosomes become short and thick and divide into four distinct chromatids.

55653.explanation: If a cell divides every minute, the number of cells gets doubled at the end of each minute. If a 100 ml beaker is filled in one hour, it will take 59 minutes to fill a 50 ml beaker.

55654.explanation: The number of chromosomes reduces to half at the end of meiosis cell division. If the plant has 2n = 8 chromosome the number of chromosomes present in daughter cells after meiosis II is 4 only.

55655.explanation: The transition period between M-phase of Meiosis I and M-phase II during which no replication of DNA occurs is called as interkinesis. The cell undergoes preparation for the next round of division.

55656.explanation: Crossing over results in the exchange of genetic material between two homologous chromosomes during meiosis I of cell division.

55657.explanation: Rudolph Virchow was the first scientist who stated that new cells are formed from the division of pre-existing cells. It is a part of cell theory postulated by Virchow in 1855.

55658.explanation: A homologous chromosome is two similar chromosomes of each type present in diploid cells. During meiosis homologous chromosomes separate from each other. In homologous pair, one chromosome is from mother while the other is from father.

55659.explanation: The astral body is formed of protein microtubules. Astral bodies are produced by centriole during cell division and attach with the centromere of the chromosome.

55661.explanation: In Diploid cells, each homologous chromosome consists of one paternal and one maternal chromosome that fuses together during fertilization of gametes. These chromosomes are called homologous chromosomes.

55662.explanation: Polyploidy is the condition in which more than one set of chromosomes is present in one cell. It is the property of increasing the number of chromosome sets of the cell and results due to the failure of the segregation of non-sister chromatids after crossing over.

55663.explanation: Egg yolk contains a lampbrush chromosome where two homologous chromosomes with several chiasmata with several loops in the chromatic region are found. They are also called giant chromosomes.

55664.explanation: The number of chromosome changes during anaphase of meiosis I and the amount of DNA content increases during S-phase of the cell cycle. This is reflected in the disturbance of the nucleocytoplasmic ratio.

55736.explanation: A saprophyte or saprotroph is an organism that gets its energy from dead and decaying organic matter. This may be decaying pieces of plants or animals. This means that saprophytes are heterotrophs. They are consumers in the food chain.

55737.explanation: Plants, unlike animals, have no special systems for breathing or gaseous exchange. Stomata and lenticels allow gaseous exchange by diffusion.

55738.explanation: Catabolism is the process of break down any large substance into smaller ones. In respiration, glucose is broken down into carbon dioxide and water molecules. Thus it is referred to as a catabolic reaction.

55739.explanation: Reduction in consumption of respiratory substrate when the mode of respiration is changed from aerobic to anaerobic is called pasture effect. It is studied in the case of Saccharomyces.

55740.explanation: Glycolysis means the splitting of glucose. The first step of the process occurs in the cytoplasm of the cell and yields a small amount of energy (measured in units of ATP) and two molecules of pyruvate. The other steps occur in the mitochondria. It is an ongoing process as your cells have a constant need for energy.

55741.explanation: The scheme of glycolysis was given by Gustav Embden, Otto Meyerhof, and J. Parnas, and is often referred to as the EMP pathway.

55742.explanation: The complete combustion of glucose, which produces carbon dioxide and water as end products, yields energy most of which is given out as heat.

55743.explanation: Glycolysis involves the breaking down of sugar (generally glucose, although fructose and other sugars may be used) into more manageable compounds in order to produce energy. The net end products of glycolysis are two Pyruvate, two NADH, and two ATP.

55744.explanation: At the end of glycolysis pathway, 2 net ATP molecules at step 6 and step 9 are produced.

55745.explanation: Hexokinase is an enzyme that phosphorylates hexoses (six-carbon sugars), forming hexose phosphate. In most organisms, glucose is the most important substrate of hexokinases, and glucose-6-phosphate is the most important product.

55746.explanation: Glycolysis is a series of reactions and extracts energy from glucose by splitting it into two three-carbon molecules called pyruvates. Glycolysis is an ancient metabolic pathway, meaning that it evolved long ago, and it is found in the great majority of organisms alive today. Glycolysis has ten steps.

55747.explanation: Fermentation is an anaerobic breakdown of carbohydrates in which an organic molecule is the final electron acceptor. It does not involve an electron transport system. Furthermore, it is a partial breakdown of glucose giving a little energy, 2 net ATPs per glucose by the way of substrate-level phosphorylation.

55749.explanation: Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) is an enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of lactate to pyruvate. When oxygen is inadequate for cellular respiration. This is an important step in energy production in cells. Many different types of cells in the body contain this enzyme. Some of the organs relatively rich in LDH are the heart, kidney, liver, and muscle.

55750.explanation: Cells store energy in a molecule called adenosine triphosphate (abbreviated as ATP). The adenosine molecule has three phosphate groups attached to it (triphosphate means three phosphates) which are held together by high energy bonds. If one of these bonds is broken, a great amount of energy is released which can be used in an endergonic reaction.

55766.explanation: Aerobic respiration is the process that leads to complete oxidation of organic substances in the presence of oxygen and releases carbon dioxide, water, and a large amount of energy present in the substrate. This type of respiration is most common in higher organisms.
