68374.explanation: The liver weighs about 3 pounds and is the second-largest organ in the body. It is roughly triangular accessory organ of the digestive system located to the right of the stomach, just inferior to the diaphragm and superior to the small intestine.

68375.explanation: The small intestine is the longest part of the alimentary canal. It extends from the pylorus of the stomach to the junction between cecum and ileum. The small intestine is about 6 meters or 20 feet long and the large intestine is about 1.5 meters or 5 feet long.

68376.explanation: Digestion starts from the mouth where food is broken down into pieces through mastication by teeth and mixed with saliva. Saliva contains salivary amylase which starts the digestion of starch.

68428.explanation: Amphibians have evolved multiple ways of breathing. Young amphibians, like tadpoles, use gills to breathe, and they do not leave the water. As the tadpole grows, the gills disappear and lungs grow (though some amphibians retain gills for life). These lungs are primitive and are not as evolved as mammalian lungs. Adult amphibians are lacking or have a reduced diaphragm, so breathing through the lungs is forced. The other means of breathing for amphibians is diffusion across the skin.

68429.explanation: The voice box, sound box or larynx, is the portion of the respiratory (breathing) tract containing the vocal cords which produce sound.

68430.explanation: Lung alveoli are the ends of the respiratory tree, branching from either alveolar sacs or alveolar ducts, which like alveoli are both sites of gas exchange with the blood as well. Alveoli are particular to mammalian lungs.

68431.explanation: Carbaminohemoglobin is a compound of haemoglobin and carbon dioxide and is one of the forms in which carbon dioxide exists in the blood. 30% of carbon dioxide is carried in blood this way (60% carried in the blood as bicarbonate [hydrogen carbonate], 10% carried as free CO2, in solution, or plasma).

68432.explanation: The inspiratory reserve volume (IRV) is the additional volume (approx. 2500 to 3100 ml) of air that can be forcibly inhaled after the inspiration of a normal tidal volume.

68433.explanation: Residual volume (RV) is about 1100 ml to 1200 ml which is the volume of air still remaining in the lungs after the expiratory reserve volume is exhaled.

68434.explanation:
Total Lung Capacity = IRV + TV + ERV + RV

Where:

IRV: Inspiratory Reserve Volume

TV: Tidal Volume

ERV: Expiratory Reserve Volume

RV: Residual Volume

68435.explanation: The pleural membrane is thin, moist, slippery, and has two layers. The outer, or parietal, pleura lines the inside of the rib cage and the diaphragm while the inner, visceral or pulmonary, layer covers the lungs.

68436.explanation: The lungs are the primary organs of the respiratory system responsible for exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide between the blood and the atmosphere. They are not directly involved in controlling breathing rhythm, blood purification, or digestion.

68437.explanation: During swallowing the glottis is covered by a cartilaginous flap called epiglottis. This prevents the entry of food into the respiratory tract.

68472.explanation:
The hemoglobin level is expressed as the amount of hemoglobin in grams (gm) per deciliter (dL) of whole blood, a deciliter being 100 milliliters.

The normal ranges for hemoglobin depend on the age and, beginning in adolescence, the gender of the person. The normal ranges are:



 Newborns: 17 to 22 gm/dL
 One(1) week of age: 15 to 20 gm/dL
 One (1) month of age: 11 to 15 gm/dL
 Children: 11 to 13 gm/dL
 Adult males: 14 to 18 gm/dL
 Adult women: 12 to 16 gm/dL
 Men after middle age: 12.4 to 14.9 gm/dL
 Women after middle age: 11.7 to 13.8 gm/dL


So his Haemoglobin count are normal, he don't need to worry.

68473.explanation: The normal leukocyte counts range between 4300 - 10000 per cubic mm in a healthy person. It can also be referred to as the leukocyte count and can be expressed in international units as 4.3 to 10.8 $\times$ 109 cells per litre.

68475.explanation: A person who has group AB blood and is, therefore, able to receive blood from a person with any other blood type. Group AB blood contains red blood cells that have both antigens A and B and thus do not have reactive antibodies in its plasma to these antigens, which are found in some other blood types.

68476.explanation: In an open circulatory system, the blood is not contained within a vessel system. Instead, tissues and organs are surrounded by the circulatory fluid, which is known as hemolymph. Hemolymph is like blood and includes interstitial fluid, which is the fluid that usually surrounds tissues. Hydra has an open circulatory system.

68478.explanation: Systemic circulation carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle, through the arteries, to the capillaries in the tissues of the body. From the tissue capillaries, the deoxygenated blood returns through a system of veins to the right atrium of the heart.

68479.explanation: The aorta (the main blood supplier to the body) branches off into two main coronary blood vessels (also called arteries). These coronary arteries branch off into smaller arteries, which supply oxygen-rich blood to the entire heart muscle. The right coronary artery supplies blood mainly to the right side of the heart.

68481.explanation: The heart beats 70 times a minute, with each beat the heart pumps 60 to 90 millilitres (2 to 3 ounces) of blood out of the heart. It can move 5 to 7 litres of blood in one minute and 7600 litres (2000 gallons) per day. In a lifetime, it beats over 2.5 billion times and pumps over 200 million litres of blood.

68482.explanation: Heart rate is the number of heartbeats per unit of time. Usually, the heart rate is expressed as beats per minute (BPM). The heart beats to supply oxygenated clean blood from the left ventricle to the blood vessels of the body via the aorta. The average resting heart rate is 72 beats per minute (bpm).

68525.explanation: An ammonotelic organism excretes nitrogenous waste as soluble ammonia. Most of the aquatic animals including protozoans, crustaceans, platyhelminths, cnidarians, poriferans, echinoderms, fishes, larvae/tadpoles of amphibians are ammonotelic. Rohu is a species of fish.

68527.explanation: The skin is one of the largest organs in the body in surface area and weight. The skin consists of two layers: the epidermis and the dermis. Beneath the dermis lies the hypodermis or subcutaneous fatty tissue. The skin has three main functions: protection, regulation, and sensation.

68528.explanation: The excretory organ of cockroach is the malpighian tubules. It is found at the junction of the midgut and hindgut and is about 150 in number. They are fine, yellow coloured and branched threads present in bundles. They lie freely in the haemolymph.

68530.explanation: The nephronil is the basic structural and functional unit of the kidney. Its chief function is to regulate the concentration of water and soluble substances like sodium salts by filtering the blood, reabsorbing what is needed and excreting the rest as urine.

68531.explanation:
The normal range for 24-hour urine volume is 800 to 2000 milliliters per day (with a normal fluid intake of about 2 liters per day). This is the range.

So average = ${800+2000\over 2} $ = 1400ml = 1.4 L

68533.explanation: Anti Diuretic hormone or ADH is also called arginine vasopressin. It's a hormone made by the hypothalamus in the brain and stored in the posterior pituitary gland. It tells your kidneys how much water to conserve. ADH constantly regulates and balances the amount of water in your blood.

68534.explanation: Glycosuria is a condition characterized by an excess of sugar in the urine, typically associated with diabetes or kidney disease.

68570.explanation: The muscle which shows no cross striations are called non-striated muscles or unstriped muscles. They look smooth, hence are called smooth muscles. The activity of these muscles are not under the control of the will of the animal, so they are known as involuntary muscles. These muscles are seen in hollow internal organs (viscera) such as the stomach, intestine, blood vessels, urinary bladder, uterus, etc.

68571.explanation: Fascia is an internal connective tissue that wraps around organs, providing support, and holding parts together. It has the appearance of a very thin spider web, connecting layers of muscle and surrounding all internal body tissues.

68573.explanation: Calcium channels (Ca++ channel) govern physiological functions including neurotransmitter and hormone release, muscle contraction, and the regulation of gene expression.

68574.explanation:
Based on the colour the skeletal muscles are classified into two types. They are red muscle(red meat or slow muscle) and white muscle (white meat or fast muscle).


Red muscles:



 Example: extensor muscle on the back of the human body
 Redmuscles are thin muscle fibres
 Red in colour due to the presence of a large amount of myoglobin


White muscles



 Example: Muscles of the eyeball
 White muscles are thick muscle fibres
 White in colour due to less amount of myoglobin

68576.explanation: The components of the girdle of the upper extremity, the pectoral girdle, are the shoulder blade, or scapula, and the collarbone, or clavicle. The head of the humerus, the long bone of the upper arm, fits into the glenoid cavity, a depression in the scapula.

68577.explanation: The pubic symphysis or symphysis pubis is the midline cartilaginous joint (secondary cartilaginous) uniting the superior rami of the left and right pubic bones. It is located anterior to the urinary bladder and superior to it. In males, the suspensory ligament of the penis attaches to the pubic symphysis.

68615.explanation: The parasympathetic nervous system is one of three divisions of the autonomic nervous system. Sometimes called the rest and digest system, the parasympathetic system conserves energy as it slows the heart rate, increases intestinal and gland activity, and relaxes sphincter muscles in the gastrointestinal tract.

68616.explanation: Nodes of Ranvier, also known as myelin sheath gaps, are periodic gaps in the insulating myelin sheaths of myelinated axons where the axonal membrane is exposed to the extracellular space.

68617.explanation: Ions are distributed unequally on the inside and outside of cells, and that cell membranes are selectively permeable to different ions. Potassium (K+) is particularly important for the resting potential. The membrane is highly permeable to K+.

68622.explanation: Reflex actions do not involve the brain. Reflex actions are controlled by the spinal cord. Any reflex action is a result of the spinal cord. The brain usually controls all voluntary actions.

68674.explanation: The body does not make iodine, so it is an essential part of your diet. Iodine deficiency can lead to enlargement of the thyroid (goiter), hypothyroidism, and mental retardation in infants and children whose mothers were iodine deficient during pregnancy.

68676.explanation: Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) is a hormone produced in the anterior, or front, the pituitary gland in the brain. The function of ACTH is to regulate levels of the steroid hormone cortisol, which released from the adrenal gland.

68677.explanation: In females, an acute rise of LH ("LH surge") triggers ovulation and development of the corpus luteum. In males, where LH had also been called interstitial cell-stimulating hormone (ICSH), it stimulates Leydig cell production of testosterone. It acts synergistically with FSH.

68679.explanation: White blood cells and platelets are produced in the bone marrow, the soft fatty tissue inside bone cavities. Two types of white blood cells, T and B cells (lymphocytes), are also produced in the lymph nodes and spleen, and T cells are produced and mature in the thymus gland.

68680.explanation: The primary function of a $\beta $ cell is to store and release insulin. Insulin is a hormone that brings about effects which reduce blood glucose concentration. Beta cells can respond quickly to spikes in blood glucose concentrations by secreting some of their stored insulin while simultaneously producing more.

68682.explanation: Erythropoiesis is the process that produces red blood cells (erythrocytes). It is stimulated by decreased O2 in circulation, which is detected by the kidneys, which then secrete the hormone erythropoietin.

68683.explanation: Cholecystokinin plays a key role in facilitating digestion within the small intestine. It is secreted from mucosal epithelial cells in the first segment of the small intestine (duodenum) and stimulates delivery into the small intestine of digestive enzymes from the pancreas and bile from the gallbladder.

129844.explanation: R.H. Whittaker in 1969 proposed the five kingdom classification . He divided organisms into kingdom monera, protista,fungi,plantae and animalia. He divided organisms on the basis of following criteria-cell structure,thallus organisation,mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationship.

129845.explanation: In trichome, the cells are joined loosely from end to end and look like the bead of a string. Trichome may contain intercalary or terminal heterocyst sites of nitrogen fixation resting bodies called akinetes.

129846.explanation: Require water for dispersal of their gametes.

129848.explanation: In Marchantia elater mother cells give rise to elaters which helps in scattering the spore differentiated from the spore mother cells. In Riccia and Funaria the elaters not found. Elaters are small neutral cells in form of fibre in capsule.

129849.explanation: Corpora allata is the plural form of Corpus Allatum . It is an endocrine gland which generates juvenile hormone and plays crucial role in metamorphosis in insects.

129851.explanation: Archaeocytes may be converted into other types of cells and are also called as undifferentiated totipotent cells.

129852.explanation: Python have tiny Hind limbs bones buried in muscles towards their tail ends. Such feature is useless for performing specific tasks. And vestigial legs are clue that snakes are descended from lizards.

129853.explanation: The food particles are ingested into the choanocytes or passed directly into underlying amoebocytes.

140045.explanation: Small tongue shaped outgrowth or appendage is present at the base of each young leaf on its adaxial or upper side. At the base of ligule, a sheath of elongated secretory cells are present called as glossopodium.

148888.explanation:
The mutualism have shown that the green algae (zoochloreiiae) symbiotic with fresh-water invertebrates augment the survival of the host during periods of low food supply.

This benefit is probably due to low molecular weight compounds of photo synthetic origin which the algae pass on to their hosts.

148889.explanation: Chameleon showing protective colouration because chameleon has a distinctive feature to blend in its surrounding colouration. It uses this feature to hide from enemy.

148890.explanation:
The Tetraodontidae is a family of primarily marine and estuarine fish of the order Tetraodontiformes. The family includes many familiar species which are variously called pufferfish, puffers, balloon fish, blow fish, blowies, bubble fish, globe fish, toadies, honey toads, sugar toads, and sea squab. They are morphologically similar to the closely related porcupine fish, which have large external spines.

The majority of pufferfish species are toxic and some are among the most poisonous vertebrates in the world.

148891.explanation: In arthropods, excretion takes place through malpighian tubules. In Platyhelminthes animals, specialised cells called flame cells are responsible for osmoregulation and excretion.

158811.explanation: The fungi imperfecti or imperfect fungi, also known as Deuteromycota, are fungi which do not fit into the commonly established taxonomic classifications of fungi that are based on biological species concepts or morphological characteristics of sexual structures because their sexual form of reproduction has never been observed. Only their asexual form of reproduction is known, meaning that these fungi produce their spores asexually, in the process called sporogenesis.

158812.explanation: Slime moulds alternates between a unicellular feeding stage and a multicellular reproductive stage

158814.explanation:
Rodents (from Latin rodere, "to gnaw") are mammals of the order Rodentia, which are characterized by a single pair of continuously growing incisors in each of the upper and lower jaws. About 40% of all mammal species are rodents; they are found in vast numbers on all continents except Antarctica. They are the most diversified mammalian order and live in a variety of terrestrial habitats, including human-made environments.

Most rodents are small animals with robust bodies, short limbs, and long tails. They use their sharp incisors to gnaw food, excavate burrows, and defend themselves. Most eat seeds or other plant material, but some have more varied diets.

158815.explanation: In insect physiology, the corpus allatum (plural: corpora allata) is an endocrine gland which generates juvenile hormone; as such, it plays a crucial role in metamorphosis.

158816.explanation:
The western mosquitofish (Gambusia affinis) is a species of freshwater fish, also known as mosquitofish or gambezi.

Mosquitofish were intentionally introduced in many areas with large mosquito populations to decrease the population of mosquitoes by eating the mosquito larvae.

158817.explanation:
Remiges are the large stiff flight feathers of the wings.

Barbules can be defined as the minute filament-like structures projecting from the barb of the feather.

Quill feathers at the base of quill wings are called as coverts. These are small feathers meant for filling gaps on the wings and tail. They are small and oppose the buoyancy of the air. Down feathers help to insulate the birds and contribute in the buoyancy.

158818.explanation:
Weberian ossicles (Weberian apparatus) Structures found in bony fish belonging to the orders Cypriniformes and Siluriformes, and derived from the first four vertebrae. They form a link between the inner-ear region and the swimbladder, facilitating sound reception.

Weberian apparatus is an anatomical structure that connects the swim bladder to the auditory system in fishes belonging to the superorder Ostariophysi. When it is fully developed in adult fish, the elements of the apparatus are sometimes collectively referred to as the Weberian ossicles. The presence of the structure is one of the most important and phylogenetically significant distinguishing characteristics of the Ostariophysi.

158819.explanation: Sensory cells which are scattered among the other epidermal cells specially near the mouth and tentacles and on the basal disk. The free end of each sensory cell bears a flagellum which is the sensory receptor for chemical and tactile stimuli. The other end branches into fine processes which synapse with the nerve cells.

158820.explanation: Adult wucheria get the nutrition from the lymphatic vessels by directly sucking the blood.

158821.explanation: The ventral nerve cord makes up the part of the central nervous system of some phyla of bilaterians particular in nematodes annelids and arthropods.

158822.explanation: Silverfish, scorpion, dragon fly and prawn all belong to phylum Arthropoda. Jointed appendages and chitinous exoskeleton are the characteristic features of this phylum.

158823.explanation: Leptospirosis is a disease caused by leptospira bacterial species these bacteria are carried in the urine of infected animals such as pigs,cattles and many wildlife species.If urine from an infected animal is deposited or drains into a body of freshwater the bacteria can survive there for weeks and people may come into close contact with freshwater or wet soil when they participate in outdoor activities. And whereas bilharzia is a disease caused by parasitic flatworms and are transmitted from fresh water snails to humans.

178745.explanation: Batrachospermum may have triphasic lifecycle. They show alternation of generations; in addition to gametophyte generation, many have two sporophyte generations.

178746.explanation: Reticulate chloroplast is a plastid that forms a cylindrical network in the peripheral region of the cells of some algae.

246649.explanation: Monera contains all prokaryotic organisms and bacteria. Fungi can have unicellular as well as multicellular organisms that comes under the Protista.

246650.explanation: Halos means salt and phile means loving.

246651.explanation: Slime molds were earlier kept under kingdom fungi but due to multinucleate character and naked protoplasm, they are now considered as belonging to monera.

246652.explanation: It is a symbiotic association between a fungus and a plant. The term mycorrhiza refers to the role of the fungus in the plant's rhizosphere, its root system.

246654.explanation: Beijerinek demonstrated that extracts of infected tobacco plant can cause infection in healthy plants and termed the fluid as contagium vivum fluidum (infectious living fluid).

246655.explanation: In a lichen; the fungal component is called mycobiont and algal component is called phycobiont.

246656.explanation: Absence of protein coat in viroid but present in virus

246658.explanation: Since viruses are considered as borderline case between living and non-living things; no kingdom has been specified for them.

246659.explanation: Phycomycetes belong to fungi. They live in aquatic habitats, moist and damp places, as obligate parasites on plants and on decaying wood.

273012.explanation: Myxomycetes belong to kingdom Protista and are known as slime molds. They have pseudopodia-like structures used for engulfing food. Asexual reproduction takes place through fragmentation or spores formation.

273021.explanation: Thallus of the Volvox is referred to as coenobium. It refers to the colony of the Volvox that is composed of some definite number of the cells. It is circular or ovoid and is hollow with an anterior and posterior end. The anterior end is always directed forward during the movement of Volvox.

273022.explanation: A few species of Selaginella are desert plants known as "resurrection plants", because they curl up in a tight, brown or reddish ball during dry times, and uncurl and turn green in the presence of moisture.

273023.explanation:
Hornworts are a group of non-vascular plants constituting the division Anthocerotophyta. The common name refers to the elongated horn-like structure, which is the sporophyte. As in mosses and liverworts, the flattened, green plant body of a hornwort is the gametophyte plant.

Hornworts may be found worldwide, though they tend to grow only in places that are damp or humid. Some species grow in large numbers as tiny weeds in the soil of gardens and cultivated fields. Large tropical and sub-tropical species of Dendroceros may be found growing on the bark of trees.

The total number of species is still uncertain. While there are more than 300 published species names, the actual number could be as low as 100-150 species.

273024.explanation: Antherozoid (spermatozoid) are the male gamete produced in the (antheridia of fungi, algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, and some gymnosperms.

273025.explanation: Pteridophytes have sporophytic(diploid cell body) plant body dominantly and thus need meiosis to form gametes(microspore and megaspore) during sexual reproduction.

273026.explanation: Bryophytes do not have a true vascular system and are unable to pull water and nutrients up from the ground at any significant distance. Lacking this specializedsystem distinguishes bryophytes from ferns and flowering plants. It is for this reason that they are considered to be rather primitive plants.

273027.explanation: Like any other plant, algae, when grown using sunlight, consume (or absorb) carbon dioxide (CO2) as they grow, releasing oxygen (O2) for the rest of us to breathe. For high productivity, algae require more CO2, which can be supplied by emissions sources such as power plants, ethanol facilities, and other sources.

273028.explanation: Funaria is a bryophyte. In bryophyte, the main plant body is gametophytic in nature. Embryo formed by fertilization grows into a sporophyte. The sporophyte is dependent on gametophyte. It produces haploid meiospores which germinate to produce a gametophyte.

273030.explanation: In apophysis of capsule of moss, the guard cells and subsidiary cells originate from same mother cell.

273031.explanation: Genera Plantarum is written by Carolus Linnaeus but work of Bentham and Hooker was published in it.

273032.explanation: Classifying organisms on the basis of descent from a common ancestor is called phylogenetic classification.

273033.explanation: In Genera Plantarum, the seed plants were classified as Gymnosperms, Dicotyledons ans Monocotyledons. But there were certain plants which were not classified in either of class and called as disputed orders. These disputed orders were then mentioned in Ordines Anomali.

273034.explanation: Megasporophyll is the structure on which the megaspores are formed. This structure corresponds to the carpel of a flowering plant.

273035.explanation: Apogamy is a type of reproduction, occurring in some ferns, in which the sporophyte develops from the gametophyte without fusion of gametes. It is the development of a diploid cell in the embryo sac of flowering plants into an embryo without being fertilized.

273036.explanation: The given match i.e. a-(iii), b-(i), c-(iv), d-(v), e-(ii) is correct.

273037.explanation: Cycads produce pollen, but the sperm still swims down the pollen tube using flagella. As it also has a naked seed, it is classified as a gymnosperm.

273038.explanation: Phyllode is that part of a plant in which its petiole becomes flat leaf like and functions as a normal leaf.

273039.explanation: Verticillaster type of inflorescence is found in Labiatae or Lamiaceae family. In this type of inflorescence, leaves are arranged in the opposite manner on the stem. From the axil of each leaf, inflorescence develops. From the main axis, the lateral axis arises on which flowers are found. Now from these branches, lateral branches develop also which bear flowers. In this type of inflorescence, each dichasial cyme changes into a monochasial (scorpioid) cyme. It is commonly found in families such as Salvia, Ocimum (Tulsi), Coleus.

273040.explanation: Vanda is a genus in the orchid family Orchidaceae and it is basically an epiphytic plant. In epiphytic or semi-epiphytic plants velamen is found. Velamen is spongy multiple epidermises that cover the roots of some epiphytic or semi-epiphytic plants.

273042.explanation: In Gloriosa the leaf apices are sensitive to function as tendril. It is a type of leaf modification of type leaf type tendril.

273043.explanation: In the Parietal placentation, the ovary is one chambered (unilocular) but becomes two-chambered due to the formation of the false septum. The ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on the peripheral part. It is basically found in mustard and argemone.

273044.explanation: Cabbage is the largest edible bud. ln cabbage plant, the stem is so short that the great mass of thick overlapping leaves tends to forms head. The older leaves surround the younger smaller, more tender leaves and the cabbage resembles a huge bud. In cauliflower, a short erect stem is produced with an undeveloped inflorescence. The whole inflorescence forms a large head of abortive flowers on thick hypertrophied branches. The onion bulb consists of edible fleshy leaf bases. In Agave, bulbils are modified floral buds that develop on the flowering axis.

273045.explanation: The insectivorous habit develops in the plants due to the deficiency of nitrogen because these plants grow in nitrogen-deficient soil usually in swamps. Some of the common examples of insectivorous plants are Nepenthes (pitcher plants), Utricularia (bladderwort), Drosera (Sundew), Dionaea (Venus Flytrap). Sundew plant is Drosera rotundifolla. Its leaf surface is always sticky due to the secretory activity of smaller glands on the end of tentacles, which release proteolytic enzymes.

273046.explanation: Long root systems reach the water level so that they can have access to the ground level water. And many of the plants have made different techniques to tackle with transpiration and lack of water.

273048.explanation: Cauliflower is one of several vegetables in the species Brassica oleracea in the genus Brassica, which is in the family Brassicaceae. It is an annual plant that reproduces by seed. Typically, only the head is eaten – the edible white flesh sometimes called "curd" (with a similar appearance to cheese curd). The cauliflower head is composed of a white inflorescence meristem.

273050.explanation: Fasciculated roots are adventitious roots occuring in clusters and all of them are swollen.They are mostly found in asparagus and dahlia.These are usually the modifications of adventitious roots.

273054.explanation: Husk fiber coir of commerce comes from Mesocarp part of the coconut (Cocos nuciefera).

273056.explanation: Fruits in general develop from the ovary and they are called "true fruits", but in some species the thalamus contributes to the formation of fruits. Apple is an example of such a fruit which develops from thalamus and thus it is correctly called false fruit or pseudocarp. It develops from inferior ovary.

273063.explanation:
Bulliform cells are large, bubble-shaped epidermal cells that occur in groups on the upper surface of the leaves of many monocots. These cells are present on the adaxial or the upper surface of the leaf. They are generally present near the midvein. These cells are large, empty, and colourless.

They are thought to play a role in the unfolding of developing leaves and in the rolling and unrolling of mature leaves in response to alternating wet and dry periods.

273065.explanation: More than a quarter of the primary productivity on land, and a large fraction of the food that humans consume, is contributed by plants that fix atmospheric CO2 by C(4) photosynthesis. It has been estimated that transferring the C(4) pathway to C(3) crops could boost yield by 50% and also increase water use efficiency and reduce the need for fertilizer, particularly in dry, hot environments. The high productivity of maize (Zea mays), sugarcane (Saccharum spp.) and several emerging bioenergy grasses is due largely to C(4) photosynthesis, which is enabled by the orderly arrangement, in concentric rings, of specialized bundle sheath and mesophyll cells in leaves in a pattern known as Kranz anatomy.

273068.explanation: In plant anatomy, the Casparian strip is a band of cell wall material deposited in the radial and transverse walls of the endodermis, and is chemically different from the rest of the cell wall - the cell wall being made of lignin and without suberin - whereas the Casparian strip is made of suberin and sometimes lignin.

273083.explanation: Adjacent cells in a plant tissue are held together by a thin, sticky, amorphous layer of cementing material. This layer is called the middle lamella. Middle lamella is cheifly made up of calcium and magnesium pectate. In ripeniong fruits the pectate compounds solubilize to a jelly like material, making the fruits soft. The cell wall and middle lamella may be ntransversed by plasmodesmata which connect the cytoplasm of neighbouring plant cells.

273084.explanation:
Electron microscopic studies of eukaryotic cells reveal the presence of a network of the reticulum of tiny tubular structures scattered in the cytoplasm that is called the endoplasmic reticulum. It is composed of cisternae, tubules, and vesicles. The endoplasmic reticulum divides the cytoplasm into two distinct compartments:- luminal and extra luminal compartments.

On the basis of the presence and absence of ribosomes, they are classified into rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum respectively.

273085.explanation: Peroxisomes are microbodies which contain enzymes for peroxide biosynthesis.

273086.explanation: Cystolith is a botanical term for outgrowths of the epidermal cell wall, usually of calcium carbonate, formed in a cellulose matrix in special cells called lithocysts, generally in the leaf of plants. Cystoliths are present in certain families, including in many genera of Acanthaceae.

273087.explanation: In plant cells the vacuoles can occupy upto 90 percent of the volume of the cell. They are bounded by a single semipermeable membrane called tonoplast. This membrane facilitates the transport of a number of ions and other materials against concentration gradients into the vacuole.

273089.explanation: It forms the living component in the dead wall. A number of plasmodesmata or cytoplasmic strands are present in pit through which the cytoplasma of one cell is in contact with other. These are lined by plasma membrane and contains a fine tubule called desmotubule. Endoplasmic reticulum plays a role in origin of plasmodesmata. These form the symplastic system between two cells.

273091.explanation: The cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells have organelles such a mitochondria, chloroplasts, Golgi bodies, lysosomes, peroxisomes etc. out of these mitochondria and chloroplasts contain DNA.Genes are found on the chromosomes and chromosomes are made up of DNA and associated proteins. Thus, mitochondria and chloroplasts also contain genes.During fertilization male gametes do not have sufficient, so most of the cytoplasm, hence, organelles, so most of the cytoplasm to the offsprings is contributed by egg itself. Hence, organelles that are present in egg's cytoplasm, also inhibit to the offprings.

273092.explanation: Ability to multiply by a fission-like process and they are the three main types of plastids classified depending upon their colour and the pigments they contain.

273093.explanation: Lysosomes are simple tiny spherical sac-like structures evenly distributed in the cytoplasm. These are formed by the process of packaging in golgi apparatus. They are bounded by a single membrane. They are rich in hydrolytic enzymes such as lipases, proteases, and carbohydrases.

Under such conditions, RuBisco the enzyme that catalyses the carboxylation of RuBP during the first step of the Calvin cycle functions as an oxygenase. Some oxygen does bind to RuBisCo and hence carbon dioxide fixation is decreased. The RuBP binds with oxygen to form one molecule of PGA (3C compound) and phosphoglycolate (2C compound) in the pathway of photorespiration. There is neither the synthesis of sugar nor of ATP.

273151.explanation:
ATP also referred to as adenosine triphosphate. it contains high energy bonds located between each phosphate group. these bonds are also referred to as phosphoric anhydride bonds.

There are three reasons these bonds are high energy:



 The electrostatic repulsion of the positively charged phosphates and negatively charged oxygen stabilizes the products (ADP + Pi) of breaking these bonds.
 The stabilization of products by ionization and resonance. As the bonds are broken there is increased stability due to the resonance of that product's structure.
 The entropy increases. There is greater stability in the products because there exists a greater entropy; i.e. more randomness. 1 mole of reactants has higher energy than 2 moles of products. The disorder is favored over order according to the 2nd law of thermodynamics.

273152.explanation:
The complete oxidation of food with the use of oxygen and when entire carbon released as CO2 is called as the aerobic respiration.

In a single cycle of aerobic respiration:

C6H12O6 + 6CO2 + 6H2O = 6CO2 + 12H2O + 38 kcal

So, according to the given cycle, we can infer that:

CO2 =6*44 g=264 gm.

H2O=12*18 gm=216 gm

264 gm of CO2 and 216 gm of H2O are formed respectively.

273153.explanation:
Glycolysis is also called the EMP pathway (Embden Meyerhof and Parnas).

It is the process of breakdown of glucose or similar hexose sugar to two molecules of pyruvic acid through a series of enzyme-mediated reactions releasing energy as ATP and reducing power as NADH2.

In this process, one glucose produces 2 molecules of pyruvic acid and substrate-level phosphorylation forms 4 ATP.

In this, the net gain is 2 ATP (without involving ETS) and there is neither consumption of oxygen nor liberation of CO2 takes place.

36 ATP molecules totally produced in aerobic respiration through glycerophosphate shuttle and it usually functions primarily in the brain and skeletal muscles.

It results in the production of 2 moles of ATP per mole of NADH2. The NADH2 results in the formation of FADH2 and thus gives rise to 2 ATP molecules.

Two NADH2 molecules produced in the cytoplasm during glycolysis gives rise to 4 ATP molecules.

Thus, the total number of ATP produced during the complete oxidation of glucose molecules formed is 36 instead of 38.

This explains that there is a loss of one ATP for each cytosolic NADH + H+.

273291.explanation: Adenosine triphosphate is the physical embodiment of cellular energy. It is created during cellular respiration. It is used by the body for a vast array of different purposes. It provides energy to cells and transports other materials throughout the body. Proper ATP production will have an effect on every aspect of all of the body's processes. Glycolysis is the process where food is metabolized into cellular energy. ATP is created during glycolysis. The electron transport chain also contributes to the creation of ATP. This allows energy from sunlight and the oxidization of sugars to be used as a type of cellular fuel. ATP is fuel for cells. It is consumed by a variety of different processes. Once it is spent, it reverts back to adenosine diphosphate and adenosine monophosphate. These are the components that originally makeup ATP. Your body actually consumes its entire weight in ATP every day. Living organisms constantly recycle this material for use by other cells. ATP energy is the fuel for life. It is the very material that carries out the action of all living cells. When you consider how much of it is used by all living things, it is truly one of the most vital energy sources in the world.

282421.explanation: The cerebellum is the part of the hindbrain which has both white and grey matter. Arborvitae is the white matter present in the cerebellum having a tree-shaped structure and helps in the conduction of sensory and motor impulse to the cerebellum.

282424.explanation: The medulla oblongata is a part of hindbrain that controls autonomic functions such as breathing, digestion, swallowing and sneezing. Hence, it is medulla oblongata of frog which helps it to respire and locomote.

282425.explanation: A person having Parkinson’s disease shows defective action of dopamine neurotransmitter in brain which is responsible for relaying messages that plan and control body movement.

282428.explanation: The ganglia of sympathetic and the central nervous system in frog develop from the neural crest cells which gives rise to central nervous system and peripheral nervous system.

282435.explanation: Trochlear is the IVth cranial nerve that regulates the eye movement. Trigeminal is the Vth cranial nerve that carries the somatosensory information from the face and head to the brain and regulates the chewing muscle movement. Glossopharyngeal is IX cranial nerve that carries somatosensory information from tongue, pharynx, tonsils to the brain and regulates the muscles used in swallowing. Hence, trochlear, trigeminal and glossopharyngeal nerve are IV, V and IX cranial nerves.

282436.explanation: The brain disease caused due to accumulation of amyloid β-peptide is called Alzheimer’s disease.

282437.explanation: The part of the brain responsible for processing emotions is the limbic system, also called the emotional brain.

282447.explanation: Diabetes insipidus occurs due to the hyposecretion of antidiuretic hormone (ADH), also known as arginine vasopressin which is synthesized in the hypothalamus and is transported as neurosecretory vesicles to the posterior pituitary.

282448.explanation: Cholesterol possesses a complex basic structure as it is the precursor of steroid hormones. Hence, steroid hormones are almost similar in structure to cholesterol.

282449.explanation: The axons of neurosecretory neurons synthesize oxytocin and vasopressin which are secreted from the posterior lobe of the pituitary gland. Hence, posterior pituitary secretions are obtained from the neuro-secretory axons of nerves.

282450.explanation: Addison's disease is caused due to hyposecretion of steroid hormones, cortisol, and aldosterone, which are secreted from the adrenal cortex of the adrenal glands.

282451.explanation: Alloxan is a toxic glucose analog, which destroys insulin-producing β-cells of islets of Langerhans in the pancreas.

282452.explanation: Thyroid gland produces thyroxine which plays a very important role in the metamorphosis of frog.

282453.explanation: Conn's syndrome occurs by the over-secretion of aldosterone by adrenal glands.

282454.explanation: Adrenaline is the stress hormone released by the adrenal gland which is responsible for an increase in the pulse rate and blood pressure during an emergency. Hence, when the person sees a tiger, adrenaline is released in the body due to fear and stress.

282455.explanation: A person suffering from hyperthyroidism has bulging or protruding eyes, tachycardia, and higher body temperature. This condition is known as thyrotoxicosis.

282456.explanation: Thyroxine hormone produced by the thyroid gland plays a very important role in the metamorphosis of the frog. Hence, tadpoles can be made to grow in size by inhibiting the thyroxine hormone.

282457.explanation: Sella turcica is a saddle-shaped depression in the body of the sphenoid bone of the human skull.

282458.explanation: The source of somatostatin growth-inhibiting hormone is the same as insulin and glucagon as insulin, glucagon, and somatostatin are secreted by beta, alpha, and delta cells of the pancreas.

282459.explanation: The thymus is a specialized organ of the immune system which is active in young ones but gradually disappears after sexual maturity. Hence, thymus starts undergoing atrophy after puberty.

282460.explanation: Thyroxine hormone secreted by the thyroid gland is required for metamorphosis in amphibians. So, in the presence of antithyroid substances like thiourea, tadpoles remain in the larval stage indefinitely and can grow as giant-sized tadpoles.

282461.explanation: The adrenal medulla secretes hormones collectively called catecholamine which increases alertness, heartbeat, the strength of heart contraction, pupillary dilation, etc.

282462.explanation: When blood calcium levels drop, the parathyroid gland secretes a parathyroid hormone which helps to raise blood calcium levels. Hence, the parathyroid gland is malfunctioning in a child whose plasma calcium level is found below the optimum level.

282463.explanation: Thymus is the primary specialized lymphoid organ of the immune system that gradually reduces with age through a process called involution.

282558.explanation: Floridean starch is a type of a storage glucan found in glycophytes and in red algae (also known as rhodophytes), in which it is usually the primary sink for fixed carbon from photosynthesis. It is found in grains or granules in the cell's cytoplasm and is composed of an α-linked glucose polymer with a degree of branching intermediate between amylopectin and glycogen, though more similar to the former. The polymers that make up floridean starch are sometimes referred to as "semi-amylopectin".

282559.explanation: Red algae or Rhodophyta are one of the oldest groups of eukaryotic cells. The red algae form a distinct group characterized by having eukaryotic cells without flagella and centrioles, chloroplasts that lack external endoplasmic reticulum, and contain unstacked (stroma) thylakoid and use phycobiliproteins as accessory pigments, which give them their red color. Red algae store sugars as floridean starch, which is a type of starch that consists of highly branched amylopectin without amylose as food reserves outside their plastids. Most red algae are also multicellular, macroscopic, marine, and reproduce sexually. Polysiphonia, Porphyra, Gracilaria, and Gelidium are some typical examples of red algae.

282562.explanation: In spirogyra, all cells are capable of forming gametes that are similar in morphology. Gametes of indistinguishable morphology are known as isogametes, hence gametes in spirogyra are isogametes.

282565.explanation: The red algae usually reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation. They reproduce asexually by non-motile spores and sexually by non-motile gametes. Sexual reproduction is oogamous and accompanied by complex post-fertilization developments.

282570.explanation: The scientific name of the tiger is Panthera tigris where Panthera is the genus name and tigris is the species name. Hence, the correct animal name matched with its particular taxonomic category is Tiger - Tigris, the species.

282572.explanation: Plasmodium falciparum is a unicellular protozoan parasite which is the deadliest species of Plasmodium that causes the most dangerous form of malaria, falciparum malaria in humans. This parasite is transmitted through the bite of a female Anopheles mosquito in humans.

282580.explanation: The dikaryon is a nuclear feature that is unique to some fungi. Compatible cell-types can fuse cytoplasms (plasmogamy). When this occurs, the two nuclei of two cells pair off and cohabit without fusing (karyogamy). This can be maintained for all the cells of the hyphae by synchronously dividing so that pairs are passed to newer cells. In the Ascomycota (ascomycetes) this attribute is most often found in the ascogenous hyphae and ascocarp while the bulk of the mycelia remains monokaryotic. In the Basidiomycota (basidiomycetes) this is the dominant phase with most Basidiomycota monokaryons weakly growing and short-lived.

282581.explanation: Aspergillus belongs to the class ascomycetes of fungi and in ascomycetes mycelium is branched and septate. Asexual spores are conidia and sexual spores are ascospores.

282582.explanation: The Agaricus belongs to the division Basidiomycetes (Basidiomycota). In basidiomycetes the sex organs are absent, but plasmogamy is brought about by fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains or genotypes. The resultant structure is dikaryotic which ultimately gives rise to basidium. Karyogamy and meiosis take place in the basidium producing four basidiospores. The basidiospores are exogenously produced on the basidium. The basidia are arranged in fruiting bodies called basidiocarps.

282583.explanation: Deutromycetes are commonly known as imperfect fungi because only the asexual or vegetative phases of these fungi are known. When the sexual forms of these fungi were discovered they were moved into classes they rightly belong to. It is also possible that the asexual and vegetative stage have been given one name (and placed under Deuteromycetes) and the sexual stage another (and placed under another class). Later when the linkages were established, the fungi were correctly identified and moved out of Deuteromycetes.

282584.explanation: Agaricus, Ustilago, and Puccinia belong to basidiomycetes as they all have branched and septate mycelium. They vegetatively reproduce by fragmentation and possess basidiospores as their sexual spores.

282585.explanation: Mucor and Rhizopus belongs to Phycomycetes because they have aseptate and coenocytic mycelium. Sexual reproduction occurs by fusion of two gamates to form zygospore.

282586.explanation: Saprophytes are the organisms that absorb soluble organic matter from dead and decaying organisms (substrates). Hence, we can say that fungi are saprophytic in nature.

282587.explanation: Aspergillus have fruiting bodies named ascocarps. These ascocarps contain asci inside which the formation of ascospores (sexual spores found in ascomycetes) takes place. Hence it belongs to ascomycetes.

282594.explanation: Lichens are symbiotic associations i.e. mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi. The algal component is known as phycobiont and the fungal component as mycobiont, which is autotrophic and heterotrophic, respectively. Algae prepare food for fungi and fungi provide shelter and absorb mineral nutrients and water for its partner.

282595.explanation: Fungi are also known to form symbiotic associations with plants (mycorrhiza). Many members of the genus Glomus form mycorrhiza. The fungal symbiont in these associations absorbs phosphorus from soil and passes it to the plant. Plants having such associations show other benefits also, such as resistance to root-borne pathogens, tolerance to salinity and drought, and an overall increase in plant growth and development.

282598.explanation: The name virus that means venom or poisonous fluid was given by Dmitri Ivanowsky (1892) recognized certain microbes as a causal organism of the mosaic disease of tobacco. These were found to be smaller than bacteria because they passed through bacteria-proof filters. M.W. Beijerinek (1898) demonstrated that the extract of the infected plants of tobacco could cause infection in healthy plants and called the fluid as Contagium vivum fluidum (infectious living fluid). W.M. Stanley (1935) showed that viruses could be crystallized and crystals consist largely of proteins. They are inert outside their specific host cell. Viruses are obligate parasites.
