435272.explanation: The symptoms of dengue fever include muscle aches, joint pains, vomiting, high fever, intense and prolonged headaches. However, the most common symptom observed in people infected with dengue fever is the decrease in platelets count.

435278.explanation: In a normal adult, the volume of blood pumped out by the Rt (Right) and Lt (Left) ventricles is the same, otherwise, the blood is bound to ‘back up’ somewhere and thus create problems.

435282.explanation: Neural signals through the sympathetic nerves (part of ANS) can increase the rate of heart beat, the strength of ventricular contraction and thereby the cardiac output.

435288.explanation: Platelets can release a variety of substances most of which are involved in the coagulation or clotting of blood. Certain factors released by the tissues at the site of injury also can initiate coagulation. Calcium ions play a very important role in clotting.

435348.explanation: RBCs are formed in the red bone marrow in adults. They are devoid of the nucleus in most of the mammals and are biconcave in shape.

435362.explanation:
The cardiac impulse is the cardiac cycle which is repeated diastole or systole of the heart. It starts from the sinoatrial node to the atrioventricular node along the bundle of atrioventricular to the Purkinje fibres which generate a heartbeat.

The correct sequence of conduction of impulse is:

A node $\rightarrow$ AV node $\rightarrow$ AV bundle $\rightarrow$ Purkinje fiber

435379.explanation: During each cardiac cycle two prominent sounds are produced which can be easily heard through a stethoscope. The first heart sound (lub) is associated with the closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves whereas the second heart sound (dub) is associated with the closure of the semilunar valves. These sounds are of clinical diagnostic significance.

435387.explanation: The QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles, which initiates the ventricular contraction. The contraction starts shortly after Q and marks the beginning of the systole.

435400.explanation:
Atria receives blood from all parts of the body which flows to the ventricles. Action potential generated at the sinoatrial node passes from the atria to the ventricles. Both these events take place at the same time.

Thus, actions mentioned in Statements 1 and 2 are synchronous.'

435402.explanation: A myocardial infarction (MI), also known as a heart attack, occurs when blood flow decreases or stops to a part of the heart, causing damage to the heart muscle.

435404.explanation: The sinus venosus, the cardiac chamber upstream of the (right) atrium, is a severely underinvestigated structure. In ectothermic vertebrates, i.e., fishes, amphibians, and reptiles, the sinus venosus aids atrial filling by contracting prior to the atrium (atria). This is facilitated by the sinuatrial delay of approximately the same duration as the atrioventricular delay, which facilitates atrial filling of the ventricles.

435406.explanation: Pulse pressure is the difference between systolic and diastolic blood pressure. It is measured in millimeters of mercury. It represents the force that the heart generates each time it contracts.

435408.explanation: The bicuspid valve is present on the left side of the heart and allows the blood to flow from the left atrium into the left ventricle.

435412.explanation: In a healthy heart with a typical rate of 70 to 75 beats per minute, each cardiac cycle, or heartbeat, takes about 0.8 seconds to complete the cycle.

435414.explanation: Lymph contains a variety of substances, including proteins, salts, glucose, fats, water, and white blood cells. It does not normally contain any red blood cells and certain proteins.

435416.explanation: Joint diastole refers to phase in cardiac cycle of heart when both atria and ventricles are relaxed. During joint diastole blood is poured into left and right atria. This phase takes only 0.4 seconds and is also called as blood receiving period of heart.

435418.explanation: Pulmonary artery originates from the right ventricle of the four-chambered heart and transport blood to the lungs.

435420.explanation: The first heart sound (lub) is associated with the closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves whereas the second heart sound (dub) is associated with the closure of the semilunar valves.

435422.explanation: Heartbeat in arthropods and annelids is neurogenic. In this, the heart beat is initiated by a nerve impulse coming from a nerve ganglion situated near the heart. The myogenic heart is a characteristic feature of molluscs and vertebrates.

435425.explanation: A heart murmur is a blowing, whooshing, or rasping sound heard during a heartbeat. The heart sound murmurs is heard during leakage of blood through valves.

435427.explanation: The phrenic arteries are small vessels that may have various sites of origin. They deliver blood to the diaphragm.

435429.explanation: The P wave of ECG occurs before the beginning of atrial contraction. Atrial contraction is represented by the P-wave of the electrocardiogram which is characterized by electrical depolarization of the atria.

435431.explanation: The brachiocephalic artery or brachiocephalic trunk is referred to as the innominate artery. It is one of the three great vessels of the aortic arch that supplies blood to the head, neck and upper extremities.

435480.explanation: The spleen acts as a filter for the blood in case of infections and immunity.

435482.explanation: The purpose of the myelin sheath is to allow electrical impulses to transmit quickly and efficiently along with the nerve cells. Nerve impulses cannot pass through the myelination, so they jump from one node of Ranvier to the next. If the whole nerve becomes myelinated then the conduction will be stopped.

435484.explanation: Labeo is a fish having two chambered heart with one auricle and one ventricle. Hence, two atria are lacking in the heart of labeo.

Trachea is supported by incomplete cartilaginous rings which prevent its collapse during inspiration and abdominal cavities. It is the principal muscle of respiration.

435873.explanation: C - Vena Cava - takes blood from body parts to right auricle, $P_{CO_2}$ = 45 mm Hg

435874.explanation:
When the muscles of all the four chambers are relaxed, the pulmonary vein brings the oxygenated blood from the lungs in the left atrium of the heart. When the right ventricle contracts, the deoxygenated blood enters the lungs through the pulmonary artery and releases carbon dioxide, and absorbs fresh oxygen from the air. The deoxygenated blood enters main vein called vena cava which carried it to the right atrium of the heart. A patch of nodal tissue is present in the right upper corner of the right atrium called the sino-atrial node (SAN). Another mass of this tissue is seen in the lower left corner of the right atrium close to the atrio-ventricular septum called the atrio-ventricular node (AVN).

Hence, the correct labels in the heart are: 1. Pulmonary veins, 2. pulmonary artery, 3. vena cava, 4. SA node, 5. AV node.

435875.explanation:
When the muscles of all the four chambers are relaxed, the pulmonary vein brings the oxygenated blood from the lungs in the left atrium of the heart. 

When the left ventricle contracts, the oxygenated blood enters the main artery called aorta from which it goes to the different body organs through small branches called arterioles and capillaries.

When the right ventricle contracts, the deoxygenated blood enters the lungs through the pulmonary artery and releases carbon dioxide, and absorbs fresh oxygen from the air.

The deoxygenated blood enters the main vein called the vena cava which carried it to the right atrium of the heart.

Hence, the correct label is: 1. Pulmonary vein, 2. dorsal aorta, 3. pulmonary artery, 4. vena cava

435876.explanation: The label 4 in the given image represents vena cava. The vena cava is responsible for carrying the deoxygenated blood from the lower and middle parts of the body to the right atrium. The partial pressure of carbon dioxide in vena cava or veins is equal to 45 mm Hg.

435877.explanation: The QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles, which initiates the ventricular contraction. The contraction starts shortly after Q and marks the beginning of the systole. Hence, the QRS complex represents the constriction of both the ventricles.

435881.explanation: In fishes, the heart pumps out deoxygenated blood, which is oxygenated by the gills and is then supplied to the body parts. Hence, it has a single circulation. As the heart pumps deoxygenated blood in fishes, it is called a venous heart.

435886.explanation: Rh- is a recessive trait, that is, someone who is Rh+ might have a hidden Rh- in their DNA. If that person and his or her partner both pass an Rh- down to a child, that child will be Rh-. Even though at least one parent is Rh+.

The speed at which an impulse travels depends on whether the nerve fibre is myelinated or

unmyelinated and also on the diameter of the fibre. In unmyelinated fibres the impulse travels steadily

along the fibre. Depending on the diameter of the fibre, impulses can travel at speeds from 18 m/sec up to 140 m/sec.

435892.explanation: Cardiac muscles are found exclusively in the heart. They are cylindrical, non-tapering, branched with faint striations. They have one or two nuclei in each cell. They are involuntary. Their function is rhythmic contraction and relaxation throughout life.

435893.explanation: RBC count increases in people living at high altitudes because there is a decrease in atmospheric pressure so to carry more amount of oxygen to the cells, more red blood cells are required.

435894.explanation: The spleen is made of red pulp and white pulp, separated by the marginal zone. White pulp mainly contains lymphocytes such as T cells whereas red pulp is made up of several different types of blood cells, including platelets, granulocytes, red blood cells, and plasma.

435895.explanation: The formation of RBC in the bone marrow is called erythropoiesis. In the early fetus, erythropoiesis takes place in the mesodermal cells of the yolk sac.

435896.explanation: Low levels of carbon dioxide in the blood cause low levels of hydrogen ions in the brain, leading to a decrease in the rate and depth of pulmonary ventilation. Alcohol causes a temporary increase in the heart rate and blood pressure. Adrenaline makes the heart beat faster, increases blood flow to the brain and muscles.

435897.explanation: The ductus arteriosus is also called the ductus Botalli. It is a blood vessel in the developing fetus that connects the trunk of the pulmonary artery to the proximal descending aorta. It allows most of the blood from the right ventricle to bypass the fetus's fluid-filled non-functioning lungs.

435898.explanation: In a portal system, blood circulates through a second capillary bed, before returning to the heart. Thus, a portal system is a kind of detour in the pathway of venous return that can transport materials directly from one organ to another. The largest portal system in the body is the hepatic portal system, which carries blood from the abdominal organs to the liver.

435899.explanation: The connection between pulmonary and aortic arches in foetus is the ductus arteriosus. It is a normal blood vessel that connects two major arteries, the aorta and the pulmonary artery that carry blood away from the heart.

435906.explanation: The electrical potential difference across the resting plasma membrane is called as the resting potential. It is negatively charged due to the differential distribution of Na+ and K+ ions.

435922.explanation: In human beings, there are 12 pairs of cranial nerves, each named for their function or structure.

435925.explanation: Cranial nerves III (CNIII) (oculomotor), IV (trochlear), and VI (abducens) control the position of the eyeballs.

435939.explanation: The fourth ventricle lies posterior or dorsal to the pons and medulla and the anterior or ventral to the cerebellum.

435942.explanation: The diencephalon is the region of the embryonic vertebrate neural tube that gives rise to anterior forebrain structures including the thalamus, hypothalamus, posterior portion of the pituitary gland, and the pineal gland. It encloses a cavity called the third ventricle.

435945.explanation: The Vagus nerve conducts the parasympathetic motor impulses which slow down the heartbeat rate by the effect of acetylcholine, a neurotransmitter released by the parasympathetic nervous system.

435949.explanation: Nodes of Ranvier are microscopic gaps found within myelinated axons.

435957.explanation: Vagus is the 10th cranial nerve that runs from the brain through the face and thorax to the abdomen.

436322.explanation: Parkinson's disease is a degenerative disorder of the central nervous system. The motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease result from the death of dopamine-generating cells in the substantia nigra, a region of the midbrain. Parkinson's disease results in loss of dopaminergic innervation to the striatum. Dopamine is a neurotransmitter responsible for transmitting signals between the substantia nigra and multiple brain regions. The connection between the substantia nigra and the corpus striatum is critical to producing smooth, purposeful movement. Loss of dopamine in this circuit results in abnormal nerve-firing patterns within the brain that cause impaired movement.

436331.explanation: Broca's area is located in a region called the inferior frontal gyrus, found in the frontal lobe.

436400.explanation: Crossing over is a concept of genetics that is often called recombination. It occurs during meiosis. Crossing over is the exchange of chromosomal segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during the production of gametes".

436402.explanation: Spindle fibres are the cytoskeletal structure of eukaryotic cells, that are formed during cell division. It contracts and expands to separate sister chromatids between daughter cells. It is made up of microtubules, which are composed of 97% tubulin protein, and 3% RNA. The polymeric tubulin is formed by alpha and beta loop. In cilia, the microtubules are arranged in the 9+2 arrangement.

436404.explanation: Second growth stage or G2​ stage is the third subphase of interphase that occurs after the synthesis or S phase in which DNA replication occurs. Hence, the number of DNA molecules in each chromosome at G2​ stage will be two.

436406.explanation: Cell division is fundamental to all living organisms and required for growth and development. As an essential means of reproduction for all living things, cell division allows organisms to transfer their genetic material to their offspring.

436408.explanation: Human cells divide once in approximately 24 hours. Cell cycle in yeast completed in about 90 minutes.

436410.explanation: Human cell, cell division proper lasts for about 24 hour.

436412.explanation: Chromatids maybe sister or non-sister chromatids. A sister chromatid is either one of the two chromatids of the same chromosome joined together by a common centromere. A pair of sister chromatids is called a dyad. Once sister chromatids have separated they are again called daughter chromosomes, each having the same genetic mass as one of the individual chromatids that made up its parent.

436414.explanation: Interphase divided into G1, G2 and S-phase, During G1-phase the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA. During S or synthesis phase DNA synthesis or replication takes place. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C then it increases to 4C.

436418.explanation: In animals, mitotic cell division is only seen in the diploid somatic cells whereas plant shows the mitotic division in both haploid and diploid cells.

436419.explanation: In prometaphase, kinetochores appear at the centromeres and mitotic spindle microtubules attach to kinetochores. In metaphase, chromosomes are lined up and each sister chromatid is attached to a spindle fiber. In anaphase, sister chromatids (now called chromosomes) are pulled toward opposite poles.

436421.explanation: Mitosis usually results in the production of diploid daughter cells with non-identical genetic complement. Mitosis creates two identical daughter cells that each contain the same number of chromosomes as their parent cell. In contrast, meiosis gives rise to four unique daughter cells, each of which has half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell.

436423.explanation: In meiosis only one cycle of DNA replication occurs.

436424.explanation: Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between two non-sister chromatids of homologous chromatids. Recombination between homologous chromosomes is completed by the end of the pachytene.

So if you have two Chromosome 1s lined up, one strand of one Chromosome 1 will break and it will reanneal with a similar breakage on the other Chromosome 1.

436433.explanation: Meiosis is a type of cell division that reduces the number of chromosomes in the parent cell by half and produces four gamete cells. The process results in four daughter cells that are haploid, which means they contain half the number of chromosomes of the diploid parent cell.

436434.explanation: The genetic constitution of gametes is finally decided in anaphase 1 because the separation of chromosomes takes place and 2n from the parent becomes n in daughter cells in this stage.

436436.explanation: During anaphase I, from each tetrad, two chromatids of a chromosome move as a unit (dyad) to one pole of a spindle, and the remaining two chromatids of its homologous migrate to the opposite pole. Thus, the homologous chromosomes of each pair, rather than the chromatids of a chromosome, are separated. As a result, half of the chromosomes, which appear in the early prophase, go to each pole.

436438.explanation: During the prophase of meiosis, I, homologous chromosomes pair and form synapses. The paired chromosomes are called bivalents. The bivalent has two chromosomes and four chromatids, with one chromosome coming from each parent.

436441.explanation: Meiosis is a specialized type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, creating four haploid cells. In meiosis, DNA replication is followed by two rounds of cell division to produce four daughter cells, each with half the number of chromosomes as the original parent cell. The two meiotic divisions are known as Meiosis I and Meiosis II.

436442.explanation: G1 is the first of four phases of the cell cycle to the interphase of cell cycle which is a metabolically active stage. During G1 ​ synthesis of ATP nucleotides, amino acids, RNAs and protein synthesis occur and growth of the nucleus is observed. DNA replicates in S- phase of the cell cycle.

436443.explanation: Metaphase is a stage in the cell cycle where all the genetic material is condensing into chromosomes. These chromosomes then become visible. It is the stage in which the nuclear envelope disappears completely so that the nucleoplasm comes in contact with the cytoplasm. Chromosomes are arranged at the equator and form a sort of metaphase plate.

436444.explanation: Microsporogenesis is the process of the formation of haploid microspores from diploid microspore mother cells inside the pollen sac by meiotic division. Megasporogenesis is the process of formation of megaspores from megaspore mother cell (MMC) by meiotic division.

436445.explanation: During the Late prophase, the chromosomes condense, the nucleolus disappears, and the nuclear envelope breaks down.

436446.explanation: The best cell division stage to observe the shape, size and a number of chromosomes is the metaphase. The chromosomes appear shortest and thickest during this phase and are arranged at the equator and form an apparent plate called as equatorial or metaphase plate thus readily visible.

436447.explanation: The cell cycle is an ordered series of events involving cell growth and cell division that produces two new daughter cells.

436448.explanation: Mitosis begins with prophase, during which chromosomes recruit condensin and begin to undergo a condensation process that will continue until metaphase.

436449.explanation: The G0 phase or resting phase is a period in the cell cycle in which cells exist in a quiescent state. Arrest of cell cycle and onset of differentiation.

436450.explanation: During meiosis, one cell divides twice to form four daughter cells. These four daughter cells only have half the number of chromosomes of the parent cell – they are haploid.

436451.explanation: The chromosome in which the centromere is located close to one of the terminal ends is known as an acrocentric chromosome. In this, one arm is extremely long and the other is extremely short. During anaphase, they appear J-shaped.

436452.explanation: In metaphase, chromosomes consisting of two sister chromatids get arranged at the equator. Discontinuous fibres radiate out from two spindle poles and get connected to the disc-shaped structure at the surface of the centromere called kinetochores. These are known as chromosome fibres or tractile fibrils.

436453.explanation: Genes do not occur in pairs in gametes. Gametes are haploid in nature as they undergo meiosis and reduces ploidy levels into half. Male and female gametes which are haploid in nature fuse to form a zygote and thus, the zygote is diploid in nature.

436454.explanation: During the cell cycle, RNA and protein synthesis takes place during G1 and G2 phases. The cell cycle is an ordered set of events, culminating in cell growth and division into two daughter cells. Non-dividing cells not considered to be in the cell cycle. The stages are G1 and G2 - phase.

436455.explanation: Colchicine is an important mutagen that works by preventing the formation of the microtubules and doubles the number of chromosomes. It is commonly used to develop polyploid plants and functions as a mitotic poison by producing many mutagenic effects on plants.

436456.explanation: The first step of chromatin structure duplication is the synthesis of histone proteins: H1, H2A, H2B, H3, H4. These proteins are synthesized during the S phase of the cell cycle.

436457.explanation: S phase is about 8 hours and anaphase only take about 0.8 percent of the cell cycle to complete, which is the shortest time required out of all the phases.

436458.explanation: The egg is haploid and has 5 pg (picogram) DNA. Its animal which is diploid will be having 10 pg DNA. In S phase DNA doubles and therefore, in G2 amount of DNA will be 20 pg.

436459.explanation: Amitosis (a- + mitosis), also called 'karyostenosis' or direct cell division or binary fission. It is cell proliferation that does not occur by mitosis, the mechanism usually identified as essential for cell division in eukaryotes

436461.explanation: A chromomere is one of the serially aligned beads or granules of a eukaryotic chromosome, resulting from local coiling of a continuous DNA thread. It is visible on a chromosome during the prophase of meiosis and mitosis.

436463.explanation: S phase is the synthesis phase in which the DNA gets replicated. It is the longest and active phase of the cell cycle and it takes nearly 80 minutes of the whole 150 minutes cell cycle process.

436466.explanation: Zygotene is the sub-stage where synapsis between homologous chromosomes begins. It is also known as zygonema. The synaptonemal complex facilitates synapsis by holding the aligned chromosomes together. After the homologous pairs synapse, they are either called tetrads or bivalents.

436468.explanation: During the zygotene and pachytene stages of prophase I of meiosis, there is pairing or synapsis between homologous chromosomes. In this pairing, similar parts of the chromosomes remain side by side by the mutual attraction between allelic genes i.e., at the two-strand stage. Further, in the diplotene stage of prophase I of meiosis, each chromosome splits longitudinally into two chromatids. Now bivalent is composed of four chromatids. This stage is known as the four-strand stage or tetrad. Crossing over is detected at the four-strand stage.

436470.explanation: Cancer: mitosis takes place in a single cell, can replicate itself to make new cells. These are cancer cells. They continue to replicate rapidly without the control systems that normal cells have.

436472.explanation: The site of meiosis in higher plants is the spore mother cell. These spores multiply by mitosis, developing into the haploid gametophyte generation, which then gives rise to gametes directly.

436474.explanation: During the pachytene stage, there is the formation of recombination nodules between homologous chromosomes, each pair is called bivalent. Each homologous of a pair is actually composed of two sister chromatids and the pair is a tetrad of chromatids, i.e., four-stranded.

436476.explanation: The DNA replicates in the S-phase of interphase in both types of cell division. The replicated DNA is arranged as sister chromatids on the same chromosomes. In the metaphase in both meiosis as well as mitosis, there are two chromatids in the chromosome.

436478.explanation:
The chromosome can be counted best at the stage of metaphase in any species and to establish a detailed study of the morphology of the chromosomes as the chromosomes are aligned in the middle of the cell.

Metaphase is the third phase of Mitosis. The process separates the duplicated genetic elements, which are present in the nucleus of the mother cell, into 2 identical daughter cells.

436480.explanation: The centromere is present in every cell. It is specifically useful in the process of cell division. During mitosis, the spindle fibers attach to the centromeres via kinetochore and all the chromosomes are arranged in an equatorial plane. After this, the chromosomes move towards their respective poles and cell division takes place.

436481.explanation: Meiosis gives rise to four unique daughter cells, each of which has half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell.

436483.explanation: Prophase stage is the longest stage in the cell cycle. In the early prophase stage, the chromatin fibres condense. In mid-prophase, chromosomes show distinct chromatids joined together at the centromere. In the late prophase, the nucleolus degenerates, and the nuclear envelope disappears.

436485.explanation: Typically, a single ascus will contain eight ascospores. The eight spores are produced by meiosis followed by a mitotic division. Two meiotic divisions turn the original diploid zygote nucleus into four haploid ones. Therefore the correct option is meiosis followed by mitosis division.

436487.explanation: In tomato, the male gametophyte is called the pollen grain which is formed from the meiosis of the microspore mother cell and the female gametophyte is called the embryo sac which is formed from the meiosis of megaspore mother cell so, in males, the meiosis occurs in the pollen sac which contains the microspore mother cell and in females, the meiosis occurs in the ovule of the ovary which contains the megaspore mother cell.

436489.explanation: An alkaloid Colchicine is used in plant breeding for doubling the chromosome. It is obtained from the corms of Autumn Crocus ( Colchicum autumnale). It arrests mitosis in metaphase by interfering with the formation of spindle fibrils Therefore called mitotic poison. As it is alkaloid it does not inhibit chromosome replication.

436491.explanation: G1 phase together with the S phase and G2 phase comprise the long growth period of the cell cycle cell division called interphase that takes place before cell division in mitosis (M phase). During G1 phase, the cell grows in size and synthesizes mRNA and protein that are required for DNA synthesis.

436492.explanation: Anaphase is the shortest stage of mitosis. The centromeres divide, and the sister chromatids of each chromosome are pulled apart - or 'disjoin' - and move to the opposite ends of the cell, pulled by spindle fibres attached to the kinetochore regions. By the end of anaphase, the 2 halves of the cell have an equivalent collection of chromosomes.

436494.explanation: Eduard Strasburger was the first to characterise in detail, and to name, the first three phases of mitosis as prophase, metaphase and anaphase (Strasburger 1884; Harris 2001; Zacharias 2001).

436496.explanation: The term gametic refers to the fact that gametes are the result of meiosis. During the gametic life cycle, a reproductive cell produces haploid gametes (sex cells such as egg and sperm) that combine to produce a zygote. The zygote grows by cell division and cell elongation to produce a multicellular diploid individual.

436498.explanation: (ABA) Cis‐abscisic acid decreases the rates of cell growth and cell division in the meristem.

436500.explanation: The centriole and Aster is not common to the mitotic cell of higher plants. The main function of the centrosome is at the time of cell division when the two centrioles separate and move on two poles. Aster and spindle are formed from it which help in the movement of chromatids. They form the basal body, cilia, flagella, etc.

436501.explanation: Formation of spindle apparatus occurs during metaphase. The spindle fiber attaches to the centromere. The nuclear membrane breaks apart into numerous "membrane vesicles", and the chromosomes inside form protein structures called kinetochores. Kinetochore microtubules emerging from the centrosomes at the poles (ends) of the spindle reach the chromosomes and attach to the kinetochores, throwing the chromosomes into agitated motion.

436504.explanation: Synthetic (S) - phase of a cell cycle occurs during interphase, before mitosis or meiosis, and is responsible for the synthesis or replication of DNA. The genetic material of a cell is doubled before it enters mitosis or meiosis, allowing there to be enough DNA to be split into daughter cells.

436507.explanation: Meiosis occurs in Microsporgenesis, Gametogenesis and Megasporogenesis.

436508.explanation: Cerebellum coordinates and controls rapid muscular activities such as running, typing, etc. Although it does not initiate such voluntary movements, but it is an important centre for coordinating movements and for controlling posture and balance.

436510.explanation: Interphase is the portion of the cell cycle that includes the G1, S and G2 phases. During interphase, the cell grows (G1), replicates its DNA (S) and prepares for mitosis (G2).

436513.explanation: Interphase is also called the resting phase or not dividing phase. But, it is actually a highly metabolic active phase, in which the cell prepares itself for the next cell division. It involves many metabolic activities. This phase also involves the synthesis of energy-rich compounds to supply energy.

436515.explanation: Meiosis takes place in the reproductive cell. The prophase of meiosis is divided into leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis. Diplotene is the longest phase which is characterized by the terminalisation of the chaismata of the homologous chromosome.

436518.explanation: Callus - unspecialised, unorganised growing, undifferentiated cell & dividing the mass of cells.

436521.explanation: The availability of mitogen and energy-rich compounds decides whether the G1 phase will be arrested (G0​ phase) or undergo the S- phase. This point is called checkpoint or G1​ cyclin or G1 point. Once the checkpoint of the G1- phase is crossed and the cell has entered S - phase, cell would normally proceed to mitosis without interruption. In Mitosis the DNA of the cell is divided into two different sets of chromosomes.

436524.explanation: Cells usually remain in G1 for about 10 hours of the 24 total hours of the cell cycle. The length of the S phase varies according to the total DNA that the particular cell contains; the rate of synthesis of DNA is fairly constant between cells and species. Usually, cells will take between 5 and 6 hours to complete the S phase. G2 is shorter, lasting only 3 to 4 hours in most cells.

436526.explanation: G1 phase decide weather the cell growth and cell division occurs end of the G1 or not. The G1​ phase, or growth 1/gap 1 phase, is the first of four phases of the cell cycle that takes place in eukaryotic cell division. In this part of interphase, the cell grows in size and synthesizes mRNA and proteins in preparation for subsequent steps leading to mitosis. G1 phase ends when the cell moves into the S phase of interphase.

436529.explanation: There are four stages in the cell cycle. The interphase is comprised of G1, S and G2​ phase. The M phase is considered as the shortest phase in the cell cycle. About 80% of the time is required in the interphase and only 20% in the M-phase. In the M-phase, the shortest phase is anaphase which takes about 0.8% of the cell cycle in which the sister-chromatids break and move apart.

436538.explanation: The first and longest phase of mitosis is prophase. During prophase, chromatin condenses into chromosome, and the nuclear envelope (the membrane surrounding the nucleus) breaks down.

436541.explanation: In dividing animal cells, the spindle bears asters at the two poles. Such a spindle is called amphiaster or centric. In-plant cells, the spindle is acentric or anastral.

436542.explanation: The anterior horns of spinal cord contain cells with fibres that form the anterior (motor) root end and are essential for the voluntary and reflex activity of muscles they innervate. If the anterior horn motor cells are destroyed, the nerves cannot regenerate, and muscles are never useful again.

436544.explanation: Mitosis because each somatic cell has two genes for nearly every trait, the condition is called diploid (2N). During development, cells grow and divide by mitosis so that each daughter cell also contains the full genetic complement of paired alleles.

436547.explanation: Chiasmata is observed in meiosis during diplotene, sub-stage of Prophase-I of meiosis I. It is the result of crossing over. Each chiasma is the site of genetic crossing over between chromosomes that have paired up (i.e . between bivalents. It is produced by breakage and reunion between any two of the four strands present at each site.

436568.explanation: It only stores and releases hormones

436577.explanation: Schwann cells and oligodendrocytes form myelin sheath around the axon. Myelin sheath serves as an insulating layer, preventing loss of energy of the nerve impulse during its passage along the fibre.

436618.explanation: In a brain, every part has a specific function. All the involuntary movements in the body are controlled by medulla oblongata.

436689.explanation: From G1 a cell can exit the cell cycle into a state of quiescence (G0) from where it can undergo differentiation or reenter the cell cycle to proliferate. If the cell continues cell division the genomic DNA will be replicated during S-phase.

436690.explanation: Meiosis takes place in reproductive organs. It results in the formation of gametes with half the normal chromosome number. Young anthers/Testes of grasshopper are the best materials to study meiosis.

436691.explanation: In Chlamydomonas / ulothrix / spyrogyra , the zygospore, after usual rest period, germinates on the arrival of favourable condition. It undergoes meiosis to form 4 or rarely 8 biflagellate zoospores.

436692.explanation: Cell response to DNA damage or incomplete replicated chromosomes in G​​​​​​2 phase. DNA damage is detected by the kinases ATM and ATR, which activate chk1 an inhibitory kinase of Cdc25. The net effect is an increase in the threshold of cyclin B1, effectively stalling the cell in G​​​​​​2 until the damage DNA is repaired.

436694.explanation: Pre - mitotic gap phase- The period in the cell cycle when synthesis of DNA is completed but before mitosis begins.

436695.explanation: Pachytene first stage of meiosis is called prophase I, and this is when the tetrad forms. The two homologous chromosomes will align next to each other. But, since each is made up of two sister chromatids it will look like a group of four.

436696.explanation: At the time of zygospore, germination meiosis takes place in Spirogyra. Under favourable conditions, zygospore undergoes zygotic meiosis to form motile tetra-flagellated comeiospores or non-motile aplanomeiospores. Each meiospore (haploid) germinates to the new filament of (+) (-) strain.

436697.explanation: Synapsis is the pairing of two homologous chromosomes that occurs during meiosis. It allows matching-up of homologous pairs prior to their segregation, and possible chromosomal crossover between them. Synapsis takes place during prophase I of meiosis. When homologous chromosomes synapse, their ends are first attached to the nuclear envelope.

436698.explanation: During sexual reproduction in angiosperms, meiosis occurs in microspore and megaspore mother cells. In one meiotic division, one microspore mother cell in the anther forms 4 microspores, each of which develops as a pollen grain. When there are 100 pollen grains, the meiotic divisions which will be required are 100/4= 25. The number of meiotic divisions for 100 pollen grains is 25.

436699.explanation: In Pteridophyte Dryopteris, adiantium the gametophytes give rise to sporophyte by gametic union and sporophyte gives rise to gametophyte by forming haploid spores(sporogenesis) after meiosis.

436700.explanation: During synapsis, bivalent has 2 chromosomes but 4 chromatids and, therefore, 4 DNA/chromomemata.

436701.explanation: The interphase is the longest phase of the cell cycle. It is divided into G1​ or first growth phase, Synthesis or S phase and G2​2 or second growth phase. The S phase is characterised by biosynthetic activity like duplication of DNA and centrioles.

436702.explanation: Prophase 1 of meiosis is the first stage of meiosis and is defined by five different phases- leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis. Leptotene is the first of five stages of Prophase 1. The second stage is zygotene. Third and fourth is pachytene, diplotene respectively. The last one is the diakinesis.

436703.explanation: Leptotene- It is the beginning of the prophase and the chromosomes appear as thin long threads. The condensation of chromosomes is still not done by this phase.

436704.explanation: Meiosis consists of one division of chromosomes and two nuclear divisions resulting in four nuclei that are usually partitioned into four new haploid daughter cells.

436705.explanation: Colchicine inhibits the formation of microtubules that are involved in the formation of spindle fibers. These spindle fibers are necessary to equally divide the chromosomes in a parental cell into two daughter cells. If microtubules are not formed the genetic material will not be distributed in the two newly forming cells. Hence new cell formation will be inhibited in the metaphase stage and the diploid cell will have twice the number of chromosomes and it will become tetraploid.

436706.explanation: Slipping of chiasmata towards the ends of bivalents called as terminalisation, which occurs during diakinesis; the final stage of the prophase in meiosis, characterized by shortening and thickening of the paired chromosomes, the formation of the spindle fibres, the disappearance of the nucleolus, and degeneration of the nuclear membrane.

436707.explanation: The diploid chromosome number is 8. It contains 16 chromatids. Meiosis I starts with the diploid (2n) cells and ends with the haploid (n) daughter cells. Since, before meiosis I, the cell contains 16 (2n) number of chromatids, the number of chromatids in each daughter cell after meiosis will be 8 (n).

436708.explanation: The phragmoplast is a microtubule spindle plant cell-specific structure that forms during late cytokinesis. The growing cell plate fuses with the existing plasma membrane, producing two daughter cells, each with its own plasma membrane. End plate serves as a scaffold for cell plate assembly and subsequent formation of a new cell wall separating the two daughter cells.

436709.explanation: Meiosis is also known as reductional division. It mainly takes place in reproductive cells. It produces genetic variability during the recombination process of meiosis. It maintains the constancy in the number of diploid chromosomes during sexual reproduction by meiosis II which is an equational division.

436710.explanation: During mitosis, the anaphase stage is characterized by splitting of the centromere. At the anaphase stage, each replicated chromosome splits at the centromere and newly-copied chromosomes start moving towards the two opposite poles.

436711.explanation: Meiosis is also called reduction division because the parent cell produces four daughter cells each having half the number of chromosomes present in the parent cell. In metaphase I, the spindle formation is complete. The bivalents move and arrange themselves on the equatorial plane. Therefore if the number of chromosomes at the equatorial plate is 2n=60, then the number of chromosomes will be 30.

436712.explanation: If a cell is treated with drugs such as Colchicine, vincristine, the assembly of the microtubules is inhibited, while the dis-assembly continues leading to continuous disorganization of microtubules. Colchicine is an alkaloid. It can be extracted from corms of plant Colchicum autumnale and C. luteum. Colchicines prevent spindle formation during mitotic metaphase.

436713.explanation: Meiosis occurs in two stages Meiosis I and Meiosis II. Crossing over and reduction in chromosome number occurs during meiosis I. The meiosis I involves prophase I, metaphase I, anaphase I, and telophase I. Prophase I is a very elaborate and complex stage. It comprises five stages- leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, and diakinesis. The crossing over occurs in the pachytene stage between non-sister chromatids of the same bivalent. The crossing over is a complex enzyme catalysed process. The recombinase enzyme complex carries out crossing over in the pachytene sub-stage of prophase I stage.

436714.explanation: In the zygotene subphase of prophase I of meiosis I, homologous chromosomes start pairing and this process of association is called synapsis. Chromosomal synapsis is accompanied by the formation of the synaptonemal complex. The complex formed by a pair of synapsed or segregation of homologous chromosomes is called bivalent or tetrad.

436716.explanation: S phase (Synthesis Phase) is the phase of the cell cycle in which DNA is replicated, occurring between G1 phase and G2 phase. Since accurate duplication of the genome is critical to successful cell division, the processes that occur during S-phase are tightly regulated and widely conserved. To produce two similar daughter cells, the complete DNA instructions in the cell must be duplicated. DNA replication occurs during this S (synthesis) phase.

436718.explanation:
Homologous chromosomes pair up by a process called synapsis and form a complex bivalent structure in the zygotene stage of prophase I of meiosis I. It allows the matching-up of homologous pairs prior to segregation.
 Synthesis of RNA and protein occurs in G2 phase. This particular phase is spent in synthesising molecules other than DNA, which are required for cell division.
 Enzyme recombinase is involved in crossing over which occurs during the pachytene stage of prophase I of meiosis I. Crossing over is a phenomenon of exchange of segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
 In the anaphase I stage of meiosis I, chromosomes move to opposite poles as centromeres do not separate.

436719.explanation: The amount of DNA and chromosome number of a somatic cell that had just completed the S-phase of its cell cycle have 4 times more DNA content and twice the number of the chromosome as compared to the gametes of the same species. In general, a gamete is haploid. A somatic cell is diploid.

436724.explanation: When a Nuclear membrane and cell plate are not formed in a cell during telophase of mitosis then a polyploid cell is formed. Polyploid is a condition in which a cell has more than two paired (homologous) sets of chromosomes.

 Pachytene - The third stage of prophase I of meiosis, followed by zygotene bivalent chromosomes clearly appear as tetrads, crossing over between homologous chromosomes occurs.
 Metaphase I - The bivalents chromosomes align on the equatorial plate of the spindle. The microtubes from the opposite poles of the spindle attach to the pair of homologous chromosomes.
 Diakinesis - The fifth and final Stage of prophase -I marked by terminalisation of chiasmata followed by diplotene. Chromosomes are fully condensed and -the meiotic spindle is assembled to prepare the homologous chromosome for separation.

 The G1​ phase is the gap between the M phase and S phase and is marked by the synthesis of mRNA and protein (excluding histones) and duplication of all cell content except DNA.
 S phase (occurs between G1 and G2 phase) of DNA replication and cell division is followed by the G2​ phase during which the cell double-checks the duplicated DNA content.

437772.explanation: Light and temperature may affect flowering in plants in various ways. The effect of photoperiods or daily duration of light hours (and dark periods) on flowering is called photoperiodism. Photoperiodic response is mediated by phytochrome, a pigment which perceives the photoperiod stimulus in leaves. It shows reversible change in red and far red wavelength. Besides correct photoperiod, some plants require low temperature for flowering. These plants remain vegetative during the warm season flower in winters on receiving low temperature. This was found by Lysenko, that the cold requiring annual and biennial plants can be made to flower in one growing season by providing low temperature treatment (vernalisation). Stimulus of vernalisation is perceived by meristematic cells, e.g., shoot tips, root apex, etc., and is named as vernalin.
