1111331.explanation: The inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase is by malonate which closely resembles the substrate succinate in structure.

1111333.explanation: Members of order Gnetales posses vessels and show absence of archegonia.

1111337.explanation: Only birds and mammals possess double circulation. Whale is a mammal.

1111352.explanation: Excretion is the removal of metabolic wastes from the body. CO2 and water (H2O) are the metabolic waste of carbohydrates and fat metabolism.

1111354.explanation: Tautonym is the taxonomic designation used for certain animals assigned with same generic name and specific name. E.g., Rattus rattus (rat), Catla catla (catla), etc. Family Leguminosae is divided into three sub-families [Papilionaceae (= Fabaceae), Mimosaceae and Caesalpiniaceae].

1111356.explanation: Flowers are zygomorphic in gulmohur. Flowers of gulmohur have bilateral symmetry. The other three options (Datura, mustard and tomato) have actinomorphic flowers.

1111358.explanation:
The character without exception is the regeneration power of sponges. All the sponges have a good power of regeneration. They can regrow any part of the body lost or cut off small fragments can grow into a complete sponge.

Presence of calcareous or siliceous spicules, marine habitat (some or freshwater living also) and asymmetrical or bilaterally symmetry are some characters with exception.

1111360.explanation: A drupe develops in mango. Drupe is a fleshy fruit that develops from either one or several fused carpels. It contains one or many seeds. The seeds are enclosed by the hard-protective endocarp (pericarp) of the fruit. The pericarp is well differentiated into an outer thin epicarp, a middle fleshy edible mesocarp and an inner stony hard endocarp.

1111362.explanation: The zone of elongation region of a root increases length of the root. The external cells possess the power of absorption of water and minerals salts from the soil. The root hair zone represents the zone of differentiation or maturation because different types of primary tissues differentiate or mature in this region. Maize and sugarcane have stilt roots.

1111364.explanation: Species is the only taxon that exists in nature as a biologically cohesive unit.

1111367.explanation: Some algae withstand or tolerate a very high temperature, and these are often called thermal algae. Such forms are known to grow up to 85oC, nearly boiling water. Their cell wall is hard and protective. A typical cell wall of algae consists of two non-living layers.The inner layeris firm consisting of microfibrils and outer layer is gelatinous and amorphous. Various polysaccharides such as cellulose, pectin, mucilage constitute the typical cell wall.The mucilage covering of the cell is thick and dense and is called the sheath. This sheath which holds the cells in colonies together, have water absorbing and water retaining capacity.It thus protects them under desiccating conditions. Thus, they can surviveunder high temperature.

1111372.explanation: An arthropod has a segmented body covered by an exoskeleton made from chitin and other chemicals. This exoskeleton serves as protection and provides places for muscle attachment. Arthropods must moult because their exoskeletons don't grow with them. The body feature from which the phylum takes its name is the jointed appendages, which include antennae and mouthparts as well as walking leges.

1111379.explanation: The correct option is: A - (iv), B - (iii), C - (ii), D - (i)

1111385.explanation: It is not essential for a genus to have several species. The genus which has single species is called monotypic, while the genus which has several species is called polytypic.

1111387.explanation: Liver is a dark reddish-brown organ which performs various functions. Liver regulates most chemical levels in the blood and excretes a product called bile. Bile, stored and concentrated in gall bladder, helps to digest fatty foods and prepares them for further digestion and absorption. Bile is a yellowish or reddish brown alkaline fluid, secreted from the liver. It is stored and concentrated in the gall bladder. Bile contains cholesterol, salts (like sodium glycocholate, sodium taurocholate and sodium bicarbonate) and pigments like bilirubin and biliverdin. Bile juice helps in the process of digestion by breaking down fatty molecules.

1111389.explanation: In racemose inflorescence, the main axis continues to grow. The flower are borne laterlly in an acropetal succession, which means the older flower are at the base and younger flowers are near the apex, e.g, radish, mustard, Amaranthus. In cymose inflorescence, the axis terminates in a flower, hence, is limited in growth. The flowers are borne in a basipetal order, which means older flowers at the apex and younger flowers are near the base, e.g. cotton, Jasmine, Calotropis.

1111391.explanation: Animals belonging to the same kingdom but different classes may belong to the same phylum.

1111392.explanation: Plasmodium, the malarial parasite, belongs to class Sporozoa.

1111393.explanation: The stomach is responsible for the initial digestion of food in frogs, particularly in breaking down insects and other small prey.

1111395.explanation: Female reproductive part of bryophytes is called archegonium. The male reproductive part of bryophyte is called antheridium. Oogonium is a cellwhich givesrise to oocyte. Sporangium is the structure containing asexual spores.

1111402.explanation: According to the characters described by the student, the plant sample belongs to bryophytes.

1111405.explanation: The three-chambered heart in frogs is less efficient than the four-chambered heart in mammals and birds because it allows partial mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood in the ventricle.

1111409.explanation: Sweet potato is homologous to turnip due to having the same origin. Both sweet potato and turnip are root but modified for different functions. Sweet potato is a modified root for storage and vegetative propagation while turnip is modified for storage purpose only.

1111410.explanation: Algae resemble to plant cell because of presence of chlorophyll in chloroplasts.

1111415.explanation: Nephridia and Malphigian organ are the excretory organs of earthworm and cockroach respectively. Nephridia consist of a simple or branched tube formed by the ingrowth of ectoderm with cilia at the inner end. Excretory products diffuse into the nephridium and are washed out to the exterior by ciliary action. Malpighian tubules, involved in the excretion of nitrogenous wastes, open into the intestine. It selectively extracts the nitrogenous products (uric acid) from the blood which-together with water and salts and deposited into the hindgut which is excreted in the faeces.

1111416.explanation: The animal belongs to mollusca. Mollusca is the second largest phylum after arthropoda and includes predominantly marine animals. They are triploblastic, bilaterally symmetrical, schizocoelic, and unsegmented protostomes. They have moist skin, a complete digestive tract, a ventral nerve cord, and had gone through torsion.

1111417.explanation: Efficient cutaneous respiration in frogs requires that their skin remains moist. Cutaneous respiration is crucial, especially for aquatic frog species.

1111419.explanation:
Anthoceros - Hornwort

Adiantum - Walking fern

Sargassum - Gulfweed

Prothallus - Gametophyte

Laminaria - Devil'sapron

1111421.explanation:
Given type of life cycle is haplodiplontic or diplohaplontic life cycle in which haploid gametophytic phase and diploid sporophytic phase alternate with each other. Both the phases are multicellular, so somatic growth follows meiosis and somatic growth follows the union of gametes or syngamy. Meiosis occurs in the sporophyte at the time of formation of spores and the spores germinate to produce gametophytic plants. Bryophytes and pteridophytes exhibit this life cycle pattern.

Algae exhibit haplontic life cycle pattern and gymnosperms and angiosperms follow diplontic life cycle pattern.

1111433.explanation: Algae mosses and ferns depends on external source of water.

1111435.explanation: The tympanic membrane, or the eardrum, is responsible for detecting sound and vibrations in frogs, helping them in communication and predator avoidance.

1111436.explanation: The figure given in represents the free central placentation. It is seen in Dianthus. In free central placentation, ovary is unilocular and ovules are borne on the axis in the centre of the ovary and septa are absent.

1111442.explanation: Gemmules is a tough-coated dormant cluster of embryonic cells produced by a freshwater sponge (Leucosolenia) for development in more favourable conditions.

1111445.explanation: Hydraulic skeleton or hydro-skeleton is a structure found in many soft-bodied animals consisting of a fluid-filled cavity, the coelom, surrounded by muscles. It is the system of support which relies on the incompressibility of fluids contained within the body cavity. In earthworms the coelomic fluid is under pressure within the coelom and therefore provides support for internal organs. Due to hydraulic skeleton, during burrowing, the anterior end becomes turgid and helps in relaxation of longitudinal muscles.

1111447.explanation: Amplexus is a behavior in which the male grasps the female to facilitate mating and the release of sperm to fertilize the eggs. It does not primarily serve to protect the female or maintain territorial dominance.

1111448.explanation: Dinoflagellates are mostly single-celled organisms classified in the kingdom protista. Dinoflagellates characteristically have two flagella for locomotion and most have a rigid cell wall of cellulose encrusted with silica. Their cell wall is divided into two halves called theca that may fit as two halves of a soap box or a petri dish.

1111449.explanation: As we go higher from species to kingdom, number of common characteristics goes on decreasing.

1111451.explanation: Roots are modified in some plants to perform functions other than absorption and conduction of water and minerals. Figure A shows tap roots of turnip, carrot and adventitious root of sweet potato and figure B shows pneumatophores in Rhizophora. Tap roots system is the characteristic of dicot plants. Tap roots (develop from radicle) and adventitious root (develop from any part of the plant other than the radicle) get swollen and store foods. Pneumatophore is a specialized structure developed from the root in certain plants growing in swamps and marshes. These types of roots come out of the ground and grow vertically upwards. Pneumatophore helps to get oxygen for respiration.

1111453.explanation: The advantage of cutaneous respiration for frogs is that it can occur even when the mouth is closed. This is crucial for frogs, especially when they are submerged in water.

1111460.explanation: Aquatic annelids like Nereis possess lateral appendages (called parapodia) which help in swimming. Radula is the rasping organ for feeding which is present in the mouth of molluses.

1111471.explanation: Olfactory organs in frogs help them to locate prey and avoid predators. They play a crucial role in the frog's survival and are not primarily responsible for vision or temperature detection.

1111472.explanation: Chrysophytes are a group of diatoms, golden algae (desmids) and golden brown photosynthetic.

1111473.explanation: The figure A, B, C and D are respectively Selaginella, Equisetum, Salvinia and Ginkgo.

1111475.explanation: Maximum number of antibiotics are produced by mycelial bacteria known as actinomycetes and most of the actinomycetes are saprotrophic (heterotrophic). Lactic acid bacteria that are used in preparation of curd are also heterotrophic.

1111477.explanation: Taxonomy is the science of naming, describing and classifying organisms and includes all plants, animals and microorganisms of the world. First step in taxonomy is identification of the organism. Identification is the finding of correct name and place of an organism according to some approved system of classification.

1111478.explanation: Sponges, cnidarians, flatworms, and ctenophorans do not have circulatory systems.

1111480.explanation: Glycocalyx provides sticky character to the bacterial cell. It is the outermost mucilage layer of the cell envelope which consists of non-cellulosic polysaccharides with or without proteins.

1111483.explanation: In the given figure of dicotyledonous seeds, the structure marked as A, B, C, D and E are respectively hilum, micropyle, plumule, cotyledon and radicle. Hilum is the scar on a seed marking the point of attachment of the developing seed vessel to the fruit. Micropyle is a small opening or pore present just below the hilum. It is the way of entry of water into the seed. Plumule is the developing bud of a plant embryo, situated above the cotyledons and consisting of the epicotyl and immature leaves. Cotyledon is an embryonic leaf in seed-bearing plants, one or more of which are the first leaves to appear from a germinating seed. Radicle is the first part of a seedling (a growing plant embryo) to emerge from the seed during the process of germination. The radicle is the embryonic root of the plant, and grows downward in the soil (the shoot emerges from the plumule).

1111484.explanation: Microscopic protists. Their body is covered by a transparent siliceous shell.

1111490.explanation: Micrographia book was written by Robert Hooke. This book was published in 1665 and for first applying the word "cell" to describe the basic unit of life.

1111492.explanation: Spongilla, belongs to porifera phylum, is a common, widely distributed fresh water sponge. Choanocytes is a flagellated cell with a collar of protoplasm at the base of the flagellum, numbers of which line the internal chambers of the canal system (characteristic feature) in sponges. Canal system in Spongilla is essentially of rhagon type with choanocytes restricted to small rounded chambers. It is not found in leech, dolphin, and penguin.

1111497.explanation: Sperms of both Funaria and Pteris were released together near the archegonia. But only the sperms of Pteris enter the archegonia, as Pteris archegonia releasesa chemical malic acid to attract its sperms for fertilization.

1111499.explanation: The cerebellum controls rapid muscular activities such as running, typing and even talking. Damage to cerebellum will produce two types of defects: defects of posture and defects of voluntary movements. It mainly causes atonia (less tone); asthenia (weakness of movements) and ataxia (in coordinated movement).

1111501.explanation: Male frogs have copulatory pad on the first digit of fore limbs which facilitate grasping the female during amplexus aiding in successful neating.

1111502.explanation: The adhesive pad of fungi penetrates the host with the help of mechanical pressure and enzymes. It pushes against the cell wall of the host and then releases cellulase to digest cellulose of the host cell wall so that the hypha can penetrate the host cell wall.

1111507.explanation: Biological classification is the scientific arrangement of organisms in a hierarchical series of groups and sub groups on the basis of similarities and differences in their traits. It helps in building evolutionary pathways and in identifying new organisms.

1111508.explanation: Balanoglossus is a connecting link between invertebrates and non-invertebrates. Balanoglossus belongs to phylum hemichordate which was earlier considered as a sub-phylum under phylum chordata. But, now it is placed as a separate phylum under non-chordata because notochord and post anal tail are absent in it.

1111517.explanation: Before 1969, all the organisms had been divided into two groups - plants and animals, mainly on the basis of presence or absence of cell wall. Linnaeus founded two kingdom system of classification - Kingdom Plantae and kingdom Animalia.

1111519.explanation: Earthworms have three types of nephridial structures. These are septal, integumentary and pharyngeal nephridia. These nephridial structures are present on different positions in the body and also vary in structures. Septal and pharyngeal nephridia are both enteronephric, i.e., nitrogen products are expelled in gut whereas integumentary nephridia is exonephric, i.e., nitrogen waste products are directly discharged outside.

1111520.explanation: Electron microscope, made up of electromagnetic lenses, is the best device to determine the structural details of a cell. It can magnify objects up to 250,000 - 400,000 times and its resolving power is 1000 times more than the light microscope. This resolution is because of low wavelength (0.005 nm) of electron beam used as light source.

1111525.explanation: Perisperm is diploid while endosperm is a triploid tissue because perisperm is residual persistent nucellus of seed formed prior to fertilisation while endosperm develops when one of the sperm cells fuses with two haploid polar nuclei. Both perisperm and endosperm are nutritive layers.

1111526.explanation: Fimbriae are small bristle-like solid structures arising from bacterial cell surface. There are 300-400 of fimbriae per cell. Fimbriae are involved in attaching bacteria solid surfaces (e.g., rock in water body) or host tissues(e.g., urinary tract in Neisseria gonorrhoeae). Some fimbriae cause agglutination of RBCs. They also help in mutual clinging of bacteria.

1111532.explanation: In tendrillar petiole, petiole is tendrillar in nature and helps the plant to climb up as in clematis and Nepenthes. The petiole, rachis and the stalk of the leaflets (petiolule) in clematis are sensitive to contact and can coil around the support to help the plant in climbing. Such tendrils are known as rachis and petiolule tendrils.

1111534.explanation: DNA replicates in bacteria just before they divide by fission.

1111535.explanation: In the binomial system of taxonomy, the second word of an organisms biological name represents species.

1111537.explanation: Roots play insignificant role in absorption of water in Pistia (water lettuce). Pistia is a floating aquatic plant in which roots are generally poorly developed and do not take part in absorption of water. Water is absorbed by the general body surface in these plants.

1111541.explanation:
Lipids are fat-soluble vitamins. Lipids can serve a diverse range of functions within a cell, including:



 Storage of energy for long-term use (e.g., triglycerides)
 Hormonalroles (e.g., steroids such as estrogen and testosterone)
 Insulation - both thermal (triglycerides) and electrical (sphingolipids)
 Protection of internal organs (e.g., triglycerides and waxes)
 Structural components of cells (e.g., phospholipids and cholesterol)

1111543.explanation: Underground stems are non-green stems that may take part in perennation, store food or help in vegetative propagation. Underground stems of potato, ginger, turmeric, zaminkand, Colocasia are modified stem to store food in them.

1111549.explanation: Mycoplasma, belongs to Kingdom-Monera, are the Simplest and smallest free-living prokaryotes which are devoid of a cell wall. Nostoc is a cyanobacterium in which cell wall comprises of peptidoglycans. Aspergillus is a fungus in which cell wall is mainly made of chitin. Funaria is a bryophyte in which cell wall is cellulosic in nature.

1111553.explanation: Carl Von Linne (also called Carolus Linnaeus) was involved with taxonomy. He was called the father of taxonomy. He laid the foundations for the modern scheme of taxonomy.

1111555.explanation: Tail end is straight in female Ascaris, while it is curved ventral wards in male Ascaris. The forelimbs in both frogs (male and female) bear small articular pads dorsally at the joints of digit, but the males possess a special nuptial, copulatory pad also. This copulatory pad is present on ventral side of the first finger of each forelimb. Copulatory pad appears as rough patches but becomes thick and sticky during breeding season. It is also involved in sexual reproduction. In copulation, the male strongly grips a female under her armpits by means of these pads. Anal cerci are present in both male and female cockroach, while anal style is present only in the male cockroach.

1111557.explanation: Viruses are not applicable to cell theory. Virus is made up of proteins and one of nucleic acids, i.e., DNA or RNA. So, they lack protoplasm, the essential part of the cell.

1111563.explanation: Pteridophytes differ from mosseslbryophytes in having well developed vascular tissue system. In mosseslbryophytes vascular tissue is absent.

1111568.explanation: In mint and jasmine, a slender lateral branch arises from the base of the main axis and after growing aerially for some time arches downwards to touch the ground.

1111569.explanation: The correct labeling in the figures of bacterial cell and Nostoc are - A - cell wall, B - cell membranes, C - DNA, D -heterocysts, E - mucilaginous sheath.

1111570.explanation: Matthias Schleiden and Theodore Schwann proposed the cell theory. Matthias Schleiden in 1838 discovered that all plants were made up of cells. Theodore Schwann in 1839 discovered that all the animals are made up of cells.

1111573.explanation: Tap root or primary roots develop from the radicle. It form lateral branches or secondary roots which are further branched to form tertiary roots. This type of root system is seen in the mustard plant.

1111577.explanation:
Objectives and functions of classification include:



 Recognition and complete description of different species.
 Development of a system for easy identification of various species.
 Formulating a scheme of hierarchical grouping of species on the basis of their similar or correlated characters.
 To establish relationships on the basis of resemblance and differences between organisms.

1111581.explanation: Seeds of monocotyledonous plants have only one cotyledon. In family Poacease (e.g., wheat, maize etc.), this cotyledon is called scutellum which is situated towards lateral side of embryonal axis. It provides nourishment to the developing embryo.

1111582.explanation: A typhlosole is an internal fold of the intestine or intestine inner wall. It occurs in bivalve molluscs, lampreys and some annelids and echinoderms. In earthworms, it is a dorsal flap of the intestine that runs along most of its length, effectively forming a tube within a tube, and increasing the absorption area of the digested food in the intestine by that of its inner surface.

1111592.explanation: Walking fern is named so because when its leaf tips come in contact with soil, it forms new plants as adventitious buds develop at leaftips. This helps in the spread of fern over a large soil surface and thus the name 'walking fern'.

1111593.explanation: Cockroach contains two mandibles (part of mouth) which bears teeth. When both the mandibles work simultaneously in a horizontal plane, the food matter is cut and masticated into fine and smaller pieces. Gizzard is a part of alimentary canal which bears six muscular folds covered by chitinous conical plates, the teeth. Gizzard is used for grinding the food.

1111595.explanation: Classification is the process by which anything is grouped into convenient categories based on some easily observable characters. In angiosperms characters of flowers are used in classification because characters of angiospermic flowers are preserved for its further studies and references.

1111600.explanation: Morels and truffles (both belong to ascomycetes) are edible mushrooms. Morels have edible ascocarps that have fleshy sponge-like conical cap or pileus and a stalk like stipe, e.g., Morchella esculenta. Truffles have tuber-like subterranean ascocarps that are often dug out with the help of trained dogs and pigs, e.g. Tuber aestivum.

1111601.explanation: Phylogenetic system or cladistics is based on evolutionary sequence as well as the genetic relationship amongst the living beings.

1111606.explanation: Figure A, Band C are respectively tap root, fibrous root and adventitious root. The root branches of the primary root are called as taproot system. The monocotyledons will have the primary root as short-lived and it has many numbers of small lateral roots. These roots develop at the stem base and they form a root system called as fibrous root system, which is observed in the wheat plant (monocot). In some plants like banyan tree and grass, parts of the plant other than radicle will be responsible for the development of root system called as adventitious root system.

1111607.explanation: Genus is more specific and species from the same genus have more characteristics in common than those just in the same family.

1111616.explanation: Diploblastic animals (e.g., poriferans) have two germinal layers (ectoderm and endoderm) during embryonic development whereas triploblastic animals have three germinal layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm) during embryonic development, e.g., platyhelminthes.

1111617.explanation: The stomatal aperture, guard cells and the neighbouring (and encircling) cells are called a stomatal complex or stomatal apparatus. Stomata consist of an opening or stomatal pore, and two kidney-shaped guard cells. The guard cells are used for opening and closing the stomatal pore, to regulate the evapotranspiration and gas exchange. These guard cells are kidney-shaped in dicot and dumbbell-shaped in monocots. The epidermal cells surrounding the guard cells are specialised and are known as subsidiary cells or accessory celIs. Stomata are often more common on the lower leaf surfaces

1111623.explanation: Though the bacterial structure is very simple, they are very complex in behaviour. Compared to many other organisms, bacteria as a group show the most extensive metabolic diversity. Some of the bacteria are autotrophic, i.e., they synthesise their own food from inorganic substrates. They may be photosynthetic autotrophic or chemosynthetic autotrophic. The vast majority of bacteria are heterotrophs, i.e., they do not synthesise their own food but depend on other organisms or on dead organic matter for food.

1111624.explanation: Cell is the structural and functional unit of living things.

1111625.explanation: In modern taxonomy, species is considered to be dynamic.

1111629.explanation: Figure is responsible to spread and vegetative propagation.

1111632.explanation: Spirulina is a cyanobacterium. This is a spiral shaped alga. The algae are considered as a source of many elements like iron, manganese and chromium. There are many essential amino acids which make the algae a rich source of protein. The protein content of this algae is considered more than the beef. The protein tablets or powder is made from this algae which can be used as food supplement.

1111635.explanation: Microtubular organisation and type of movement differentiate prokaryotic flagella from eukaryotic flagella.

1111639.explanation: Taxonomic hierarchy is the arrangement of various taxa. Carl Linnaeus developed a hierarchical system for organising living organisms in which highest rank was given to kingdom, followed subsequently by phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species. Species was Linnaeus's least inclusive level of classification and includes all organisms of similar morphologies that can interbreed and produce viable offspring. According to the given hierarchical system, family comes between order and genus.

1111641.explanation: Ureters act as urinogenital duct which open into the cloaca in case of male frog. They run backwards from the kidneys and open into the cloaca. In female, ureters carry urine alone, while in male it transports both sperms and urine. Hence, they are called urino-genital ducts.

1111645.explanation: Shows the organism which is scientifically correctly named, correctly printed according to the International Rules of Nomenclature and correctly described. Plasmodium falciparum is a protozoan parasite that causes malaria in humans. Being digenetic, its life cycle is completed in two hosts - man and female Anopheles mosquito. Its sexual cycle is completed in Anopheles mosquito. During their life cycle, an infective stage (called sporozoites) is formed, which is then transmitted to humans with the bite of infected female Anopheles. Scientific name of common house lizard is Hemidactylus whereas Musca domestica is the scientific name of housefly. Scientific name of Indian tiger is Panthera tigris. Full name of E. coli is Escherichia coli.

1111648.explanation: In the given figure, part labelled as A, B, C and D are epicarp, mesocarp, seed and endocarp respectively. In mango and coconut, the fruit is known as drupe. Drupe develops from monocarpellary superior ovaries. In mango, the pericarp is differentiated into an outer thin epicarp, middle fleshy edible mesocarp and an inner stony hard endocarp. In coconut, the mesocarp is represented by the fibrous part.

1111651.explanation: Binomial nomenclature was developed by Linnaeus (Philosophia Botanica, 1751). Linnaeus described 5900 species of plants in his book Species Plantarum (1753) and 4326 species of animals in his book Systema Naturae (1758).

1111653.explanation: Tendril is a slender thread-like appendage of a climbing plant. It often grows in a spiral form, which stretches out and twines round any suitable support.

1111659.explanation: Erythrocytes contain the pigment haemoglobin, which imparts the red colour to blood, and transport oxygen and carbon dioxide to and from the tissues. Human erythrocytes are enucleated and discoidal while in frogs erythrocytes are large, oval and biconvex nucleated cells.

1111665.explanation:
Lichen are peculiar dual organisms produced by the intimate association of two organisms a fungus and an alga. The association between the two organisms is symbiosis. Both the organisms are mutually benefitted in this association and are dependent on each other. The algal cell photosynthesizes with the help of chloroplast.

Therefore, lichens are autotrophic. A part of these manufactured carbohydrates is used by the alga in its nutrition, the rest is supplied to the fungal partner. The fungus in turn provides water and nutrients which it absorbs from the soil using the rhizoidal hyphae. Thus, both the partners get benefitted from each other. The algal partner is called phycobiont and the fungal partner is called mycobiont.

1111666.explanation: Syconus is a composite fruit which develops from the hypanthodium inflorescence, e.g., Ficus carica, Ficus Benghalensis. The flask shaped fleshy receptacle encloses female flower which produces small achene like fruitlets and has a small pore protected by scale leaves.

1111668.explanation: Bacterial leaf blight of rice is caused by Xanthomonas oryzae, a bacterium which is gram-negative, aerobic, capsulated, and motile with a single polar flagellum. Primary infection is carried through the infected seeds. The entry of the pathogen occurs through wounds and stomata. This disease is characterised by the appearance of linear, yellow to straw coloured stripes, usually on both the edges of the leaf. As the disease progresses, the drying and twisting of the leaf tip occurs. The most destructive phase of the disease is the 'Ikresek' or wilt resulting from early systemic infection.

1111669.explanation: Algae are a group of chlorophyllous, nonvascular plants with thallose plant body. Different algae show different pogments present in the cell like chlorophyll a, b, xanthophylls, carotenes ets. These pigments provide the base for classification of various groups of algae into different classes. Chlorophyceae possess chlorophyll - a,b pigments, bacillariophyceae contains diatomin pigment, phaeophyceae has fucoxanthin, rhodophyceae has r - phycocyanin and r - phycoerythrin, cyanophyceae has phycobilin pigment.

1111671.explanation: Ribosomes are a common feature to prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

1111672.explanation: Danish bacteriologist Christian Gram for the first time classified bacteria on the basis of the cell wall into two groups - gram +ve and gram -ve by staining with crystal violet and safranin. Gram +ve cell walls are less complex with peptidoglycan compounds and proteins and no lipids in the cell wall. Whereas in Gram -ve cell walls are more complex with peptidoglycan compounds, phospholipids and lipopolysaccharidesand contain 20% lipids.

1111677.explanation: The major part of the grain is occupied by a large endosperm which is rich in starch. The endosperm has one to three layered peripheral protein layers called aleurone layer which separates the embryo with endosperm.

1111678.explanation: The structures marked as A, B, C, D and E in the given figure of monocotyledonous seeds, are respectively endosperm, embryo, scutellum, coleoptile and coleorhiza. Endosperm is the part of a seed which acts as a food store for the developing plant embryo, usually containing starch with protein and other nutrients. Embryo is the part of a seed which develops into a plant, consisting (in the mature embryo of a higher plant) of a plumule, a radicle, and one or two cotyledons. Scutellum is the large shield like cotyledon of the embryo of certain monocots. It is specialized for the absorption of food from the endosperm. Coleoptile is the first leaf above the ground, forming a protective sheath around the stem tip. It surrounds the plumule. Coleorhiza is the sheath that envelops the radicle in certain plants and that is penetrated by the root in germination.

1111680.explanation: Pinus is a monoecious plant, i.e., both male and female cones are present in same plant but on different branches.

1111682.explanation: Classification is the arrangement of organisms into convenient categories or groups on the basis of their similarities and differences in certain easily observable but fundamental characters. A hierarchy of categories is raised keeping in mind the affinities or relationships of various groups.

1111683.explanation: Ureotelic mode of excretion is common in both frog and humans. Excretion of urea is known as ureotelism and the animals which excrete urea are called ureotelic. Urea is less toxic and less soluble in water than ammonia. Hence, it can stay for some time in the body. Ureotelic animals include Ascaris, earthworm (both are ammonotelic and ureotelic), cartilaginous fishes like sharks and sting rays, semi-aquatic amphibians such as frogs and toads, aquatic or semi-aquatic reptiles like turtles, terrapins, and alligators, and man and all other mammals. Amphibian tadpole (e.g., tadpole of frog) excretes ammonia but after metamorphosis frog excretes urea.

1111692.explanation:
A prokaryotic autotrophic nitrogen-fixing symbiont is found in Cycas.

Cycas form facultative symbiotic association with autotrophic nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria. This association provides fixed carbon and a stable environment to the cyanobacteria in exchange for fixed nitrogen. These cyanobacteria are endosymbionts and live within the roots of Cycas.

1111694.explanation: Nucleoid is an irregularly shaped region found within the prokaryotic cell. It contains all or most of the genetic material in the form of chromosomes (called genophore). In contrast to the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell, it is not surrounded by a nuclear membrane.

1111697.explanation: In pomegranate, the fruit is chambered, developed from inferior ovary and has seeds with succulent testa. In this, the whole fruit is covered by a hard rind which is made up of exocarp and a part of meso carp. It develops from multilocular syncarpous inferior ovary. Mesocarp forms the plate like infolding (i.e., chambered) and the seeds are covered by endocarp and contain bright red succulent testa.

1111699.explanation: Puccinia-smut is incorrectly matched. Puccinia is a pathogen of rust. Rust is a group of parasitic fungi of the phylum Basidiomycota. Many of these species attack the leaves and stem of cereal crops. Pathogens of rust are Puccinia, Uromyces, Melampsora, Hemileia.

1111703.explanation:
Sex pili are minute and non-flagellar hair-like structures projecting from the wall of many gramnegative bacteria and few Gram +ve ones. They are entirely composed of a protein called pilin. They are used as sex organs during conjugation, form conjugation tube during conjugation. They confer the property of stickiness whereby bacteria tend to adhere to one another (clump formation). They are of two types-long conjugating pili and short attachment pili.

Naked circular DNA is the genetic material which is not enclosed by nuclear membrane noncomplexed with proteins. It is called nucleoid or genophore. Plasmids (Hayes and Lederberg, 1952) are additional or extrachromosomal small rings of DNA having a few useful but nonvital genes, e.g., for fertility factor, R- factors or resistance factor.

1111705.explanation: The feature of prokaryotes that sets them apart from eukaryotes is their lack of internal membranes, that is, their cell interiors are not compartmentalised into organelles in the way that eukaryotic cells are.

1111709.explanation: Pheretima (earthworm) and related organisms feed upon the decaying organic matter found in the soil. They also feed on the bits of plants and animal matter. Thus, they are omnivorous.

1111711.explanation: The pathogen Microsporum is genus of kingdom fungi that causes diseases of skin and hair in humans and animals like dog, cat, monkey. Ringworm is caused by the dermatophyte fungi species of Microsporum, Trichophyton and Epidermophyton. Rhizopus, a black bread mould belongs to group Zygomycetes of Kingdom Fungi.

1111714.explanation: Most of the algae (eukaryotes) possess a definite cell wall containing cellulose and other carbohydrates. Algal cell wall is composed of different chemical components (e.g., xylan, mannan, galactancs alginic acid, silica, agar, pectin, carrageenin, etc.) which vary widely among different groups. Cell wall of blue-green algae is made up of micro-peptides (proteins). This micro-peptide is not found in eukaryotic algae.

1111715.explanation: Genus and species are the parts of scientific names of binomial nomenclature.

1111717.explanation: Calyx of the flower contains sepals which are green in colour and look like leaf and protect the other whorls of the flower. Corolla is present inside the calyx and made up of petals. Petals are different in color and shapes and protect the other whorls present inside it. It attracts insects for pollination due to its color. Androecium is present inside the corolla and made up of stamens. Each stamen contains filament, anther and a connective.

1111721.explanation: Androecium (male whorl) is composed of stamens. Each stamen which represents the male reproductive organ consists of a stalk or a filament or an anther.

1111723.explanation: The described statements are associated with trichomes. Trichomes are hair-like outgrowth from an epidermal cell of a plant, as a bristle, prickle, root hair, etc. They are ephemeral or persistent and their cell wall is made up of cellulose. Trichomes serve a variety of functions based on their location. As root hairs (and as leaf hairs in epiphytes), trichomes absorb water and minerals. As leaf hairs, they reflect radiation, lower plant temperature, and reduce water loss. They also provide defence against insects.

1111728.explanation: Acoelomates are animals having no body cavity or coelom, e.g., poriferans, coelenterates, ctenophora, platyhelminths, and nemathelminths. In pseudo-coelomates, body space is pseudo-coelom or false coelom, e.g., ectoprocta, aschelminthes. Incoelomates, body space is a true coelom enclosed by mesoderm on both sides. Remaining phyla of bilateria, from annelida to arthropoda are coelomates. Molluscs and insects are coelomates while flatworms are acoelomates.

1111729.explanation: Plasmid is a genetic structure in a cell that can replicate independently of the chromosomes, typically a small circular DNA strand in the cytoplasm of a bacterium or protozoan. Plasmids are much used in the laboratory manipulation of genes. This structure provides genetic instructions for certain cell activities (e.g., antibiotic resistance) and can be transferred from cell to cell in a bacterial colony.

1111733.explanation:
Cyanobacteria are gram negative prokaryotes which are popularly known as blue-green algae.

Although cyanobacteria are true prokaryotes, but their photosynthetic system closely resembles with that of eukaryotes because they have chlorophyll a and photosystem II and they carry out oxygenic photosynthesis.

Like the red algae, cyanobacteria use phycobiliproteins as accessory pigments. Photosynthetic pigments and electron transport chain components are in thylakoid membranes lined with particles called phycobilisomes, which contain phycobilin pigments, particularly phycocyanin and transfer energy to photosystem II.

They contain nitrogenase enzyme for nitrogen fixation. This enzyme becomes inactive in the presence of oxygen but the thick walled heterocysts provide suitable anaerobic enviornment for nitrogenase activity even in aerobic conditions.

1111734.explanation: Pinus and Cedrus have branched stem. Cycas has unbranched stem.

1111735.explanation: Prokaryotes are single-celled organisms of the domains Bacteria and Archaea. All prokaryotes have plasma membranes, cytoplasm, ribosomes, a cell wall, DNA, and lack membrane-bound organelles. Many also have polysaccharide capsules. Prokaryotic cells range in diameter from 0.1 - 5.0 $\mu$ m.

1111738.explanation:
Nostoc belongs to cyanophyceae. In cyanophyceae, sexual reproduction is completely absent. They reproduce by colony formation, hormogonia, akinetes, heterocysts and endospores. However genetic recombination has been observed. It may be probably through transformation or conjugation.

The other three algae- Spirogyra, Ulothrix and Volvox belong to chlorophyceae. The members of this class show isogamous, anisogamous and oogamous type of sexual reproduction.

1111740.explanation: Oscillatoria is a filamentous Gram - ve cyanobacteria which perform oxygenic photosynthesis because of the presence of chlorophyll-a like eukaryotic algae and other higher plants.

1111741.explanation:
Black stem rust is caused by Puccinia graminis. The genus Puccinia includes 700 species, which cause rust diseases of many economic plants such as wheat, barley, oats, etc. It is called a rust because of the reddish-brown color of the spores that are found chiefly upon the surface of the host leaves and stem. P. graminis is heteroecious i.e., requiring two hosts, wheat and barberry for the completion of normal life cycle.

According to the nature of the spores, the life cycle of the P. graminis is divided into five stages. It is during, teleuto stage, the teliospore (or teleutospores) produce dark brown to black pustules on the surface of stem and leaves of the wheat that result into 'black stem rust of wheat'.

1111745.explanation: The correct option is (A = Pepo, B = Drupe). The type of fruit given is pepo (A) and drupe (B). Pepo is an indehiscent fleshy one-celled many-seeded berry (such as a pumpkin, squash, melon, or cucumber) that has a hard rind and is the characteristic fruit of the gourd family. Drupe is an indehiscent fruit consisting of outer epicarp, fleshy or fibrous mesocarp, and stony endocarp enclosing a single seed, a sin the peach, plum, and cherry.

1111746.explanation: Hydra, a representative of coelenterata shows body organisation of cell-tissue grade. Cells are mostly scattered and differentiated for different functions. Some cells form tissues like nerve net or nervous tissue.

1111747.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes, which consist of a single cell with a simple internal structure. It can be classified into two groups on the basis of reaction of bacteria to Gram's stain.

1111752.explanation: Spermatophyta, which includes seed bearing plants, consistsofgymnosperms and angiosperms. Acacia and sugarcane both are angiosperms. Pinus and Cycas both are gymnosperms. Rhizopus belongs to kingdom fungi and Triticum is an angiosperm. Ginkgo is gymnosperm and Pisum is an angiosperm. So, Ginkgo and Pisum correctly represent the grouping spermatophyta.

1111753.explanation: Fimbriae are hair-like structures present in large number in bacteria. They help in attaching bacteria to solid surfaces or host tissues.

1111758.explanation: Bilateral symmetry is found in few invertebrates and all vertebrates.

1111759.explanation: Malpighian corpuscle (renal corpuscle) comprises glomerulus and Bowman's capsule. The Malpighian corpuscle is named after Marcello Malpighi, an Italian physician and biologist.

1111767.explanation: In some seeds, during the process of the development of the embryo, the food up in the endosperm is continuously drawn up by the developing embryo and thus completely exhausted. Such seeds are known as exalbuminous or non-endospermic. The common examples are gram, pea, bean, tamarind, orchid, etc.

1111768.explanation: Chara is a freshwater,green algafound submerged in shallow water ponds, tanks, lakes and slow running water. In Chara, antheridium and oogonium (globule and nucule respectively) are borne at the nodes of short branches,with globule towardslowerside and nucule towardsupper side.

1111769.explanation: The application of name of taxonomic groups is determined by means of nomenclature types. When a single specimen is clearly designated in the original description, this specimen is known as the 'holotype' of that species. 'Isotype' is a plant specimen that is a duplicate of or very similar to the type specimen and can be used as a reference specimen if the type specimen is lost. If a number of small herbaceous plants are collected at the same time, all belonging to the same new species, is considered as the holotype, the rest are isotypes. A 'paratype' is a specimen cited with original description other than the type on which the description of the new taxon has been based. Thus, there can be only one sheet of holotype, whereas a number of sheets of isotypes and paratypes. A 'lectotype' is a specimen selected from the original material to serve as nomenclatural type when the holotype was not designated at the time of publication or for so long as it is missing.

1111771.explanation: Yeast is a group of unicellular fungi of the phylum Ascomycota. They occur as single cell or as a group or chain of cells. Yeast of the genus Saccharomyces ferment sugar and are used to make bread and beer.

1111776.explanation: Glycocalyx is the outermost layer of the cell envelope. Cell wall lies between plasma membrane and glycocalyx.

1111777.explanation: Diploblastic animals have two germinal layers, outer ectoderm and inner endoderm, e.g., porifera and coelenterate. Triploblastic animals have three germinal layers - outer ectoderm, middle mesoderm, and inner endoderm, e.g., platyhel- minthes, aschelminthes, annelida, arthropoda, molluscs, echinodermata, and chordata.

1111780.explanation: The correct representation of organisation levels in living beings is Atomic $\rightarrow$ Molecular $\rightarrow$ Subcellular $\rightarrow$ Cellular $\rightarrow$ Tissue $\rightarrow$ Organ system $\rightarrow$ Individual.

1111785.explanation: Episome is a genetic element inside some bacterial cells, especially the DNA of some bacteriophages, that can replicate independently of the host and also in association with a chromosome with which it becomes integrated.

1111790.explanation: Cyclostomes are an eel-like jawless vertebrate with a round sucking mouth. Ornithorhyncus and Tachyglossus are oviparous mammals. A crocodile is a reptile which possesses four-chambered heart. In cartilaginous fish (except Chimaera) gills are not covered by an operculum.

1111791.explanation: According to the position of gynoecium, the flowers are of three kinds: perigynous, hypogynous and epigynous. The given statements describe the perigyny condition of flowers. In perigynous condition of flower, the calyx, corolla and androecium arise from the around of ovary. In these flowers the ovary is semi-inferior, e.g., plum, rose and peach.

1111792.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus wrote Species Plantarum and provided a basis for the classification of plants.

1111795.explanation: Prokaryotic cell is usually small (0.1 - 5.0 $\mu$ m) in size whereas eukaryotic cell size is comparatively larger (5 - 100 $\mu$ m).

1111796.explanation: The animals in which the coelom is absent are called acoelomates, e.g., flatworms (Planaria). In flat-worms the space between ectoderm and endoderm is filled with parenchyma derived from mesoderm.

1111798.explanation: All species of Chara reproduce sexually and show highly advanced oogamy. Male and female gametangia are called antheridia and oogonia respectively. Male fructification (cluster of antheridia) is called globule and the female IS nucule. They are borne at the nodes of short branches, globule towards lower side and nucule (female structure) towards upper side.

1111802.explanation: Sexual reproduction, a key feature of species, results in the production of offspring different from the parents due to recombination and mutations. This shows that the species may change with time. Thus, the species are really dynamic groups and not static as held earlier.

1111803.explanation: Root hairs - Help in absorbing water and minerals from the soil.

1111809.explanation: The length of different internodes (that occur between two adjacent node) in a culm of sugarcane is variable because of intercalary meristem. Intercalary meristem is present at the base of internode and is found in the stem of grasses and other monocotyledonous plants. In earlier stages, internode is wholly or partially meristematic but later on few of its parts become matured more rapidly as compared to the rest, so a definite continuous sequence of development is maintained, i.e., mature tissue left behind whereas new ones grow which later results in variable length.

1111810.explanation: The correct option is (a): A - (iii), B - (ii), C - (iv), D - (i)

1111816.explanation: Binomial nomenclature is the formal system of naming species. The essence of it is that each species name is in (modern scientific) Latin and has two parts, so that it is also sometimes popularly known as the 'Latin name of the species; although this terminology is frowned upon by biologists, who prefer the phrase scientific name.

1111817.explanation: White rust occurs in crucifers and is characterised by the appearance of irregular white blisters containing conidiosporangia on the leaves and stems. White rust is caused by Albugo Candida (Cystopus candidus).

1111823.explanation: Pinus is more advanced from the evolutionary point of view. It belongs to gymnosperm and bear seeds and have well developed vascular conducting system. While Selaginella, Funaria and Chlamydomonas do not bear seeds.

1111829.explanation: Gymnosperms show distinct alternation of generations. The sporophytic phase is dominant which is differentiated into root, stem and leaves. The number of chromosomes in a leaf cell is diploid (2n), (2n = 16). Double fertilization is absent in gymnosperms. The endosperm develops before fertilization directly from the megaspore. So, the number of chromosomes in endosperm will be 8 (n = 8).

1111830.explanation: Glycocalyx is the unorganised layer of extracellular material that surrounds bacteria cell envelope which consists of non-cellulosic polysaccharides with or without proteins. It may occur in the form of loose sheath, called slime layer. A slime layer in bacteria is an easily removable (e.g., by centrifugation).

1111835.explanation:
The Cyathus is known as bird's nest fungi, and Lycoperdon is called puffballs. Both these fungi belong to the group of club fungi or basidiomycetes. These fungi produce spores inside club-shaped fruit bodies called basidium. Typically, basidium has 4 basidiospores produced exogenously.

Peziza and Morchella, Claviceps belong to ascomycetes (produce ascospores in ascocarps). Mushrooms are basidiomycete fungi.

1111838.explanation: Methanogens are a type of archaebacteria which are strict anaerobes. Nutritionally they are autotrophs which obtain both energy and carbon from decomposition of products. They occur in marshy areas where they convert formic acid and carbon dioxide into methane with the help of hydrogen. This capability is commercially exploited in the production of methane and fuel gas inside gobar gas plants e.g., Methanobacterium, Methanococcus.

1111841.explanation: Phosphorus is present in the form of phospholipid bilayer in plasma membrane. It is an essential component of all nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) but never found in proteins.

1111842.explanation: Many free-living bacteria and blue green algae are capable to fix atmospheric nitrogen. Rhodospirillum is a free living photosynthetic anaerobic nitrogen fixing non-sulphur bacteria. It is capable of synthesising its organic food in presence of light and in absence of O2 by a process known as bacterial photosynthesis. Beijernickia and Azotobacter are free living but aerobic nitrogen fixing bacteria. Rhizobium is a symbiotic nitrogen fixing bacteria.

1111843.explanation: Diatoms are marine or freshwater unicellular organisms which have cell walls (frustules) composed of pectin impregnated with silica and consisting of two halves, one overlapping the other. The siliceous frustules of diatoms do not decay easily.

1111848.explanation: The organisms attached to the substratum possess radial symmetry in all vertical planes. All the animals belonging to cnidaria (e.g., jellyfish) and echinodermata (e.g., starfish) are radially symmetrical, and typically sessile in their adult form. In radial symmetry the parts in an organ or organism when cut through the centre in any direction produce two halves that are mirror images of each other.

1111849.explanation: Castor is an example of a seed with endosperm, perisperm, and caruncle. The seed of castor are endospermic dicot seeds. They possess endosperm (below perisperm as a large, white swollen and oily mass) which acts as storage tissues of seed. They also possess perisperm (as a very thin membrane over kernel) and caruncle. Caruncle protects micropyle and develops as an integumental outgrowth after fertilisation.

1111855.explanation: Phycomycetes are characterised by the presence of coenocytic multinucleate and branched mycelium. They are lower fungi, which typically form a non-septate mycelium.

1111861.explanation: Alginicacid is obtained from brown algae whereas carrageenan is obtained from red algae.

1111865.explanation: Trichinella spiralis is an ovoviviparous nematode parasite, occurring in rodents, pigs, horses, bears, and humans, and is responsible for the disease trichinosis. Trichinosis is characterised by symptoms like diarrhoea, nausea, vertigo, pain in limbs and fever, etc. It shows viviparity, i.e., produces live young's (larvae) not eggs.

1111867.explanation: Chemical digestion is a process which can take place by the action of enzymes and broken down food particles into the simpler nutrients suitable for the absorption and assimilation into the body. It begins in the mouth when food mixes with saliva. The chemical process of digestion of starch is initiated in the oral cavity by the hydrolytic action of the carbohydrate splitting enzyme, the salivary amylase. This enzyme is secreted by salivary gland. Pepsin is a gastric enzyme, secreted from chief cells. It breaks down proteins into smaller peptides. Trypsin is a protein-digesting enzyme. It is present in pancreatic juices and secreted into the small intestine during a meal as an inactive proenzyme called trypsinogen. Once in the intestine, enteropeptidase secreted from intestinal cells, converts trypsinogen into active trypsin enzyme. Pancreatic amylase is secreted by the pancreas into the small intestine. Pancreatic amylase completes the digestion of carbohydrate and produces glucose, that is absorbed into the blood and carried throughout the body.

1111869.explanation:
Rhizopus is a saprophytic fungus that grows on dead organic matter. The mycelium is differentiated into three kinds of hyphae: rhizoidal, stolons and sporangiophores.

The rhizoidal hyphae are for anchorage and absorbing food by secreting enzymes. Stolons grow horizontally over the surface of the substratum. Sporangiophores are specialized hyphae that bear a sporangium at their tip (inside columella a dome-shaped sterile portion the sporangia). It helps in dispersal of spores and usually persists even after bursting of the sporangium.

1111871.explanation: In basal type of placentation, the ovary is unilocular and ovules generally reduced to one borne at the base of the ovary, e.g., compositae.

1111872.explanation: Opuntia has fleshy organs where water and mucilage are stored. It is a xerophytic plant which lives in dry habitat. In this plant, stem is modified into flat green leafy structure, phylloclade.

1111873.explanation: In Rhodospirillum, anoxygenic photosynthesis occurs because electron donor is organic compound instead of water hence no oxygen is released. In other plants water is used as electron donor and H+ and O2 are produced during photolysis of water.

1111875.explanation: Trichome is a smalI hair or other outgrowth from the epidermis of a plant stem, typically unicellular and glandular. Trichomes that often cover the plant body are the result of divisions of epidermal celIs. They may be branched or unbranched and soft or stiff. The trichomes help in preventing water loss due to transpiration. Transpiration is a process where plants absorb water through the roots and then give off water vapour through pores in their leaves

1111878.explanation: The sporophyte is diploid and produces spores.

1111883.explanation: Amoeboid protozoans move and capture their prey by putting out pseudopodia (false feet).

1111885.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the first or generic word starts with a capital letter while the second word or specific epithet starts with a small letter. The name of taxonomist appears after the specific epithet, i.e., at the end of the biological name and is written in abbreviated form, e.g., Ficus benghalensis L., indicates that this species was first described by Linnaeus.

1111887.explanation:
Dorsal hollow nerve cord derives from ectoderm that rolls into a hollow tube during development. In chordates, it is located dorsal to the notochord. The nerve cord found in most chordate embryos develops into the brain and spinal cord, which compose the central nervous system.

In vertebrate fishes, the pharyngeal slits are modified into gill supports, and in jawed fishes, into jaw supports. Humans are chordates due to possessing notochord. In vertebrates, the notochord is present during embryonic development, at which time it induces the development of the neural tube and serves as a support for the developing embryonic body. The notochord, however, is not found in the postnatal stage of vertebrates; at this point, it has been replaced by the vertebral column (also called spine).

1111889.explanation: Scutellum is the tissue in a grass or wheat or maize seed that lies between the embryo and the endosperm. It is the modified cotyledon and specialised for the digestion and absorption of the endosperm.

1111891.explanation: Runner is not an example of water hyacinth. Examples of runners are doob grass, Oxalis etc. Runner is a modification of subaerial stem. It arises from the vase of the stem as a lateral branch and runs along the surface of the soil. It develops distinct nodes and internodes. At each node, the runner produces roots below and leaves above.

1111899.explanation:

 (B) Peduncle
