1112431.explanation: RBC (red blood cell) of the human is the best material for the study of structure of cell membrane. Chemical studies on the RBC cell membrane enabled the scientists to infer the possible structure of plasma membrane. The plasma membrane of the RBC consists of a complex, well-ordered group of lipids and proteins stretched over the outer surface of the cell in the form of a lipid bilayer punctuated by penetrating or attached proteins.

1112432.explanation: The fluid mosaic model explains both structural and functional aspects of cell membrane. Fluid mosaic model explains various observations regarding the structure of functional cell membranes. The model, which was devised by S. J. Singer and G. L. Nicolson in 1972, describes the cell membrane as a two-dimensional liquid that restricts the lateral diffusion of membrane component.

1112434.explanation:
Centromere is divided into four types on the basis of the relative position of centromere. These are metacentric, submetacentric, telocentric, and acrocentric.



 Metacentric chromosomes have the centromere in the centre, such that both sections are of equal length. Human chromosome 1 and 3 are metacentric.
 Submetacentric chromosomes have the centromere slightly offset from the centre leading to a slight asymmetry in the length of the two sections. Human chromosomes 4 through 12 are submetacentric.
 Acrocentric chromosomes have a centromere which is severely offset from the centre leading to one very long and one very short section. Human chromosomes 13, 15, 21, and 22 are acrocentric.
 Telocentric chromosomes have the centromere at the very end of the chromosome. Humans do not possess telocentric chromosomes, but they are found in other species such as mice.

1112436.explanation: Meiosis is the cell division process that occurs in the gamete cells and results in daughter cells that contain half the amount of genetic information (genes) than a body cell. Gamete cells are the cells found in the ova and sperm. Once fused at fertilisation, the resulting embryonic cell contains the total number of genes needed for the development of the foetus (half from the ovum and half from the sperm).

1112439.explanation: Saturated fatty acids (SFA) contain no double bonds and have general formula R-COOH in which the R-group is a straight-chain hydrocarbon of the form CH3(CH2)n with varying length ranging from short chain length (volatile liquids) to chain lengths of 30 or more carbon atoms (waxy solids), though the most common and important fatty acids, found in many different plant and animal fats, contain between 12 and 22 carbon atoms.

1112440.explanation: ER functions as cytoskeleton or skeletal framework by providing mechanical support to colloidal cytoplasmic matrix. It conducts information from cell to cell. RER helps in protein synthesis. SER takes part in detoxification of toxic chemicals in liver.

1112441.explanation: The beta-pleated sheet is an example of secondary structure of protein. $\beta$ pleated sheet is formed by hydrogen bonds between protein strands, rather than within a strand. The beta sheet is stabilised by hydrogen bonds between the carbonyl oxygen of an amino acid in one strand and the backbone nitrogen of a second amino acid in another strand.

1112445.explanation: Cotyledons and testa respectively are edible parts in ground nut and pomegranate. Cotyledon is an embryonic leaf in seedbearing plants, one or more of which are the first leaves to appear from a germinating seed. Testa is the outer layer of seed coat. Itis thick, hard and leathery whereas tegmen is the inner layer of seed coat which is thin and papery.

1112446.explanation: Association between roots of higher plants and fungal hyphae is called mycorrhiza. Both the organisms are benefitted in this relationship. The fungal hyphae take nutrition from the plant and in return increase surface area for absorption of water and minerals for the plant Mycorrhizas are found in the roots of Pinus and between roots of higher plants.

1112447.explanation: Cell wall is a very tough, flexible, and rigid layer that surrounds the cell membrane. Cell wall determines the shape of the cells and provides a strong structural support to prevent the bacterium from bursting or collapsing.

1112451.explanation: Keel (enclosing stamens and pistil) is the characteristic feature of flower of family Papilionaceae, e.g., bean, gram, pea etc. These flowers have butterfly-shaped corolla (called papilionaceous corolla).

1112452.explanation: The given figure shows anaphase I of meiosis. In anaphase I, the homologous chromosomes break apart while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromere. At the end of anaphase I, two groups of chromosomes are produced at two poles, having half the number of parental chromosomes.

1112453.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose

1112458.explanation: Notochord is a mesodermally [the middle layer of cells or tissues of an embryo, or the parts derived from this (e.g. cartilage, muscles, and bone)] derived rod-like structure formed on the dorsal side [posterior] during embryonic development in some animals. Animals with notochord are called chordates and those animals which do not form this structure are called non-chordates, e.g., Porifera to Echinoderms.

1112459.explanation: In some organisms karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis because of which multinucleate condition arises leading to the formation of syncytium (e.g., liquid endosperm in coconut).

1112460.explanation: The given figure A and B represent late anaphase and prophase respectively. Late anaphase is the stage of cell division in which the doubled set of chromosomes separates into two identical groups that move to opposite ends of the cell. In mitosis, anaphase is preceded by metaphase and followed by telophase. In case of prophase the chromosomes become visible as paired chromatids and the nuclear envelope disappears. It is the first stage of cell division of mitosis.

1112464.explanation: Cell walls are found outside the plasma membrane of a cell.

1112465.explanation: When stamens are attached to the petals, they are epipetalous as in brinjal, or epiphyllous when attached to the perianth as in the flowers of lily.

1112466.explanation: Essential fatty acids are linoleic, arachidonic acid and linolenic acid. All essential fatty acids are unsaturated, however all unsaturated fatty acids are not essential, e.g., oleic acid and palmitoleic acid can be synthesised in the body and are thus not essential in the diet.

1112469.explanation: The correct order of mitotic events which occur during meiosis is: Formation of synaptonemal complex, recombination, separation of homologous chromosomes, separation of sister chromatids.

1112470.explanation: The mitochondrion is a double membrane-bound organelle which contains outer and inner membranes composed of phospholipid bilayers and proteins. The two membranes have different properties.

1112472.explanation: Organisms of prokaryotes will get benefit in absence of fungi.

1112476.explanation: Monadelphous used for the androecium in a flower of china rose (Hibiscus rosasinensis), Achyranthes, etc. China rose of malvaceae family possess numerous stamens. In monadelphous condition, all filaments become fused and form a group, while other remain free.

1112478.explanation: Glyoxysomes is a specialised form of peroxisome (a type of microbody) found in some plant cells, notably the cells of germinating oil seeds. It contains the enzymes of the glyoxylate cycle - a variant of the citric acid cycle by way of which stored lipids are converted to carbohydrates.

1112479.explanation: Food synthesis by a process called photosynthesis is performed by chloroplast (a type of plastid). Endomembrane system is a grouping of some membrane bound organelles which function in close coordination with one another. Golgi complex, ER, Iysosomes, and vacuole form endomembrane system. Other organelles, viz., plastids, mitochondria, peroxisomes, etc., do not coordinate and thus are not a part of endomembrane system.

1112481.explanation: The number of chromosomes will be same (50), but each chromosome will have 2 chromatids.

1112484.explanation: Spindle is microtubular apparatus that appears in many eukaryotic cells at the beginning of nuclear division and is responsible for the ordered separation of the chromosomes; chromosomes are attached to the spindle fibres by their centromeres. Two types of spindle fibres can be distinguished as the interpolar fibre, which stretches continuously from pole to pole of the spindle; the kinetochore fibre, which stretches from the pole to the centromere (kinetochore) of an individual chromosome. The mechanism by which the chromosomes move, and the spindle fibres contract remains unclear. Cells of animals and lower plants possess centrioles, which act as organiser regions for spindle microtubule formation, but centrioles are absent from the cells of higher plants.

1112488.explanation: This drug would mostly affect the tertiary structure of proteins. Primary structure is defined by the peptide bonds between amino acids. These bonds occur between the amino and carboxy termini of two respective amino acids. Secondary structure is largely defined by characteristic folding patterns such as the $\alpha$ -helix and $\beta$ -sheet. These are stabilized by hydrogen bonds between main chain carbonyl oxygens and amide hydrogens. The tertiary structure is the 3D shape of the amino acid, which is stabilized by various interactions and forces within the folded polypeptide chain. Disulfide bonds are unique to the tertiary structure, which provide a strong, stable bond between the sulphur atoms of two cysteines in a protein.

1112491.explanation: The given shows the reticulate venation in which the veinlets are randomly arranged and form a complex network of veinlets, e.g., dicotyledonous plants like a rose plant.

1112493.explanation: At prophase I DNA replication has already occurred, and the original amount of DNA has been doubled to x. At anaphase I. The amount of DNA in the cell remains the same because no cytokinesis has occurred yet to separate the cytoplasm.

1112494.explanation: According to the endosymbiotic theory, prokaryotes entered eukaryotic cells and eventually evolved into the mitochondria and chloroplasts found in eukaryotic cells today.

1112496.explanation:
Statements - (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) are not correct.



 Calyx and corolla are helping or accessory whorls whereas androecium and gynoecium are reproductive organs of a flower.
 Actinomorphic flowers can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane and zygomorphic flowers can be divided into two similar halves in one plane.
 Flowers without bracts are termed as ebracteate and flowers with bract, reduced leaf found at the base of the pedicel are called as bracteates.
 Parthenocarpic fruit is formed without fertilization of the ovary.

1112500.explanation: Golgi apparatus is an organelle present in most eukaryotic cells. It is made up of membrane-bound sacs, and is also called a Golgi body, Golgi complex, or dictyosome. The job of the Golgi apparatus is to process and bundle macromolecules like proteins and lipids as they are synthesised within the cell.

1112502.explanation: ER (endoplasmic reticulum) is of two types - SER (smooth endoplasmic reticulum) and RER (rough endoplasmic reticulum). RER has ribosome attached to its surface. Ribosomes on the rough endoplasmic reticulum are called 'membrane bound' and are responsible for the assembly of many proteins. This process is called translation.

1112505.explanation: Segregation of Mendelian factor (Aa) occurs during anaphase I. The paired homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis I so that each gamete receives one chromosome of each homologous pair. During anaphase I chromosome divides at the point of centromere or kinetochore and thus two sister chromatids are formed, which are called as chromosomes.

1112506.explanation: Proline plays a central role in the formation of alpha helices and beta sheets. While proline's unique structure may also disrupt both alpha helixes and beta sheets, its ability to make sharp turns facilitates the formation of both structures, with proline commonly being found at the beginning of alpha helices or at the turns in beta sheets.

1112508.explanation: In the given figure, the root tip shows their different regions marked as A, B and C. The correct labelling of A, B and C are region of maturation, region of elongation and region of meristematic activity respectively.

1112509.explanation: Cytokinesis is the division of protoplast of the cell into two daughter cells after the nuclear division or karyokinesis, so that each daughter cell comes to have its own nucleus. Cytokinesis is different in animal and plant cells. Cytokinesis in animal cells is of cleavage type. In plant cell, cytokinesis is of two types: cleavage and cell plate. Cleavage method of cytokinesis takes place in some lower plants. Cell plate method is a common method of cytokinesis in plant cells.

1112511.explanation: In anaerobic respiration, bacteria produce lactic acid.

1112512.explanation: The cell would normally proceed to mitosis without interruption once it has entered the M phase.

1112514.explanation: The ribosomes are classified on the basis of sedimentation coefficient in the centrifuge. It is measured as Svedberg unit (S). On the basis of sedimentation coefficient, they are 70S and 80S. Eukaryotic ribosomes are somewhat larger, 80S overall, with a 60S and a 40S subunit.

1112516.explanation: August Weismann in 1887 predicted that the number of chromosomes must be reduced by one half during gamete formation. The two divisions of meiosis are called the first and the second meiotic divisions. In meiosis I, the number of chromosomes is reduced from diploid to haploid condition, whereas in meiosis II, the two chromatids of each chromosomes separate from each other and go to separate daughter cells, as a result the number of chromosomes remains the same as produced by meiosis-I.

1112518.explanation: 'C' represents an enzyme under the effect of a non-competitive inhibitor [decreased Vmax - 'A' depicts the enzyme upon binding to an activator Vmax and 'B' shows the enzyme upon binding to a competitive inhibitor (Vmax is unchanged)].

1112519.explanation: In frog, there is present a cylindrical testis near each kidney, being suspended by mesorchium. There arise several thin vasa efferentia from each testis that emerges through mesorchium and join the uriniferous tubules of the posterior part of the kidney to opens into the Bidder's canal which in turn opens into the ureter.

1112520.explanation: Fasciola belongs to platyhelminthes. It is commonly known as 'Liver fluke' and is an endo-parasite in the bile duct of sheep. It is an acoelomate animal.

1112521.explanation: Mitotic anaphase differs from metaphase in possessing same number of chromosomes and half number of chromatids. During anaphase of mitosis, chromosomes divide at the point of centromere or kinetochore and thus two sister chromatids are formed. While during metaphase, chromosomes become maximally distinct due to further contraction and thus size of chromosomes is measured at mitotic metaphase.

1112522.explanation: Mitosis is a type of cell division by which eukaryotic cells multiply. This division results in two daughter cells and each having the same number and kind of chromosomes as the parent's cells have.

1112523.explanation: Glycoproteins are proteins that contain sugars like carbohydrates as prosthetic group. In most glycoproteins, the linkage is between asparagine and N-acetyl-D-glucosamine. Some glycoproteins are immunoglobulins, membrane proteins and muscle proteins. These are formed in Golgi apparatus in the process of glycosylation and are important components of plasma membrane in which they extend throughout the lipid bilayer. Lipoproteins are -protein complexed with lipids like triglycerides, phospholipids etc. Nucleoproteins are proteins associated with nucleic acids and chromoproteins are proteins associated with pigments, e.g. Cytochrome and phytochrome.

1112524.explanation: Chromosome is a thread-like structure of nucleic acids and protein found in the nucleus of most living cells, carrying genetic information in the form of genes.

1112525.explanation: Glycolipids and glycoproteins of plasma membrane facilitated the process of cell recognition and cell adhesion.

1112527.explanation: Metaphase is a stage of mitosis in the eukaryotic cell cycle in which chromosomes are at their most condensed and coiled stage. Metaphase is the best stage in mitosis for analysing the chromosomes and to study their morphology.

1112528.explanation: Jelly is deposited as a covering on the egg of the frog in the oviduct.

1112529.explanation: Ascus is a sac, typically cylindrical in shape, in which the spores of ascomycetes fungi develop. Basidium is a microscopic club-shaped spore-bearing structure produced by certain fungi. Euglena, Spirulina and sponges are the examples of protista, cyanobacteria and Animalia respectively.

1112530.explanation: A - Coleoptile; B - Coleorhiza; C - Radicle; D - Scutellum.

1112532.explanation: In cockroaches and prawn excretion of waste material occurs through Malpighian tubules and green glands respectively.

1112533.explanation: In the given structure of fungal cell, A is the cell wall. Fungal cell wall contains chitin along with other polysaccharides, proteins, etc. Chitin is a mucopolysaccharide and is also present in exoskeleton of insects and arthropods. In fungi, the reserve food material is present in the form of glycogen (shown by B) and oils. C represents mitochondrion. Fungi are chlorophyllous organisms and lack chloroplasts and photosynthetic pigments. D represents nucleus. Septate hyphae may be uni-or mutli-nucleate and aseptate hyphae are usually multinucleate (= coenocytic).

1112534.explanation: In animal cell cytokinesis involves the contraction of the contractile ring of microfilament. Contractile ring of microfilaments develops peripherally below die cell membrane in the equatorial region.

1112535.explanation: Lipid molecules of plasma membrane possess both polar hydrophilic (water loving) and on polar hydrophobic (water repelling) ends. The hydrophilic region occurs at outer surface whereas the hydrophobic region consists of two tails of fatty acids. Hydrophobic tails usually occur towards the centre of the membrane. It results in the formation of a lipid bilayer.

1112537.explanation:
During metaphase, the microtubules of the spindle (white) have attached and the chromosomes have lined up on the metaphase plate. The key features of metaphase are as follows:



 spindle fibres attach to kinetochores of chromosomes,
 chromosomes are moved to spindle equator and get aligned along metaphase plate through spindle fibres of both poles.

1112538.explanation: The $\alpha$ -helix and a $\beta$ -pleated sheet are types of secondary structure of proteins. In contrast to the alpha helix, hydrogen bonds in beta sheets form in between -NH groups in the backbone of one strand and C=O groups in the backbone of the adjacent strands. This is the main difference between Alpha Helix and Beta-Pleated Sheet.

1112550.explanation:
Dialysis is of two types: haemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis. Peritoneal dialysis uses a natural filter inside the body i.e., peritoneal membrane to remove wastes and extra fluid from the body.

The dialysis fluid fills the belly and pulls out wastes and extra fluid from the body. Blood is not removed from the body as in the case of hemodialysis.

1112558.explanation: The right and left hepatocyte ducts combine to form common hepatic duct and this common hepatic duct joins to the duct arising from gall bladder (cystic duct) and forms common bile duct. When the later joins to pancreatic duct, and the combination is called as hepatopancreatic duct or ampulla, which opens up into the duodenum and its opening is guarded by sphincter of Oddi.

1112560.explanation: The oxygen evolved from green plants during photosynthesis comes from water was proved by Ruben and Kamen by using the heavy isotope of oxygen (18O).

1112563.explanation: Cell elongation in internodal regions of the green plants takes place due to the presence of gibberellins. This process of the elongation of plant due to internodal growth is called bolting.

1112570.explanation: Competitive inhibition is a reversible inhibition where inhibitor competes with the normal substrate for the active site of enzyme. It fits into the active site of an enzyme and binds with it. The enzyme now cannot act upon the substrate and reaction products are not formed, e.g., the activity of succinate dehydrogenase is inhibited by malonate. Km value or Michaelis constant is defined as the substrate concentration at which half of the enzyme molecules are forming an enzyme-substrate (ES) complex, or the concentration of the substrate when the velocity of the enzyme reaction is half the maximal possible. A smaller Km value indicates greater affinity of the enzyme for its substrate and, hence, shows a quicker reaction. The competitive inhibitor decreases the affinity of the enzyme for substrate, thus increasing the Km value.

1112572.explanation: Phototropism is the growth of an organism which responds to a light stimulus. It is most often observed in plants but can also occur in other organisms such as fungi. The cells on the plant that are farthest from the light have a chemical called auxin that reacts when phototropism occurs.

1112575.explanation: Endomembrane system is a grouping of some membrane organelles which function in close coordination with one another, viz., nuclear membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes vacuoles, and cell membrane. Functions of other organelles are not coordinated. They are not part of endomembrane system, e.g., plastids, mitochondria, peroxisomes, glyoxysomes, etc.

1112580.explanation: The energy released by oxidation in respiration is not directly used, but its stored as ATP. Which is broken down whenever energy needs to be utilised.

1112581.explanation: An allosteric binding site is separate from the active site. When it is occupied by a ligand, it undergoes an induced fit which affects the shape of the active site. This will affect the ability of the active site to 'recognize' the substrate and hence affect enzyme activity. Both the active site and allosteric binding site are likely to contain amino acids with aliphatic side chains, some of which may be important to the binding process. The ability of a binding site to accept a wide variety of differently shaped molecules will vary depending on the specific binding site involved.

1112582.explanation: Brunner's glands are branched tubular glands and are confined to the duodenum. They secrete alkaline watery fluid that neutralises the acidic chyme leaving the stomach, a little enzyme and mucus. They are named after Swiss anatomist J. C. von Brunner.

1112586.explanation: The citric acid cycle provides most of the electron carriers for the electron transport chain.

1112589.explanation: The movement of three protons through F0 channel of ATPase results in the formation of one ATP molecule.

1112590.explanation: Aerobic respiration is more advantageous than anaerobic respiration because it produces more energy.

1112591.explanation: In CAM plants, initial and final carboxylation are temporally separated. During night, PEP carboxylase in the mesophyll cells fixes CO2 in the form of malic acid which is stored in vacuoles. During day, malic acid is de-carboxylated to release CO2 which then enters C3 cycle.

1112598.explanation: In meiotic cells, homologous chromosomes synapse during zygotene. During zygotene, the two homologous chromosomes get attached to each other laterally due to development of nucleoprotein between them. It is like nucleoprotein core present between two chromatids of a chromosome. Pairing is such that the genes of the same character present on the two homologous chromosomes come to lie exactly opposite. The process of attachment of the homologous chromosomes is known as synapsis or syndesis.

1112599.explanation: Mitochondria are called the powerhouse of cell. It makes most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), a molecule that cells use as a source of energy.

1112601.explanation: Wheat is a C3 plant so the primary CO2 acceptor in it is RuBP.

1112603.explanation:
In vascular plants especially the taller ones, if the apical bud is intact and growing of the lateral bud remains suppressed, removal of apical bud causes fast growth of lateral buds. This influence of apical bud in suppressing the growth of lateral buds is termed as apical dominance.

Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) is a natural auxin which is responsible for apical dominance. GA is Gibberellic acid cause's rapid elongation growth. ABA (abscisic acid) is a powerful growth inhibitor. Florigen is a chemical involved in flowering.

1112609.explanation: The correct sequence of formation of given intermediates of Kreb's cycle are as follows: Succinate $\rightarrow$ Fumarate $\rightarrow$ Malate $\rightarrow$ OAA

1112611.explanation: Light is essential for photosynthesis. The amount of photosynthesis depends upon the quality, intensity and duration of light.

1112616.explanation: In meiosis, chromosomes exchange genetic material.

1112619.explanation: In electron transport chain, there are 7 electron acceptors, which are as follows Co-Q $\rightarrow$ Cyt b $\rightarrow$ Cyt c1 $\rightarrow$ Cyt C $\rightarrow$ Cyt a $\rightarrow$ Cyt a3 $\rightarrow$ O2. Oxygen is the ultimate electron acceptor. These electron acceptors are present in a specific sequence along inner mitochondrial membrane.

1112622.explanation: A protein structure that forms between homologous chromosomes during meiosis is synaptonemal complex (SC). Synaptonemal complex is a highly ordered proteinaceous structure that assembles at the interface between aligned homologous chromosomes during meiotic prophase. The SC has been demonstrated to function both in stabilisation of homolog pairing and in promoting the formation of interhomolog crossovers (COs).

1112623.explanation: Chlorophylls are green, xanthophylls are yellow and carotenes are orange pigments.

1112625.explanation: RuBP carboxylase or RuBisCO is the most abundant enzyme.

1112627.explanation:
Zeatin is a cytokinin derived from adenine. Zeatin was discovered in immature com kernels from the genus Zea. Being a growth promoting plant hormone, it promotes growth of lateral buds and when sprayed on meristems it stimulates cell division to produce bushier plants.

IAA or indole acetic acid is a natural auxin whereas IBA (indole butyric acid) or NAA (naphthalene acetic acid) are synthetic auxin.

1112629.explanation: For the start of respiration, a living cell requires glucose and oxygen.

1112634.explanation: Chloroplast is a vesicle, bound by an envelope of two-unit membranes and filled with a fluid matrix called stroma. The lamellae, after separation from the inner membrane, usually take the form of closed, flattened, ovoid sacs, the thylakoids, which lie closely packed in piles, the grana.

1112635.explanation: Ribosomes are sub-microscopic polypeptide manufacturing naked granular nucleo protein organelles. Each ribosome consists of two subunits: one larger and the other smaller. The subunits occur separately in the cytoplasm and join to form ribosomes only at the time of protein synthesis. Mitochondria, chloroplast, and endoplasmic reticulum consist of membranes.

1112641.explanation: ChI b, carotene and xanthophyll are called accessory pigments. They absorb light and transfer the energy to chlorophyll a.

1112643.explanation: Emerson found that two separate groups of pigments or photosystems work in photosynthesis. Photosystem I (PS I) absorbs long red wavelengths and photosystem II absorbs wavelengths shorter than 690 nm.

1112645.explanation: Z-scheme involves both PS I and PS II. Electrons released from photolysis of H2O are picked up by reaction centre of PS II. The chlorophyll a in the reaction centre of PS II absorbs light of 680 nm wavelength and excites electrons. The excited electrons are passed by a series of electron acceptors in a sequence - Pheophytin, Plastoquinone (PQ), Fe-S complex, Cytochrome b6-f complex and plastocyanin. The movement of electrons is downhill, in terms of an oxidation-reduction or redox potential scale. From plastocyanin, the electrons are passed on to the pigments of PS I. At the same time, the chlorophyll a in the reaction centre of PS I absorbs 700 nm wavelength and electrons get excited. The excited electrons pass downhill through a series of acceptors which are, modified chlorophyll a, Fe-S proteins, Ferredoxin and finally to NADP+. NADP reductase combines NADP+ with H+ to form NADPH.

1112646.explanation: The given figures show the stages of meiosis I. A, B, C, and D are respectively prophase I, metaphase II, anaphase III and telophase IV. Prophase I is a long process during which homologous chromosomes par closely and interchange heredity material. This phase is divided into five substages. These are leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, and diakinesis. During zygotene stage, homologous chromosomes are brought together through synaptonemal complex.

1112647.explanation: Enzymes work by binding to the substrate and stabilizing the transition state, which lowers the activation energy required for the reaction to proceed. This increases the rate of the reaction.

1112651.explanation: Adrenal gland, located on top of each kidney, does not involve in the process of digestion. It is an endocrine gland which secretes hormones like adrenaline and the steroids aldosterone and cortisol. Liver is involved in the process of digestion by secreting bile which helps in the emulsification of fats. Pancreas secretes digestive juices containing many digestive enzymes. It plays an essential role in converting the food we eat into fuel for the body's cells.

1112652.explanation: During meiosis, genetic information is exchanged between the maternally and paternally inherited copies of a pair of chromosomes to create new combinations of genes. This process of genetic recombination helps to increase genetic variability within a species. It allows for the transmission of virtually limitless combinations of genes from parent to offspring. The resulting gametes have 23 new chromosomes, one member of each of the 23 pairs, representing unique combinations of the original maternal and paternal copies.

1112655.explanation: Enolase works on 2-pbosphoglyceric acid (3C-compound), aconitase on citric acid (6C-compound), fumarase on fumaric acid (4C-compound) and alcohol dehydrogenase on acetaldehyde (2C-compound). Thus, increasing order of these enzymes based on the carbon number of the substrates on which they act is - IV, I, III, and II.

1112657.explanation: Iron and magnesium are essential for chlorophyll synthesis. Correcting the nutrient deficiency will restore the green color of the leaves, improve photosynthesis, and ultimately increase seed yield.

1112659.explanation: The temperature dependence of biological membrane is affected by the lipid composition of the membrane. Low temperatures can cause a membrane to enter a gel-like phase with very high membrane-lipid viscosity, whereas high temperatures can cause a membrane to become 'hyper fluid' with very little viscosity. The greater the proportion of unsaturated carbon - carbon bonds (double-bonds) in a lipid's fatty acid molecules, the easier solidification of it occurs, in cold temperature and thus the lesser the changes in plants membrane at lower temperature.

1112661.explanation: The growth of the leaf is measured in term of surface area.

1112664.explanation: In non-competitive inhibition, the Km of the reaction stays constant while the Vmax will decrease with increased amounts of inhibition. Therefore, inhibition that does not alter Km, must be non-competitive inhibition.

1112665.explanation: A-Principal director of macromolecular traffic (Golgi bodies) B-Site of oxidative phosphorylation (Mitochondria) C-Intracellular transport (ER) D-Site of phosphorylation (Chloroplast) E-Storage of cell sap.

1112667.explanation: Both ATP and NADPH are synthesized during non-cyclic photophosphorylation.

1112670.explanation: Centriole is a small, cylindrical cellorganelle, seen near the nucleusin the cytoplasm of most eukaryotic cells. It is made of rnicrotubules which exists as part of the centrosome, which helps organise microtubules in the body.

1112677.explanation: Carmine (or acetocarmine) is a classic dye used specifically for staining chromosomes. It binds to DNA and provides excellent contrast, making it ideal for visualizing chromosomes during mitosis or meiosis.

1112681.explanation: Vitamin A (retinol) is a fat-soluble vitamin that cannot be synthesised by mammals and other vertebrates and must be provided in the diet. It is a constituent of the visual pigment rhodopsin. Deficiency affects the eyes, causing night blindness.

1112683.explanation: The small bubbles formed around the green parts of an aquatic plant in bright sunlight in the experiment performed by Jan Ingenhousz were of oxygen.

1112687.explanation: ABA is produced in many parts of green plants. Its presence is suspicious in lower plants (bryophytes and pteridophytes). ABA is formed by melvonic acid pathway, not by glycolysis.

1112688.explanation: In diplotene stage of meiosis I, the chromosomes mayunfold to nearly normal form and start transcription of mRNA and rRNA to build up food reserves in the cytoplasm. This process is most pronounced in the primary oocytes of amphibians, reptiles and birds. In some species, the chromosomes enlarge greatly, assuming lamp brush form.

1112689.explanation: Ground tissue system includes all the tissues of plant body except epidermal tissue system and vascular tissues. It forms the bulk of body and consists of mainly parenchymatous, collenchymatous, sclerenchymatous, glandular and laticiferous tissues. It can be divided into three types based on the nature of the cell walls.

1112693.explanation:
During Kreb's or citric acid cycle, substrate level phosphorylation occurs during the conversion of succinyl CoA to succinic acid. Succinyl CoA is acted upon by enzyme succinyl CoA synthetase to form succinate (a 4C compound). The reaction releases sufficient energy to form ATP(in plants) or GTP (in animals) by substrate level phosphorylation. GTP can form ATP through a coupled reaction.

Succinyl CoA + GDP/ADP + H3PO4 $\overset{\mathrm{Succinyl}\;\mathrm{CoA}}{\underset{\mathrm{synthetase}}\rightleftharpoons}$ Succinate + CoA + GTP/ATP

1112695.explanation: The proper designation of the complex of SAM and its enzyme together is the holoenzyme. A holoenzyme describes the complex of an enzyme that has its cofactor bound and is considered 'complete'. A cofactor is a non-protein chemical compound bound to an enzyme to assist in catalysis. A coenzyme is a specific type of cofactor that carries chemical groups between enzymes, like methyl groups.

1112697.explanation:
In the given figure of T.s. of dicot root, the parts marked as A, B, C, D, E and F are respectively cortex, epiblema, pith, endodermis, root hairs and pericycle. Dicot root consists of a single layer of epiblema which bears unicellular root hairs. Endodermis is followed by one or more layers of pericycle. Inner to pericycle lies radially arranged vascular bundles. This arrangement keeps the xylem bundles in direct contact with the outer tissue of the roots which conduct water absorbed by root hairs to the inside. Xylem is exarch.

Casparian strip is present in endodermis. Endodermis is the innermost layer of the cortex, consisting of a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without any intercellular spaces. The tangential as well as radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of water impermeable, waxy material suberin-in the form of casparian strips.

1112699.explanation: Abscisic acid is a hormone which is produced during adverse environmental condition. It also causes the closure of stomata under conditions of water stress as also under high concentration of CO, in the guard cells. Abscisic acid inhibits the K+ uptake by guard cells and promotes the leakage of malic acid. It results in reduction of osmotically active solutes so that the guard cells become flaccid and stomata get closed.

1112701.explanation: The parts A and B of chloroplast are the thylakoid and stroma respectively. Thylakoid is involved in light reaction and stroma is involved in dark reaction.

1112703.explanation: C4 plants have an alternative CO2 fixation pathway (Hatch and Slack pathway) in which two carboxylation reactions occur- first in mesophyll chloroplasts by PEP carboxylase and the second in bundle sheath chloroplast by RuBisCO.

1112705.explanation: Photosystem I absorbs light independent of Photosystem II. Plastocyanin reduces photooxidised P700 in PS I. Electrons released from splitting of water reduces photo-oxidised P680 in PS II. Electrons excited from P680 in photosystem II are replaced with electrons from water.

1112706.explanation: Lamp brush chromosomes are a special form of chromosome found in the growing oocytes (immature eggs) of most animals, except mammals. They were first described by Walther Fleming in 1882. Lamp brush chromosomes of tailed and tailless amphibians, birds and insects are described best of all. They are present during the prolonged prophase of the first meiotic division.

1112707.explanation: Stele means 'pillar'. It is the central core of the stem and root of a vascular plant, consisting of the vascular tissue (xylem and phloem) and associated supporting tissue. It consists of pericycle, vascular bundles(xylem and phloem) and pith (if present).

1112709.explanation: The approximate total yield of ATP that is produced via the Kreb's cycle from a single molecule of acety1 CoA is 10 molecules of ATP.

1112712.explanation: Letter 'C' is represented by substrate. Substrate is a molecule upon which an enzyme acts. Enzymes catalyse chemical reactions involving the substrate(s). In the case of a single substrate, the substrate bonds with the enzyme active site, and an enzyme-substrate complex is formed.

1112717.explanation: In the process of glycolysis, when 3 - phosphoglyceraIdehyde (PGAL) is converted to 1,3 - bisphosphyglycerate (BPGA), NADH + H+ is formed from NAD+. This reaction is called oxidative dehydrogenation.

1112723.explanation: C4 pathway (Hatch and Slack pathway) involves carboxylation reactions - first in mesophyll chloroplasts by PEP carboxylase and the second in bundle sheath chloroplasts by RuBisCO. In CAM plants, two carboxylation reactions occur at different times. During night, PEP carboxylase in the mesophyll cells fixes CO2 in the form of malic acid which is stored in vacuoles. During day, malic acid is de-carboxylated to release CO2 which then enters C3 cycle.

1112724.explanation: Meiosis is a double division which occurs in a diploid cell and gives rise to four haploid cells, each having half the number of chromosomes as compared to parent cells. It occurs in the cell that produce gametes in sexually reproducing organisms. Reduction division is known as meiosis, gametes formed from this division is called meiogametes.

1112727.explanation: Auxanometer is an instrument which measures the growth in the length of a plant organ. More common auxanometer is arc or lever auxanometer, and automatic auxanometer.

1112729.explanation: Auxin is produced by growing apical part of the plant, i.e., apices of stems and roots. Then, it goes to the lateral parts (basipetal) and causes, the apical (root and shoot) parts of the plant to elongate.

1112730.explanation: Modern detergents contain enzyme preparation of alkaline protease which is called alkaliphile, for removing protein stains.

1112731.explanation: Paper chromatography is the technique used to separate photosynthetic pigments.

1112735.explanation:
The layers labelled as A, B, C, and D in the given figure are mucosa, submucosa, muscularis, and serosa respectively. Mucosa consists of an epithelium that is in direct contact with the lumen and is supported by areolar connective tissue containing a few smooth muscle cells. The epithelium is often folded to increase the surface area that is in contact with food. The mucosa has different functions in different parts of the alimentary canal. In some regions, it secretes only mucus, which protects underlying cells. In others, it secretes mucus and digestive secretions containing enzymes and absorbs nutrients.

Mucosa contains specialised goblet cells that secrete sticky mucus throughout the gastrointestinal tract. On the mucosa layer, small fingerlike projections called villi and microvilli help to increase surface area for nutrient absorption.

1112737.explanation: A simple sugar, glucose, is formed as the first substance by green plants during photosynthesis. Starch is synthesised later from glucose.

1112740.explanation: Each photosystem has a pair of specific chlorophyll a as reaction centre surrounded by light-harvesting complexes (LHCs) or antennae formed by chlorophyll b, carotenoids, and other photosynthetic pigments, with associated proteins.

1112741.explanation: Wavelength of 620-750 run of visible spectrum is red light.

1112742.explanation: Enzyme functions as catalysts by lowering the activation energy.

1112743.explanation: Monocot root possesses polyarch condition of vascular bundles with a well-developed pith.

1112747.explanation:
The first 5 carbon dicarboxylic acid in Kreb's cycle is $\alpha$ -ketoglutaric acid. The $\alpha$ -ketoglutarate that accumulates when $\alpha$ -ketoglutarate dehydrogenase is inhibited can be used in nitrogen metabolism as a precursor for several amino acids and the purine bases.

 $\alpha$ -ketoglutarate $\rightarrow$ Glutamate $\rightarrow$ Other amino acids $\rightarrow$ Purines.

 $\alpha$ -ketoglutarate of Kreb's cycle produces an important amino acid called glutamate on amination.

1112751.explanation:
The ratio of the volume of CO2 liberated to the volume of oxygen absorbed per molecule during respiration is called respiratory quotient (RQ). The value of RQ indicates the types of respiratory substrate.

RQ = Volume of CO2 evolved/Volume of O2 conswned

RQ = $\frac {102}{145}$ 

RQ = 0.7

1112757.explanation: Respiration is an energy liberating enzymatically controlled multistep catabolic process of stepwise breakdown of organic substances (commonly hexose sugar glucose) inside the living cells. The final electron acceptor in respiration is oxygen

1112759.explanation: Photosynthesis completes in two phases depending on the requirement of light: Photochemical phase and Biosynthetic phase. Biochemical phase or light reaction of photosynthesis occurs in the presence of light in the thylakoid membrane of chloroplast.

1112760.explanation: Meiosis takes place in reproductive organs. It results in formation of gametes with half the normal chromosome number. Young anthers are the best material to study meiosis.

1112766.explanation: The complex V of ETS of mitochondrial membrane is ATP synthase, which has a head piece, stalk, and a base piece. Out of these, the head piece is identified as the coupling factor-1 (F1), stalk portion is necessary for binding F1 to inner mitochondrial membrane and base piece is isolated as F0 and present within the inner mitochondrial membrane.

1112769.explanation: In the given figure of dicot stem, the parts marked as A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H and I are respectively epidermal hair, epidermis, hypodermis, parenchyma, endodermis, pericycle, vascular bundle, medullary rays and medulla or pith. Dicot stems with primary growth have pith in the centre, with vascular bundles forming a distinct ring visible when the stem is viewed in cross-section. The outside of the stem is covered with an epidermis, which is covered by a waterproof cuticle. A cortex consisting of hypodermis (collenchyma cells) and endodermis(starch containing cells) is present above the pericycle and vascular bundles. Vascular bundles are conioint, collateral and open. Cambium helps in secondary growth.

1112772.explanation: Kupffer cells, also known as stellate macrophages and Kupffer-Browicz cells, are specialised macrophages located in the liver, lining the walls of the sinusoids. They form part of the mononuclear phagocyte system.

1112775.explanation: Arithmetic growth is linear because in this type of growth, there is a sequential adding of the new cells. One daughter cell remains meristematic (dividing), while the other becomes mature and gets differentiated to perform special function.

1112995.explanation: Water is a polar solvent, well known for interacting with polar molecules. The polarity of a given molecule helps determine its solubility in water. Molecules which are water-insoluble, or those which cannot form hydrogen bonds, tend to cluster together tightly to minimize their exposure to water. These molecules are typically hydrophobic. Single molecules within the aqueous human plasma are water soluble, so molecules within it tend to be water soluble. Thus, albumin must have a more polar outer layer. Aquaporins allow water to flow through them by encouraging transient hydrogen bonds to form in the lumen of the channel. Aquaporins are also embedded in the very hydrophobic lipid bilayer of the plasma membrane. Therefore, Aquaporins must have a hydrophobic, nonpolar outer layer, but a polar core. Albumin has a more non-polar core with a polar outer layer, while aquaporins have a more polar core with a nonpolar outer layer.

1113038.explanation: Phospholipids, cholesterol, and galactolipids are the main lipid components of the plasma membrane. Proportion of these components varies in different cell membranes. According to fluid mosaic model of cell membrane, lipid molecules are present in viscous bilayer and protein molecules occur at places both inside and on outer side the lipid bilayer. Intrinsic or integral proteins are insoluble in water solutions and are associated with lipids. They attach to oligosaccharides to form glycoproteins. They pass into the lipid bilayer to different depths and establish hydrophobic bonds with lipid molecules. Some of the integral proteins run throughout the lipid bilayer. The extrinsic or peripheral proteins are superficially present on the two surfaces of the membrane, more on the cytosolic face than on the external face. Peripheral proteins are separated by mild treatment with high ionic strength or with metal chelating agents, are soluble in aqueous solution and are usually free of lipids, for example, spectrin.

1113056.explanation: The reduction of activity of succinate dehydrogenase by malonate is an example of competitive inhibition. Competitive inhibition is a reversible inhibition where inhibitor competes with the normal substrate for the active site of enzyme. A competitive inhibitor is usually like the normal substrate and, therefore, fits into the active site of an enzyme and binds with it. The enzyme now cannot act upon the substrate and reaction products are not formed. Hence, the action of an enzyme may be reduced or inhibited. Since a competitive inhibitor occupies the site only temporarily, the enzyme action is not permanently affected. Thus, addition of a lot of succinate can reverse the inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate.

1113098.explanation: The hormone which reduces transpiration rate by inducing stomatal closure is ABA. ABA is a stress hormone which is synthesised by plant during drought or other stressful environmental condition. It causes rapid movement of potassium ions out of the guard cells, closes stomatal apertures, and thus reduces the rate of transpiration.

1113099.explanation: Photorespiration is a wasteful process as there is loss of photosynthetically fixed carbon and no energy rich compounds are formed. Photorespiration does not occur in C4 plants. C4 plants are photosynthetically efficient than C3 plants.

1113101.explanation: Alcoholic fermentation is a process in which molecules such as glucose etc. are converted into cellular energy and thereby produce ethanol and carbon dioxide as metabolic waste products. During alcoholic fermentation, NAD+ is produced when acetaldehyde is reduced to ethanol.

1113102.explanation: Usable energy of respiration is trapped in ATP molecules.

1113103.explanation:
In glycolysis, two molecules of ATP are consumed during two phosphorylation reactions to form fructose 1,6 -biphosphate. In return four molecules of ATP are produced by substrate level phosphorylation (conversion of 1,3 -biphosphoglycerate to 3 - phosphoglycerate, and phosphoenol pyruvate to pyruvate). Two molecules of NADH2 are formed at the time of oxidation of glyceraldehyde 3 - phosphate to 1,3 - biphosphoglycerate. The net reaction of glycolysis is as follows:

Glucose + 2NAD+ + 2ADP + 2H3PO4 $\rightarrow$ 2 Pyruvate + 2NADH + 2H+ + 2ATP

Each NADH is equivalent to 3 ATP, so the net gain in glycolysis is 8 ATP.

1113108.explanation: Sieve tubes are suited for translocation of food because they possess broader lumen and perforated cross walls. Sieve tubes are elongated tubular conducting channels of phloem. The end wall possesses many small pores and have thin cellulosic wall.

1113111.explanation: During photorespiration, RuBP, instead of CO2, binds with O2 and splits into one molecule of 3-phosphoglyceric acid (3C) and 2-phosphoglycolic acid (2C). Phosphate group of 2-phosphoglycolic acid is removed to form glycolic acid. Glycolic acid is then transported to peroxisome where it is converted into glycine which is then transported to mitochondrion. In mitochondrion, glycine is converted into serine with release of one CO2 molecule.

1113112.explanation: Kinetochores are assembled at the centromere of each chromosome and are the sites where microtubules attach to segregate the chromosomes. In meiosis there is only one fused kinetochore per chromosome, in mitosis there are two kinetochores per chromosome.

1113113.explanation:
Prosthetic group is a tightly bound, specific non polypeptide unit required for the biological function of some proteins. The prosthetic group may be organic (such as a vitamin, sugar, or lipid) or inorganic (such as a metal ion) but is not composed of amino acids. The complete conjugate enzyme, consisting of an apoenzyme and a cofactor, is called a holoenzyme. An active site is formed jointly by apoenzyme and cofactor. Co-factor is small, heat-stable part of a conjugate enzyme.

It may be classified into three types:



 Prosthetic group-Organic compounds tightly bound to apoenzyme.
 Co-enzyme-Organic compounds transiently (usually occur only during the course of catalysis) bound to apoenzyme.
 Metal ions-A number of metal ions join co-ordination bonds with side chains at the active site.

1113114.explanation: C3 cycle occurs in all photosynthetic plants in a cyclic manner and involves three stages: carboxylation, reduction and regeneration of RuBP.

1113116.explanation: Both chloroplasts and mitochondria possess a great degree of functional autonomy. They have their own DNA that shows both replication and transcription (production of RNA). The DNA of these organelles is inherited by the offspring via the cytoplasm of gametes. For example, human mitochondrial DNA is passed from generation to generation through the maternal line in the ovum.

1113117.explanation: Crescograph is a sensitive devise, devised by J.C. Bose. It records primary growth very accurately. It magnifies growth up to 10,000 times giving information of growth per second.

1113121.explanation: Respirometer is an instrument used for measuring rate of respiration and respiratory quotients.

1113124.explanation: The large intestine absorbs water and contains many symbiotic bacteria that aid in the breaking down of wastes to extract some small amounts of nutrients. The liver carries out many important functions, such as making important blood proteins and bile, changing food into energy, and cleaning alcohol and poisons from the blood. The acidic environment of the stomach does not allow bacterial growth.

1113125.explanation: Holoenzyme is conjugated enzyme which consists of a protein part called apoenzyme and a non-protein called cofactor. Coenzymes are also organic compounds but their association with apoenzyme is only transient and acts as cofactors.

1113126.explanation: Enamel is the hardest substance of the toot structure. It is the outermost layer which covers the crown. It is composed primarily of minerals in the form of hydroxyapatite crystals. Due to highly mineralised, enamel is hard but brittle.

1113127.explanation: When an enzyme binds to the appropriate substrate, subtle changes in the active site occur. This alteration of the active site is known as an induced-fit. Induced-fit enhances catalysis, as the enzyme converts substrate to product.

1113128.explanation: Electrons released from splitting of water reduces photo-oxidised P680 in PS II.

1113129.explanation: Succulents growing in arid conditions such as Agave, Opuntia, Sedum, and Aloe have evolved Crassulacean acid metabolism to carry out photosynthesis without the loss of water.

1113130.explanation: The absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b show that chlorophyll a gives absorption peaks at 430 nm and 662 nm, while chlorophyll b gives peaks at 453 nm and 642 nm. So, they absorb maximum light in the blue and red regions of light.

1113132.explanation: In the process of respiration, the compound, i.e., glucose reacts with oxygen, which is called oxidation therefore, organic substance gets oxidised.

1113133.explanation: Chailakhyan in 1937 gave the view that flower hormone namely florigen is synthesised in the leaves under favourable photoperiodic conditions. This hormone is transmitted to the growing point where the flowering occurs.

1113134.explanation: Absence of lysosome is responsible for the disorder. Lysosomes are the organelle responsible for digesting waste material, and a misfolding lysosomal protein is the cause of Tay Sachs. Without this protein, gangliosides cannot be digested, and instead build up in cells (especially brain cells) and interfere with development.

1113136.explanation: More energy is produced in aerobic respiration than anaerobic respiration because in anaerobic respiration food is completely oxidised.

1113138.explanation: It was peripheral protein in the stabilising solution whose concentration has been increased. Peripheral proteins are held to the membrane surface primarily through electrostatic or hydrogen bonds. These proteins can be removed easily and cleanly from the surface of membranes by either altering the pH or the media salt concentration. One commonly used method that in fact often defines peripheral proteins employs release with alkaline carbonate.

1113140.explanation: RQ or respiratory quotient is the ratio of the volume of CO2 produced to the volume of O2 used in a unit time. If RQ is 0.6 in a respiratory metabolism, it means that the oxidation of the respiratory substrate consumed more oxygen than the amount of CO2 released.

1113142.explanation: During reduction stage of Calvin cycle, a glucose molecule is formed through a series of reactions. Each molecule of 3PGA is phosphorylated using ATP and 1, 3-bisphosphoglyceric acid is formed. Each molecule of 1, 3-bisphosphoglyceric acid is converted into glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate (G3P) using NADPH.

1113144.explanation: Angiotensin-II is a powerful, vasoconstrictor thus increases glomerular blood pressure and thereby GFR.

1113148.explanation: The amount of the filtrate formed by the kidneys per minute is called glomerular filtration rate (GFR). GFR in a healthy individual is approximately 125 mL / min, i.e., 180 litres per day.

1113150.explanation: Prawn respires with gills (Branchial respiration) and insects respire by tracheae (Tracheal respiration).

1113153.explanation: Persons with blood group A have the A antigen on the surface of their RBCs, and antibodies to antigen B in their plasma.

1113156.explanation: Leucocytes are colourless, nucleated amoeboid cells found in blood which are devoid of haemoglobin and are capable of coming out of blood capillaries through the process of diapedesis.

1113157.explanation: Low temperature required for vernalisation is usually 0 - 5oC. In nature, the plants requiring vernalisation are commonly biennials (e.g., cabbage, sugar beet, carrot), which complete their life cycle in 2 years. They germinate and grow vegetatively in the first year and produce flowers in the second year of growth. These plants fulfill their cold requirement during winters. However, such biennial plants can be made to flower in one growing season by providing low temperature treatment (i.e., 0 - 5oC temperature) to young plants or moistened seeds.

1113160.explanation: Transport of CO2 by blood is much easier than oxygen due to high solubility of 002 - About 7% of CO2 is transported dissolved in plasma, 23% loosely bind with the hemoglobin and forms bicarbonates and about 70% of CO2 reacts with water to form carbonic acid in erythrocytes in the presence of enzyme carbonic anhydrase (fastest enzyme known so far).

1113161.explanation: The given image shows the section of a leaf of C4 plant. In this image, P are the bundle sheath cells rich in RuBisCO and Q are the mesophyll cells rich in PEP carboxylase. Chloroplasts in the mesophyll cells (Q) are granal and in bundle sheath cells (P) are agranal. PEP carboxylase fixes CO2 with PEP in the mesophyll cells (Q) and forms a 4-carbon compound, oxaloacetic acid (OAA). In bundle sheath cells (P), CO2 released from 4 C acid enters the C3 or the Calvin pathway.

1113163.explanation: Micturition is a reflex of avoiding urine. If the urine content of urinary bladder reaches more than 300 mL micturition reflex starts. Neural mechanism of micturition is called micturition reflex.

1113164.explanation: Kinetin, a modified form of adenine, was discovered from autoclaved herring sperm DNA.

1113165.explanation: In infants, defecation is not under voluntary control and it takes place by reflex actions, i.e., process of defecation occurs by the reflex action without the voluntary control of external anal sphincter. Both involuntary and voluntary muscles are directed by brain.

1113166.explanation: T cells or T lymphocyte is a type of lymphocyte (a subtype of white blood cell) that plays a central role in cell-mediated immunity. T cells can be distinguished from other lymphocytes, such as B cells and natural killer cells, by the presence of a T-cell receptor on the cell surface.

1113170.explanation: Fermentation is the incomplete oxidation of glucose under anaerobic conditions by sets of reasons where pyruvic acid is converted to CO2 and ethanol (alcoholic fermentation) or lactic acid (lactic acid fermentation). In fermentation, there is a net gain of only 2 ATP molecules for each molecule of glucose degraded to pyruvic acid.

1113171.explanation: During oxygen transport the oxyhemoglobin at the tissue level liberates oxygen to the cells because in tissue O2 tension is low and CO2 tension is high.

1113173.explanation: Analysis of urine helps in clinical diagnosis of many metabolic disorders as well as malfunctioning of the kidney. For example, presence of glucose (glycosuria) and ketone bodies (ketonuria) in urine are indicative of diabetes mellitus.

1113174.explanation: Milk protein can be digested by pepsin and chymotrypsin.

1113175.explanation: About 90% of the total water is absorbed in the small intestine, while balance 10% is absorbed in the stomach and large intestine. Large intestine also absorbs some minerals, drugs, and products of bacterial digestion like amino acids and vitamin-B complex and vitamin-K. It secretes mucus, which lubricates faeces and facilitate its flow into the rectum, where it is stored temporarily.

1113176.explanation: Leucocyte is a white blood cell (WBC). It is a colourless blood cell of immune system which circulates in the blood and body fluids and is involved in counteracting foreign substances and disease.

1113179.explanation: During reduction stage of Calvin cycle, a glucose molecule is formed through a series of reactions. Each molecule of 3PGA is phosphorylated using ATP and 1, 3-bisphosphoglyceric acid is formed. Each molecule of 1,3-bisphosphoglyceric acid is converted into glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate (G3P) using NADPH. Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate is converted into one molecule of glucose through a series of reactions that are reversal of glycolysis. So, this is also called glycolytic reversal.

1113180.explanation: In the tissues, there is low pO2 high pCO2, high H+ and high temperature. All these conditions are favourable for the dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin.

1113182.explanation: Blood serum does not coagulate because it does not contain any clotting factors. Blood serum is the component that is neither a blood cell nor a clotting factor. It is the blood plasma that includes all proteins not used in blood clotting (coagulation) and all the electrolytes, antibodies, antigens, hormones, and any exogenous substances (e.g., drugs and microorganisms).

1113186.explanation: Gall bladder is a small, pear-shaped organ which is located just posterior to the liver. It is used to store and recycle excess bile (that is not required immediately for digestion) from the small intestine so that it can be reused for the digestion of subsequent meals. Bile is a yellowish-brown fluid produced by the liver and used to break up and digest fatty foods in the small intestine. Gall bladder is a part of the human biliary system, which is involved with the production, storage, and transportation of bile. Bile, produced from liver, is used to break up and digest fatty foods in the small intestine. The most common side effect of the removal of gall bladder is a decrease in bile secretion.

1113187.explanation: Blood platelets occur only in mammals. They are much smaller than RBC. Blood platelets are the source of thromboplastin, necessary for blood clotting.

1113188.explanation: Pyloric sphincter is a sphincter present at the opening from the stomach into the duodenum. It is usually closed, but opens when a peristaltic wave passes over it. It plays an important role in digestion, where it acts as a valve to control the flow of partially digested food from the stomach to the small intestine.

1113191.explanation:
Acetyl CoA (2-carbon compound) combines with oxaloacetate (4-carbon compound) in the presence of condensing enzyme citrate synthase to form a tricarboxylic 6-carbon compound called citric acid, it is the first product of Kreb's cycle. CoA is liberated in the whole reaction.

Acetyl CoA +Oxaloacetic acid +H2O $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Citrate}\;\mathrm{synthase}}$ Citrate + CoA

1113193.explanation: Contraction of gall bladder occurs due to cholecystokinin.

1113194.explanation: Abscisic acid (ABA) is formed from three isoprene subunits and is a key hormone in plant adaptation to environmental stresses. Abscisic acid (ABA) is often referred to as a inhibitory rather than stimulatory hormone. It is involved in the closure of stomata, bud, and seed dormancy and is known to inhibit other hormone actions. It promotes senescence and ageing in other parts of plants.

1113198.explanation: Haemoglobin is a red protein responsible for transporting oxygen in the blood of vertebrates. Its molecule comprises four subunits, each containing an iron atom bound to a haem group.

1113199.explanation: All phototrophic bacteria are capable of performing cyclic photophosphorylation so they have only one photosystem that is, PS I.

1113202.explanation:
Layers between the glomerular and Bowman's capsule through which the filtration takes place are as follows:



 Endothelium of the glomerular blood vessel.
 Basement membrane between the endothelium of glomerular blood vessels and epithelium of the Bowman's capsule.
 Epithelium of the Bowman's capsule.

1113203.explanation: Decapitating a growing plant means removing shoot apex of the plant. Auxin, a growth promoting phytohormone present in apex inhibits the growth of axillary buds so that only the apex continues to grow. When the apex containing auxin is removed or decapitation is done, then axillary buds show their growth, this is because the apical dominance is removed. This practice of removal of apical dominance is applied in tea gardens, hedges, rose gardens etc.

1113205.explanation: The phenomenon of apical dominance can be seen in most of the vaseular plants in which, in the presence of apical bud, growth of lateral buds (fanned just below the apex) is suppressed. At the removal of apical bud, the lateral buds grow vigorously. It is widely used in tea plantation and hedge making.

1113210.explanation: Monocyte is a type of white blood cell (leucocytes) that fights off bacteria, viruses and fungi. Monocytes are the biggest type of white blood cell in the immune system. Originally formed in the bone marrow, they are released into our blood and tissues. When certain germs enter the body, they quickly rush to the site for attack.

1113212.explanation: Oxidative phosphorylation does not release CO2.

1113215.explanation: Succinate dehydrogenase is the only enzyme of Kreb's cycle which is located in inner mitochondrial membrane, in eukaryotes and in cytosol in prokaryotes while all other enzymes of this cycle are located in the mitochondrial matrix.

1113217.explanation: 'Q' is the endodermis, which is the innermost layer of cortex and usually lacks Casparian strips in a dicot stem. 'R' is the sclerenchymatous pericycle that provides mechanical strength. 'S' is xylem which is endarch (centrifugal) with respect to the position of the protoxylem and metaxylem.

1113218.explanation: Thrombokinase hydrolyses prothrombin to thrombin in presence of Ca2+. Thrombin converts soluble fibrinogen to insoluble fibrin.

1113219.explanation: JGA is the special sensitive region formed by cellular modification in the distal convoluted tubule and the afferent arteriole at the location of their contact.

1113221.explanation: The most important function of cytokinins is the promotion of cell division. The varying amounts of cytokinins, along with sufficient auxins is required for the growth of callus in tissue culture experiments. Cytokinins delay the senescence of leaves and other organs by mobilisation of nutrients. It is known as Richmond-Lang effect.

1113222.explanation: Carbamino-hemoglobin is a compound of hemoglobin and carbon dioxide and is one of the forms in which carbon dioxide exists in the blood.

1113223.explanation: Maltose is a disaccharide, which gives two molecules of glucose on hydrolysis. Itis present during the germination of starchy seeds. It is produced commercially from the starch by hydrolysing the enzyme, diastase.

1113224.explanation: Photolysis of water occurs in the oxygen-evolving complex associated with PS II. This protein-bound inorganic complex contains cofactors: four manganese (Mn) ions, calcium ions and chloride ions.

1113226.explanation: Conditional reabsorption of Na+, and water takes place in this DCT (distal convoluted tubule). DCT is also capable reabsorption of Cl- and selective secretion of hydrogen and potassium ions and to maintain the pH and sodium-potassium balance in blood.

1113228.explanation:
HCI does not directly involve in the digestion. It activates pepsinogen and prorennin which is then converted into pepsin and rennin respectively by lowering the pH of the stomach between 1.5 and 2.5. Pepsin functions at acidic medium and breaks up the peptides from the protein and converts it into peptones. Therefore, in the absence of HCI, protein digestion does not take place.

However, before HCI can be secreted and start digesting food, many other things must happen. Peptides, found primarily in protein, stimulate the process that leads to HCI secretion. Peptides cause a chemical called gastrin to be secreted by G-cells. The presence of gastrin then stimulates the release of histamine. Finally, the histamine stimulates the parietal cells to begin secreting HCI.

HCI also protects the body from illness by killing pathogens commonly found on foods.

1113229.explanation: During glycolysis glucose is converted into pyruvic acid. In this case O2 is not utilised.

1113230.explanation: Auxin helps to initiate root production in stem cuttings. This property of auxin is widely used in the propagation of plants through stem cuttings.

1113234.explanation: Since the given plant is a succulent, CAM will be followed as a pathway for biosynthetic phase of photosynthesis. In this pathway, PEP is the primary CO2 acceptor. The initial carboxylation occurs during night and final carboxylation occurs during day.

1113241.explanation: Succus entericus or intestinal juices are the secretion of intestinal glands. Brunner's glands in the intestine opens into crypts of Lieberkuhn, which secretes enzymes and mucus. Basically, succus entericus is considered as the secretion of crypt of Lieberkuhn.

1113242.explanation: In C4 cycle, PEP carboxylase fixes CO2 with PEP in the mesophyll cells and forms a 4-carbon compound, oxaloacetic acid (OAA). Then, another 4-carbon compound, malic acid or aspartic acid, is formed from OAA. These compounds are transported to the bundle sheath cells where, C4 acid is broken down to form C3 acid and CO2. The bundle sheath cells are rich in RuBisCObut lack PEPcase. So, CO2 released in the bundle sheath cells enters the C3 or the Calvin pathway, a pathway common to all plants. C3 acid, so formed, is again transported to the mesophyll cells and regenerated back into PEP.

Physiological value of carbohydrates is 4.0 kcal/g, proteins 4.0 kcal/g and of fats is 9.0 kcal/g.

1113252.explanation: Auxin is a growth promoting phytohormone. It moves mainly from the apical to the basal end (basipetally). This type of unidirectional transport is termed polar transport. Auxin is the only plant growth hormone known to be transported polarly. Recently it has been recognised that a significant amount of auxin transport also occurs acropetally (from basal end to the apical end) in the root.

1113254.explanation: Growth hormones or phytohormones are defined as organic substances which are synthesised in minute quantities in one part of the plant body and transported to another part where they influence specific physiological processes. Phytohormones are chemical substances which are synthesised by plants and are naturally occurring.

1113255.explanation: Osmoreceptors are sensory receptors that detect changes in osmotic pressure and contribute to maintaining fluid balance in the body. They are primarily found in the hypothalamus and kidneys. Osmoreceptors in the body are activated by changes in the blood volume, body fluid volume and ionic concentration. When the osmotic pressure of the blood rises, water moves down the osmotic gradient into the cell, causing the cell to swell. An excessive loss of fluid from the body can activate these receptors, which stimulate the hypothalamus to release ADH (antidiuretic hormone) or vasopressin from neurohypophysis (posterior lobe of pituitary).

1113257.explanation:
The wall of the alimentary canal is composed of four layers of tissues. These layers (from the innermost layer to outward) are mucosa, submucosa, muscularis, and serosa. Each layer has different tissues and functions.

Layers A, B, C, and D are respectively mucosa, submucosa, serosa, and muscularis.

Mucosa layer protects against bacterial invasion. The lamina propria of the mucosa contains lymphoid tissue that makes up the mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) and responds to pathogens encountered in the alimentary canal. Other function of mucosal layer is secretion of enzymes, mucus, hormones etc. and absorption of digested food.

Submucosa contains blood vessels and carries nutrients to away during absorption. Its major function is protection. Serosa is the outermost layer and secretes serous fluid. Muscularis regulates motility of gastrointestinal tract.

1113258.explanation: The enzyme RuBisCO is a key enzyme in photosynthesis. It can use either CO2 or O2 as a substrate. RuBisCO combines ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP) with CO2 in the first step of the Calvin cycle and leads to the production of sugar. The reaction that uses O2 is the first step of the photorespiration pathway, which wastes energy. Two key factors are the relative concentrations of CO2 and O2 and the temperature. Under high temperature and higher ratio of O2 to CO2, RuBisCO carries out the reaction that uses O2.

1113259.explanation: When food in the form of bolus reaches into the stomach by involuntary movement of muscular coat of oesophagus, it mixes thoroughly with the gastric juices present in the stomach. This thoroughly mixed food is called chyme.

1113260.explanation: Auxin helps to prevent fruits and leaf drop at early stages but promote the abscission of older mature leaves and fruits.

1113263.explanation: The partial pressure of O2 in expired air is 116 mm Hg. In alveolar air it is 104 mm Hg, in arterial blood it is 95 mm Hg and in venous blood it is 40 mm Hg.

1113264.explanation: Artificial application of auxins like IAA, IBA, and NAA to unpollinated pistils can form seedless fruits. NAA and 2, 4 - D are often employed for inducing flowering in litchi and pineapple. Application of auxins (e.g., IAA, IBA) and conjugate auxins (e.g., IBA - alanine) to unpollinated pistils make them develop into seedless fruits (or parthenocarps).

1113282.explanation: In a cellular respiration, energy stored in a glucose molecule, which enters into cytoplasm is called glycolysis then enters into Kreb's cycle, which is also called tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA cycle) and finally in electron transport chain or system. Therefore, the correct sequence is Glycolysis Kreb's cycle - electron transport chain.

1113284.explanation: In small intestine the food meets two juices: pancreatic and intestinal juice. Pancreatic juice contains a carbohydrase. named pancreatic a-amylase. This enzyme hydrolyses more starch and glycogen to dextrin and the latter to double sugar, maltose and isomaltose and 'limit' dextrins. Starch and glycogen Pancreatic $\alpha$ -amylase isomaltose + Limit dextrins.

1113290.explanation: Ethylene production by plants is autocatalytic, i.e., a small amount of ethylene will stimulate production of its larger amounts. Thus, a few ripe fruits will initiate ripening of nearby fruits. It is therefore, a common practice to keep few ripe bananas with unripe bananas to hasten ripening.

1113293.explanation: O2 and CO2 are exchanged in the alveoli by simple diffusion. The factors that affect the diffusion are pressure gradient of the gases, solubility of the gases and the thickness of the membranes involved in diffusion.

1113295.explanation:
Auxins are plant hormones that play a crucial role in root development and growth. They promote:



 Primary root elongation
 Lateral root formation
 Adventitious root development, especially in cuttings

1113298.explanation: Henle's Loop Reabsorption in this segment is minimum. However, this region plays a significant role in the maintenance of high osmolarity of medullary interstitial fluid. The descending limb of Henle is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes. This concentrates the filtrate as it moves down. The ascending limb is impermeable to water but allows transport of electrolytes actively or passively.

1113301.explanation: ABO blood grouping is based on the presence or absence of the surface antigens-A and B on RBCs.

1113304.explanation: The tubular epithelial cells in different segments of the nephrons perform reabsorption either by active or passive mechanisms.

1113306.explanation: The products of light reaction (ATP and NADPH molecules) are used during reduction and regeneration stages of C3 cycle.

1113308.explanation: In C4 plants, PEP carboxylase fixes CO2 with PEP in the mesophyll cells and forms a 4-carbon compound, oxaloacetic acid (OAA). Proton gradient established during electron transport of light reaction is broken down to produce ATP synthesis.

1113311.explanation: Water is one of the reactants in the light reaction but its availability affects the plant, rather than directly affecting the photosynthesis. Water stress causes the stomata to close hence, reducing the CO2 availability. Also, it makes the leaves to wilt which reduces the surface area of the leaves available for photosynthesis.

1113312.explanation: Lymphocytes are the smallest (6-10 nm) and the most common (20-25% of total leucocytes) leucocytes after neutrophils (60-65% of total leucocytes).

1113313.explanation: Apical dominance is the phenomenon by which presence of apical bud does not allow the nearby lateral buds to grow by releasing auxins. When the apical bud is removed, the lateral buds sprout. When a plant is decapitated, i.e., its apical bud is removed then the lateral buds sprout, resulting in dense bushy growth. This phenomenon is widely used in the tea plucking and hedge making.

1113314.explanation:
